content.text: # Epic: Pre-surfacing reviewer-findings verifier agent (F4 + F5 bundle)
## Context

DSO maintainers and autonomous-resolution sub-agents currently consume reviewer findings — including invalid ones — without any pre-surfacing verification step. PR-80 saw 8 of 11 round-2 findings invalid; PR #102 had 3 verified hallucinations claiming "undefined function" on functions defined at lines 94/108 of the same file; PR #103 cycled 19→33→17 findings with ~0% line-overlap. Invalid findings consume autonomous-resolution attempts (CLAUDE.md rule 11; default 5 attempts each), introduce unnecessary complexity into the codebase when acted upon, and erode trust in the review pipeline. The existing `code-reviewer-arbiter` is a post-defense dispute adjudicator invoked only on `ESCALATE_REVIEW` or `oscillation_no_arbiter_engagement` — it cannot catch these failure modes because invalid findings reach the PR untouched and burn resolution attempts before any defense escalates.
## Approach

This epic bundles two related fixes from the post-PR-#103 calibration analysis: F4 (structured `verification_evidence` schema field) and F5 (verifier sub-agent that consumes it). F5 needs F4 to function on absence claims, so they ship together.

**F4 — Schema extension and reviewer-prompt updates.** Extend the existing reviewer-findings schema (which already carries `cited_excerpt`, shipped at commit 729d2c2075) with a sibling field `verification_evidence: {command, output}`. When a reviewer finding makes an absence claim, the reviewer captures the grep/stat/path-resolve command plus its output as proof. Update all 10 existing `code-reviewer-*` agent files (light, standard, performance, deep-arch, deep-correctness, deep-hygiene, deep-verification, security-red-team, security-blue-team, test-quality) to emit this field. Absence-language detection uses an expanded synonym anchor list at the schema-validation boundary: canonical triggers (undefined / missing / does not exist / not defined / not found) plus reviewer-rephrasing variants (unable to locate / appears to be absent / no implementation / no definition visible / cannot find / cannot be found / has no corresponding / has no definition / no [X] visible / is called but [no/has no]). Empirical probe (this brainstorm session) showed reviewer LLMs gravitate to canonical triggers in practice, so the anchor list catches the realistic failure mode without a semantic-classifier fallback.

**F5 — Verifier sub-agent.** Build a new `code-reviewer-verifier` sub-agent dispatched between every reviewer and `record-review.sh` in both the CI llm-review path (`plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/runner.py`) and the local `/dso:review` path (REVIEW-WORKFLOW reviewer dispatch). The verifier runs against critical/important/fragile findings only (minor findings pass through unverified). For each in-scope finding, the verifier inspects the cited file (read at the snapshot SHA, not live filesystem) and the F4 `verification_evidence` payload, then emits one of three rulings:
- `confirm` — claim is verifiably true; finding enters the autonomous-resolution loop unchanged.
- `downgrade-to-minor` — claim is true but reachability, scope, or severity is wrong; finding becomes a normal minor PR comment (no resolution attempt).
- `drop` — claim is verifiably false; finding is removed before reaching the PR or resolution loop.

Rubric: defer to the original reviewer on uncertainty (the verifier never drops a finding on insufficient evidence — it confirms and lets the existing autonomous-resolution loop handle it). Empirical probe (this brainstorm session) confirmed sonnet does NOT systematically over-confirm under this rubric on clear contradictions — drop rate was 3/3 on the PR-#102 hallucination class (Test 1) and 3/3 on an authoritatively-toned variant (Test 2). The rubric correctly defers (1 confirm, 2 downgrade, 0 drop) on a genuinely-ambiguous case (Test 3 — definition exists in a sibling file).

**Snapshot SHA anchor.** The reviewer's dispatch wrapper captures `<reviewed_sha>` at reviewer-dispatch time. Both reviewer and verifier operate against this SHA. The local verifier reads files via `git show <reviewed_sha>:<path>`; the CI verifier's pre-packaged file contents are extracted from `<reviewed_sha>` (not the working tree, not the verifier-dispatch-time SHA). Mid-review commits cannot shift the verifier's view.

**Independent verification_evidence re-execution (CI).** The CI dispatch wrapper re-executes the reviewer's stated `verification_evidence.command` against `<reviewed_sha>` (sandboxed: read-only allowlist, no network). The captured output is compared against `verification_evidence.output`. On mismatch, the verifier receives an `evidence_invalidated: true` flag in its prompt; the verifier treats invalidated evidence as positive contradiction, favoring `drop` when the original claim depended on it. This closes the "hallucinated grep output" loophole — a fabricated reviewer evidence command produces no matching output and flips the verifier's input.

**Asymmetric tool access.** The CI verifier is an LLM API call with file contents and re-executed evidence pre-packaged into the prompt by the dispatch wrapper (no Bash, no Read at runtime). The local verifier is a Claude Code sub-agent with `Read`, `Glob`, and a bounded `Bash` allowlist (`grep`, `stat`, `ls`, `file` — no writes, no network). Both paths use the sonnet tier and a path-aware prompt template that explicitly distinguishes "context is complete" (CI: pre-packaged) from "context is live-readable" (local).

Each ruling carries a `file:line-region` fingerprint. Schema enforces `<path>:<line-start>-<line-end>` with `line-start == line-end` for single-line findings (no `path:120` shorthand). This shape is the stable matching surface for a future cross-cycle convergence matcher (F7b).

**Feature flag.** Config key `review.verifier_enabled` (default `false`). Verifier dispatch is wrapped in a flag check at both CI and local entry points. When disabled, the pipeline behaves identically to the pre-epic state. Per-project opt-in after fixture validation. The dispatch wrapper itself catches all exceptions and treats wrapper-side crashes as `verifier_status: failed` — never blocks `record-review.sh`.

**Coordinated rollout.** Schema validation of `verification_evidence` operates in two phases. (1) Soft-deprecation window: missing field on absence-tagged findings logs a warning to review output but does not reject. (2) Hard enforcement: activates only when the consuming project's plugin cache has BOTH the F4 schema and the 10 updated reviewer agents present (detected by version-marker file shipped by the plugin). Window length: configurable via `review.verifier_strict_after` (default: 2 minor plugin releases after F4 ships).

**Failure handling.** Any verifier failure (timeout, malformed output, MAX_AGENTS=0, sub-agent unavailable, API error, dispatch wrapper crash) annotates the finding with `verifier_status: failed` and passes it through unchanged (fail-open). Per-review failure-rate threshold (`review.verifier_failure_threshold`, default 0.30) escalates the entire review to user attention. Threshold range bounds: validation rejects values outside `(0.0, 1.0]`. **Cascading-failure brake**: when failure rate exceeds the threshold AND in-scope-finding count ≥ 5, the autonomous-resolution loop is also paused for the failing findings (CLAUDE.md rule 11 attempt counter held), preventing pre-epic invalid-finding pipeline restoration under sustained CI degradation.

**Telemetry.** Per-review confirm/downgrade-to-minor/drop counts, verifier-failure rate, fingerprint emissions, and minor-finding rate (canary for severity-undergrading regression) surface in (a) per-review output (PR comment in CI, terminal output locally) and (b) `review-stats` aggregations alongside existing reviewer-tier and resolution-rate metrics.

**Regression fixture corpus** (verifier-specific; distinct from the general reviewer rubric corpus owned by epic a72d-df57) built from open bug tickets `ee3a-43fc-652b-49ff` (PR #102 hallucinated "undefined function"), `b2ef-cd72-76b1-4f01` (PR #100 invalid critical findings + severity-inflated important), `9e84-2b78-c2ce-426b` (PR-#102 false-positive trust-boundary on .coderabbit.yaml). Corpus replayed at sprint close in **both** CI and local paths to verify ruling behavior AND cross-path equivalence (≥95% identical rulings required). Includes: a known-ambiguous case (asserts the defer-rubric ruling), a known-fabricated-evidence case (asserts CI re-execution flips to `drop`), and a known-rephrased absence claim using non-canonical wording (asserts F4 expanded-synonym anchor catches it).

**Governance — rule 11 exception.** ADR `docs/adr/0013-verifier-severity-authority.md` (drafted during this brainstorm) documents that the `code-reviewer-verifier` sub-agent's `downgrade-to-minor` and `drop` rulings are an explicit, narrowly-scoped exception to CLAUDE.md rule 11 (no severity overrides in `runner.py`). The exception is gated on (1) sub-agent identity, (2) ruling enum, (3) documented dispatch surface, and (4) `review.verifier_enabled=true`. The implementation work for this epic is limited to updating CLAUDE.md rule 11 to add the one-sentence cross-reference pointing to the ADR — the ADR text itself is already in the repo.
## Success Criteria

1. Reviewer-findings schema extends `cited_excerpt` with a sibling `verification_evidence: {command: string, output: string}` field. Schema validation requires `verification_evidence` on every finding whose claim text matches the absence-language pattern set (canonical + expanded reviewer-rephrasing variants per Approach). Enforcement applies in both CI llm-review and local `/dso:review` paths. Validation runs in soft-deprecation mode initially per `review.verifier_strict_after`; hard rejection requires both F4 schema and the 10 updated reviewer agents present in the plugin cache (version-marker check).

2. All 10 existing `code-reviewer-*` agent files updated to emit `verification_evidence` when their finding cites absence-language; each agent has a behavioral fixture asserting it emits the field on a known absence-claim diff. The 10 agents are updated in a single plugin-cache version bump alongside the schema validator.

3. `code-reviewer-verifier` sub-agent file exists at `plugins/dso/agents/code-reviewer-verifier.md`. Ruling shape: `{finding_id, ruling: confirm|downgrade-to-minor|drop, fingerprint: "<path>:<line-start>-<line-end>" (line-start == line-end on single-line findings), verifier_status: ok|failed, evidence_invalidated: bool, rationale}`. Schema validated at the verifier output boundary.

4. CI dispatch wrapper in `plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/runner.py` calls the verifier between reviewer dispatch and `plugins/dso/hooks/record-review.sh` for each critical/important/fragile finding. Wrapper pre-packages the cited file contents (extracted from `<reviewed_sha>`, not live filesystem), the `verification_evidence` payload, and a re-executed-evidence comparison result. Minor findings bypass the verifier.

5. Local `/dso:review` reviewer pipeline dispatches the verifier as a Claude Code sub-agent with `Read`, `Glob`, and bounded `Bash` allowlist (`grep`, `stat`, `ls`, `file`). The verifier reads files via `git show <reviewed_sha>:<path>` (not the live working tree). Minor findings bypass the verifier.

6. Verifier rulings have explicit semantics in the autonomous-resolution loop: `confirm` enters the loop unchanged; `downgrade-to-minor` becomes a normal minor PR comment with no resolution attempt; `drop` removes the finding before any PR-surface or resolution-loop processing.

7. CI dispatch wrapper independently re-executes the reviewer's `verification_evidence.command` against `<reviewed_sha>` (sandboxed: read-only allowlist, no network) and compares output against `verification_evidence.output`. On mismatch, the verifier prompt receives `evidence_invalidated: true`; verifier rules `drop` when the original claim depended on the invalidated evidence. Behavioral fixture: a reviewer-emitted command whose output is fabricated triggers `drop`.

8. Snapshot SHA invariant: `<reviewed_sha>` is captured at reviewer-dispatch time and propagates through reviewer, verifier, record-review.sh, and PR-comment surface. Test asserts that a mid-review commit (push between reviewer and verifier dispatch) does not change the SHA the verifier evaluates against.

9. Verifier failure handling: any failure annotates the finding with `verifier_status: failed` and passes it through unchanged (fail-open). `review.verifier_failure_threshold` (default 0.30, range `(0.0, 1.0]`) — failures above threshold escalate the review to user attention via a distinguishable PR comment label. **Cascading-failure brake**: when threshold exceeded AND in-scope-finding count ≥ 5, autonomous-resolution loop pauses for the failing findings (rule 11 attempt counter held).

10. Per-ruling `file:line-region` fingerprint emitted for every verified finding (confirm or downgrade); shape `<path>:<line-start>-<line-end>` with `line-start == line-end` on single-line findings; validated by schema. Surfaces as a stable matching surface for future F7b convergence work.

11. Telemetry: confirm/downgrade/drop counts, verifier-failure rate, per-finding fingerprints, AND review-level minor-finding rate (severity-undergrading canary) visible in (a) per-review output (PR comment for CI, terminal output for local) and (b) `review-stats` aggregations. The new fields (`verifier_confirm_count`, `verifier_downgrade_count`, `verifier_drop_count`, `verifier_failure_rate`, `verifier_minor_finding_rate`, `verifier_fingerprints[]`) are added to the review-stats schema definition that epic 5df7-63ac (integrated observability) will consume — schema additions are co-coordinated with that epic.

12. Regression fixture corpus (verifier-specific; distinct from a72d-df57's general reviewer rubric corpus) replayed at sprint close in **both** CI and local paths. Required ruling behavior: `drop` on PR-#102 hallucinated "undefined function" (ee3a-43fc); `downgrade-to-minor` on PR-#100 severity-inflated important (b2ef-cd72); `drop` on .coderabbit.yaml false-positive trust-boundary (9e84-2b78); the defer-rubric ruling on the known-ambiguous case; `drop` on the known-fabricated-evidence case (re-execution flips it); `verification_evidence`-required on the known-rephrased absence claim. Cross-path ruling equivalence: ≥95% identical rulings between CI and local paths across the corpus.

13. Feature flag `review.verifier_enabled` (default `false`) gates verifier dispatch at both CI and local entry points. When disabled, pipeline behaves identically to pre-epic state (verified by replaying the corpus with flag off and confirming pre-epic ruling distribution). The dispatch wrapper catches all exceptions and treats wrapper-side crashes as `verifier_status: failed` — never blocks `record-review.sh`.

14. CLAUDE.md rule 11 is updated to add a single sentence at the end of its existing text pointing to `docs/adr/0013-verifier-severity-authority.md` and naming the four-prong exception scope (sub-agent identity, ruling enum, dispatch surface, feature-flag gating). The ADR text itself is already in the repo (drafted during the brainstorm session for this epic).
## Probe Findings (resolved during brainstorm)
Two pre-implementation probes were run during brainstorm to de-risk the rubric and pattern-set design:
**F1 Sycophancy Probe** — 3 test cases × 3 sonnet runs each measuring confirm-bias on clear contradictions under the defer-on-uncertainty rubric.
- Test 1 (clear contradiction, PR-#102 hallucination class): **drop 3/3** — sonnet correctly drops on direct evidence contradiction.
- Test 2 (same contradiction, authoritative reviewer tone): **drop 3/3** — authoritative tone does not bias the verifier toward confirm.
- Test 3 (genuine ambiguity, definition exists in sibling file): **0 drop / 1 confirm / 2 downgrade-to-minor** — verifier handles ambiguity thoughtfully without blanket-deferring.

- **Conclusion**: defer-on-uncertainty rubric is empirically sound under sonnet. The 3-way rubric (`confirm` / `downgrade-to-minor` / `drop`) is retained without need for an explicit `uncertain` ruling.
**F3 Absence-Language Variant Probe** — 8 rephrased absence claims through schema-validator pattern sets + 3 sonnet reviewer outputs on a real missing-function diff.
- Static pattern (canonical triggers only): **6 of 8 variants bypassed** — 75% bypass rate on intentionally-rephrased absence claims.
- Static pattern (expanded triggers — canonical + 13 reviewer-rephrasing variants): **0 of 8 bypassed** — full coverage.
- Reviewer-output collection (3 emissions on a real bug): **3/3 used canonical triggers** ("not defined", "undefined", "missing"). Reviewer LLMs gravitate to canonical phrasing in practice.
- **Conclusion**: expanded synonym anchor is sufficient for the realistic failure mode; haiku-tier semantic-classifier fallback is unnecessary and removed from the spec.
## Scenario Analysis (surviving)
- **Verifier dispatch doubles review latency under load** (`high`, `runtime`) — addressed by feature-flag default-off (SC13) + per-finding parallelization opportunity in dispatch wrapper.
- **Race between verifier file Read and concurrent worktree edits** (`high`, `runtime`) — addressed by snapshot SHA anchor (SC8).
- **CI pre-packaged file contents stale relative to reviewer snapshot** (`high`, `runtime`) — addressed by snapshot SHA anchor (SC8).
- **Absence-language regex false negatives bypass verification_evidence requirement** (`high`, `runtime`) — addressed by expanded synonym anchor (SC1) + Probe Findings F3 (validated empirically).
- **Fail-open on verifier failure restores the pre-epic invalid-finding pipeline** (`high`, `runtime`) — addressed by cascading-failure brake (SC9).
- **Schema validation rejects in-flight reviewer outputs from older agent versions** (`critical`, `deployment`) — addressed by coordinated rollout / version-marker gating (SC1).
- **Verifier agent file missing in plugin cache after partial sync** (`high`, `deployment`) — addressed by feature flag default-off (SC13) + dispatch-wrapper exception catch (SC13).
- **agent-routing.conf collision with concurrent dso-8l5h extraction epic** (`high`, `deployment`) — surfaced as Cross-Epic Interaction (dso-8l5h); deployment-time check in implementation plan.
- **CI llm-review job lacks rollback path when verifier hard-fails** (`critical`, `deployment`) — addressed by feature flag (SC13) + wrapper exception catch (SC13).

- **Bounded Bash allowlist blocks legitimate verification on grep-incompatible filesystems** (`medium`, `configuration`) — accepted; `git show <SHA>:<path>` reads do not require the allowlist on those platforms.
- **Fingerprint shape ambiguous for single-line findings** (`medium`, `configuration`) — addressed by schema constraint `line-start == line-end` (SC3, SC10).
- **Minor findings bypass verifier — severity-undergrading attack** (`medium`, `configuration`) — addressed by minor-finding-rate canary in telemetry (SC11).
- **Hallucinated `verification_evidence`** (`critical`, `assumption`) — addressed by independent CI re-execution + `evidence_invalidated` flag (SC7).

- **Defer-to-reviewer-on-uncertainty inverts cost model** (`high`, `assumption`) — **REJECTED by Probe F1** — empirically the rubric works correctly; sonnet does not over-confirm on clear contradictions.
- **Critical/important/fragile classification reliability** (`high`, `assumption`) — partially addressed by minor-finding-rate canary (SC11); residual risk accepted.
- **CI verifier and local verifier produce equivalent rulings** (`high`, `assumption`) — addressed by cross-path ruling equivalence SC (SC12).
- **Rule 11 governance handwave** (`medium`, `assumption`) — addressed by ADR + rule 11 update (SC14).
## Prompt Alignment Findings (resolved)
- **Matched signal**: agent definitions (new `code-reviewer-verifier` agent + 10 updated `code-reviewer-*` agents).

- **Bot-psych F1 — Over-confirm sycophancy**: Probe F1 ran during brainstorm — hypothesis NOT confirmed. Sonnet correctly drops on clear contradictions (3/3 in two test cases). Defer-on-uncertainty rubric retained.
- **Bot-psych F2 — CI vs. local prompt-template divergence**: addressed by path-aware prompt template (Approach) + cross-path ruling-equivalence fixture (SC12).

- **Bot-psych F3 — Absence-language pattern evasion**: Probe F3 ran during brainstorm — partially confirmed (75% bypass on rephrased variants for canonical pattern; 0% bypass for expanded pattern; reviewer LLMs use canonical in practice). Expanded synonym anchor adopted (SC1); semantic-classifier fallback rejected as unnecessary.
- **Bot-psych F4 — Failure-threshold volume-sensitivity**: addressed by cascading-failure brake (SC9) — threshold drives an actionable consequence (resolution-loop pause), not just a label.
## Dependencies
- `cited_excerpt` schema field is shipped (commit 729d2c2075). F4 extension is in scope of this epic, not a prerequisite.
- ample-seize-siege (677d-a6a0-0c2e-4b9e) — closed.
- No other blocking dependencies.
## Cross-Epic Interactions
- Resource: ticket schema (resolution enum + reviewer-findings)
Overlapping epic: 1de7-50d4 — Resolution and reporter enum
Constraint: verifier ruling shape coexists with new resolution enum; document integration order.
- Resource: ticket-system schema for external distribution
Overlapping epic: 371f-cfc3 — Package DSO ticket system for external distribution
Constraint: forward-declare verifier schema additions in distributed schema; reserve schema-version migration strategy.
- Resource: review-stats aggregations and telemetry schema
Overlapping epic: 5df7-63ac — Add integrated observability
Constraint: define verifier telemetry fields in unified telemetry schema before emission.
- Resource: REVIEW-WORKFLOW orchestration / per-worktree review dispatch
Overlapping epic: 70f6-05f1 — Scale worktree isolation to parallel review with Clash conflict prevention
Constraint: ensure verifier dispatch is replicated per-worktree and remains sandwiched between reviewer and record-review.sh.
- Resource: closure-checks schema and end-state intent flow
Overlapping epic: a03c-d55e — Closure Checks schema migration
Constraint: verifier ruling output compatible with closure-checks schema modifications.
- Resource: test_artifact manifest field (fingerprint linkage)
Overlapping epic: 94ed-f55c — Plan-time intent allocation
Constraint: coordinate fingerprint format (file:line-region) with test_artifact.path schema for cross-consumer lookups.
- Resource: reviewer prompt rubric / replay corpus
Overlapping epic: a72d-df57 — Reviewer rubric replay corpus

Constraint: this epic's regression fixture corpus (SC12) is verifier-specific (3 named bug fixtures + 3 synthesized cases for ruling/evidence/rephrasing); it is NOT the general reviewer rubric replay corpus owned by a72d-df57. Sprint ordering preference: this epic ships before a72d-df57 builds its general corpus, so the corpus targets the v2 schema.
- Resource: code review pipeline dispatch infrastructure
Overlapping epic: cbea-3722 — Integrate ACCESSIBILITY_REVIEWER agent
Constraint: define dispatch ordering between verifier and accessibility reviewer; ensure findings schemas are compatible for unified post-processing.
- Resource: dso-config.conf config key namespace
Overlapping epic: dso-0wi2 — Project level config flags
Constraint: use `review.verifier_*` prefix (`review.verifier_enabled`, `review.verifier_failure_threshold`, `review.verifier_strict_after`).
- Resource: plugins/dso/agents/ directory + review dispatch infrastructure + agent-routing.conf
Overlapping epic: dso-8l5h — Extract review and evaluation sub-agents

Constraint: align verifier agent file naming with dso-8l5h extraction pattern; coordinate agent-routing.conf registration; deployment-time check in implementation plan asserts verifier registration succeeded.
- Resource: review overlay agent dispatch framework
Overlapping epic: dso-q0lo — Prevent the explosion of documentation created by LLMs (code-reviewer-doc overlay)
Constraint: clarify overlay agent ordering; ensure classifier output schema supports both overlay dispatch signals.
- Resource: code review finding volume / quality signals in review-stats
Overlapping epic: e22e-b7a2 — Implementation reliability
Constraint: track verifier drop/downgrade actions separately in review-stats so improvements and verifier filtering do not conflate.
- Resource: reviewer-findings + severity classification semantics (umbrella calibration epic)
Overlapping epic: e7f3-2b45 (grainy-speck-ball) — Code review calibration umbrella
Constraint: this epic is one of four calibration fixes (F4+F5 here, F6 shipped PR #106, F7b separate epic TBD).
- Resource: plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/runner.py
Overlapping epic: f9f8-a15c — Add Gemini provider to CI LLM review provider abstraction
Constraint: position verifier dispatch after provider selection but before record-review.sh call.
- Resource: review-findings schema + resolution-loop entry mechanics
Overlapping epic: jira-dig-1673 — Reviewer override discipline
Constraint: verifier `drop` ruling prevents findings from reaching override-discipline gate entirely; clarify whether `downgrade-to-minor` findings can still trigger override-discipline.
## Follow-on (separate ticket, filed in Phase 3)
- New P1 epic: Approach 4 minor-finding ticket gate + re-routing `downgrade-to-minor` rulings through it. Blocked by this epic.

content.text: ## Context

The calibration program lacks an empirical Tier-3 catch-power signal. Tests pass deterministic Tier-1/Tier-2 checks (assertion shape, intent articulation, manifest-claim breadth and header-source from 7f42) while sometimes failing to catch behavior-changing mutations on the code they claim to verify. Without mutation testing, the project has no empirical ground truth for "does this test catch a real regression?" — only structural proxies. The DSO maintainer, sprint orchestrators, and code-reviewer-test-quality have no visibility into per-PR kill-rate trends; the project cannot tell whether changes to test-writing prompts (d566, 69e8 graduations) are actually improving test catch-power.

This epic delivers per-PR mutation testing for the DSO plugin's first-class stacks (Python, Ruby, JS/TS, Flask, Go), runs in parallel with llm-review as a non-blocking CI job, ships calibration-first with a count-floor surfacing a maintainer-review story ticket, and after thresholds are committed enters enforcement mode where threshold breach auto-creates a bug ticket. Bash is out of scope due to the absence of mature mutation tooling in the bash ecosystem.
## Success Criteria

SC1: plugins/dso/docs/contracts/mutation-testing-findings.md published. Per-stack-result schema: {stack, mutation_tool, tool_version, total_mutants, mutants_generated (distinct field — zero indicates PR touched only non-mutable code), killed_mutants, surviving_mutants: [{file, line, operator, expected, actual}], kill_rate, runtime_seconds, runtime_exceeded (bool), exit_status}. Aggregate-result schema: {pr_number, schema_version=1, calibration_mode_active, per_stack_results: [...], aggregate_kill_rate}. Tooling MUST preserve unknown fields in passthrough for forward-compatibility.

SC2 (Phase 1 — Python pilot): plugins/dso/workflows/mutation-testing.yml shipped as plugin template. Triggered on pull_request (synchronize, opened). Concurrency group keyed to PR ref so new commits cancel in-flight runs. PR-label `skip-mutation-testing` opts a PR out entirely (cost-control escape hatch). When PR's mutable-stack file count exceeds `mutation.max_files_per_run` (default 100), workflow auto-skips with annotation suggesting label use or PR split. Python matrix job installs mutmut pinned to `mutation.python.tool_version` from dso-config.conf; on install failure, tries `mutation.python.fallback_versions` in order; final failure emits `TOOL_INSTALL_FAILED` annotation distinguishing tool-yank from mutation-failure. Runs mutmut incremental mode against diffed Python files. Writes findings JSON per SC1. Uploads as workflow artifact. Aggregate job upserts PR comment with marker `MUTATION_TESTING_FINDINGS_<pr-number>` (distinct from llm-review's marker — no race possible), writes GHA workflow summary, falls back to GHA-summary-only when comment-write is unavailable (fork PRs). Operates in calibration mode (no enforcement, no auto-bug-creation).

SC3 (Phase 2 — polyglot expansion): Ruby (mutant), JS/TS (Stryker `--incremental`), Go (go-gremlins) added as parallel matrix jobs alongside Python. Flask covered by Python. Each per-stack job installs its tool pinned to `mutation.<stack>.tool_version` with `mutation.<stack>.fallback_versions` chain. Per-stack runtime cap via `mutation.<stack>.timeout_seconds` (defaults: Stryker 600, mutmut 900, mutant 1200, gremlins 900). On timeout, partial-result emitted with `runtime_exceeded=true`. fail-fast: false across matrix entries. When ALL stacks return `runtime_exceeded=true`, PR comment surfaces prominent `ALL_STACKS_TIMEOUT` warning, no bug ticket created (even in threshold mode), `aggregate_kill_rate=null`. Aggregate job merges all stack findings into a single PR comment.

SC4 (Phase 3 — calibration auto-surfacing): CI workflow tracks accumulated telemetry. Floor: ≥20 PRs telemetry AND ≥4 weeks elapsed since first telemetry run AND no existing `mutation-calibration-review` tagged story ticket — all three conditions required. Workflow auto-creates story ticket titled "Review mutation testing telemetry and set per-stack thresholds". Body opens with: "Your observed kill rate is X%. What threshold fits your project's risk tolerance?" (number not headlined). Reference points table with p25 / median / p75 rows and a second column "Approximate alert frequency" showing what share of PRs would fire a threshold alert at that rate. Self-reflection prompt: "Does your calibration window include PRs that modified test files? If most PRs in the window were non-test, this kill rate may underestimate steady-state." Stable tag `mutation-calibration-review` prevents duplicate creation. Workflow emits config-consistency warning annotation when `mutation.threshold.<stack>.min_kill_rate` is set but `mutation.calibration.completed=false` (or vice versa).

SC5 (Phase 4 — threshold-mode enforcement): Workflow reads `mutation.calibration.completed` from dso-config.conf. When true AND per-stack `mutants_generated > 0`: per-stack kill rate compared against `mutation.threshold.<stack>.min_kill_rate`. On breach, bug ticket auto-created via `.claude/scripts/dso ticket create bug` pushing to the tickets orphan branch using the same CI auth pattern as the existing Jira bridge / outbound checkpoint. Retry-with-backoff (3 attempts); on final failure writes `TICKET_CREATE_FAILED` artifact to the workflow run plus a workflow-level annotation. Bug ticket includes a 4-field structured blurb (max 60 words total):
- CONTEXT — link to behavioral-testing-standard.md Tier-3 rationale and 411b epic for background

Content-hash deduplication tag `mutation-breach-<sha>` where sha is hash(stack, source_file, mutant_locations) — scoped per-stack-per-source-file, NOT per-PR-diff. Recurring root-causes dedup correctly across PRs; structurally-similar diffs in different files don't collide.

SC6 (Phase 5 — onboarding integration): The consolidated `/dso:onboarding` (delivered by dependency 136b-6758) gains a mutation-testing phase. LEADS WITH TRADEOFFS before per-stack questioning: estimated CI time cost, false-positive context, and one sentence on what the maintainer is asked to do when bugs fire. Detects in-scope stacks via manifest files (Python: pyproject.toml or setup.py; Ruby: Gemfile; JS/TS: package.json; Go: go.mod). Single-stack auto-default: detected single in-scope stack auto-enables with a one-line notice "Mutation testing defaulted ON for <stack> — run /dso:onboarding --mutation-off to disable". Multi-stack: per-stack Socratic-confirm after the tradeoff context block. Writes `mutation.<stack>.enabled` keys to dso-config.conf. Copies `mutation-testing.yml` to `.github/workflows/`. Ensures the tickets-branch push permission scope exists in CI auth configuration. Documents bash as unsupported in the dialogue with ecosystem-limitation rationale.

SC7 (Phase 5 — create-dso-app.sh setup-script integration): plugins/dso/scripts/create-dso-app.sh updated. When scaffolding a new DSO-using project, the script applies the same single-stack-auto-default + multi-stack-confirm pattern as SC6. Writes default `mutation.<stack>.enabled=true` for detected stacks. Copies mutation-testing.yml alongside other CI workflow templates. Adds tickets-branch push permission to CI auth section. Coordination via ticket comment on d765-a3b6-84bd-4816 noting 411b's setup-script touchpoints.
SC8 (out-of-scope documentation + scope-seal): mutation-testing.yml header contains an explicit scope-seal block:
# SCOPE-SEALED: bash mutation tooling is out of scope — see 411b epic; do not reopen.
# Rationale: no mature mutation testing tool exists in the bash ecosystem.
# Supported stacks: Python (mutmut), Ruby (mutant), JavaScript/TypeScript (Stryker),
# Flask (Python — mutmut), Go (go-gremlins).

behavioral-testing-standard.md gains a Tier-3 addendum noting the supported stacks and the bash scope-seal with the 411b epic ID reference. plugins/dso/docs/contracts/mutation-testing-findings.md notes the scope decision. plugins/dso/docs/CI-INTEGRATION.md updated to document mutation-testing parallel job semantics, per-stack timeout handling, ALL_STACKS_TIMEOUT behavior, and TOOL_INSTALL_FAILED annotation. Reviewer assertion: code-reviewer-test-quality (or equivalent test-quality reviewer agent) flags any proposed bash-mutation-tooling additions as a scope violation.
SC9 (synthetic end-to-end test): Ten scenarios covering happy paths, adversarial paths, and post-calibration end-to-end loop:
(a) Phase 1 — PR with Python file changes triggers mutmut; PR comment posted with calibration-mode kill-rate telemetry.
(b) Phase 2 — PR with Python + JS + Go file changes produces aggregate PR comment with per-stack stats.

(c) Phase 3 — fixture with 20-PR telemetry + 4-week elapsed AND no existing mutation-calibration-review story produces exactly one calibration-review story ticket with all required fields. Re-running the same fixture produces no duplicate.

(d) Phase 4 — fixture with mutation.calibration.completed=true + per-stack threshold + synthetic breach produces a bug ticket with all required fields including 4-field blurb (max 60 words) and content-hash dedup tag. Re-running the same fixture produces no duplicate bug.

(e) Phase 5 — dispatch consolidated /dso:onboarding against a Python-only fixture project: mutation.python.enabled=true; mutation-testing.yml present in .github/workflows/; tickets-branch push permission scope present.
(f) skip-mutation-testing PR label opts out: workflow runs but no mutation jobs execute; PR comment surfaces opt-out confirmation.
(g) mutants_generated=0 produces no bug ticket (PR touched only non-mutable code).
(h) runtime_exceeded partial result is emitted in findings JSON when per-stack timeout fires.
(i) ALL_STACKS_TIMEOUT: all stacks return runtime_exceeded=true; PR comment surfaces warning; no bug ticket created even in threshold mode.

(j) Post-calibration end-to-end loop validation: PR with known-undertested function (mutant survives) against repo with mutation.calibration.completed=true AND per-stack threshold committed produces an auto-created bug ticket appearing in `ticket list --type=bug --status=open`. Same PR with added killing test produces no new bug ticket. Confirms the feedback loop is live end-to-end.

SC10 (validation signal): mutation-testing.yml referenced in CLAUDE.md Quick Reference table as the project's mutation-testing surface. mutation-testing-findings.md listed in plugins/dso/docs/contracts/ index. Both references link to 411b epic for context. Verify by: grep CLAUDE.md for "mutation-testing.yml" AND `ls plugins/dso/docs/contracts/` shows mutation-testing-findings.md.

SC11 (self-use): The 411b sprint deploys `mutation-testing.yml` to `.github/workflows/` in the host DSO repo before sprint close, and at least one 411b story-PR triggers a successful mutation-testing workflow run with a posted PR comment containing the `MUTATION_TESTING_FINDINGS_<pr-number>` marker. Dogfooding loop is proven end-to-end: the workflow ships AND fires on the very PRs that ship it. Verification (in-session, at sprint Phase I): `test -f .github/workflows/mutation-testing.yml` returns 0; `gh pr view <411b-story-pr> --comments | grep -q "MUTATION_TESTING_FINDINGS_"` returns 0 on at least one 411b story PR.
## Approach
5 sequential phases with an explicit interim release gate:
- Phase 1: SC1 (contract) + SC2 (Python pilot CI workflow)
- Phase 2: SC3 (Ruby + JS/TS + Go expansion)
Phases 1-2 (Python pilot + polyglot expansion) constitute a shippable informational-mode increment; Phases 3-5 follow in the same milestone:
- Phase 3: SC4 (calibration auto-surfacing)
- Phase 4: SC5 (threshold-mode enforcement + auto-bug-creation)
- Phase 5: SC6 + SC7 (onboarding + create-dso-app.sh integration) + SC8 (scope-seal documentation)
SC9 + SC10 (synthetic + validation signal) verified across phases as each ships.
## Scenario Analysis (Blue Team surviving)

- Per-stack mutation runtime explosion on large PRs (critical/performance): partially mitigated by SC2 max_files_per_run auto-skip + SC3 per-stack timeout caps + ALL_STACKS_TIMEOUT handling; residual is the case where most-but-not-all stacks time out.

- CI compute cost budget at scale (critical/cost): partially mitigated by skip-mutation-testing PR label + concurrency group + per-stack runtime caps; no org-level monthly-minute budget guard; accepted as residual for first version.

- Tool version drift / pin yanking (important/reliability): partially mitigated by fallback_versions chain + TOOL_INSTALL_FAILED annotation; residual is the case where all fallback versions are also unavailable.

- Calibration thresholds become stale as codebase evolves (moderate/correctness): unmitigated; no automatic re-calibration trigger; accepted as residual — operator may flip mutation.calibration.completed=false manually to re-enter calibration mode.
- Calibration data poisoned by low-quality initial test suites (moderate/correctness): partially mitigated by SC4 self-reflection prompt; no automatic floor enforcement on observed median.
- Monorepo diff scoping failure in Python with shared package dependencies (moderate/correctness): unmitigated; documented limitation of incremental-mode mutmut on monorepos.
- Phase 5 blocked indefinitely if 136b-6758 slips (moderate/planning): unmitigated; no degraded-mode onboarding path specified; if 136b-6758 slips significantly, Phase 5 is rescoped at that time.
## Out of Scope
- Bash mutation testing — no mature ecosystem tool; SCOPE-SEALED with rationale documented in SC8.
- Promotion to merge-blocking gate — reserved for a future hybrid epic informed by calibration data; this epic ships warn-only / informational-only.
- Pre-commit mutation invocation — operationally untenable per the time-cost analysis (1–4 min added to every commit).
- Nightly batch runs — PR-time only in this version.
- Mutation testing within the llm-review job itself — separate parallel job per the architectural decision.

- Test-writer agent prompt modifications — 411b's feedback loop is indirect via auto-created bugs flowing through /dso:fix-bug and 69e8's negative-example graduation; 411b does not modify how tests are written.
- Project-side dependency-manifest modifications — no pyproject.toml / package.json / Gemfile / go.mod additions in host projects (CI-installs-on-demand).
- Org-level monthly-minute cost budget guard — not specified in first version; can be a follow-on if cost becomes a concern.
- Automatic threshold re-calibration trigger — not specified in first version; operator flips mutation.calibration.completed=false manually if recalibration is needed.
## Operational Constraints (Architecture-vs-Evidence Audit Remediation, 2026-05-16)
### Workflow Trigger Filter Enumeration (Probe-2 remediation)
`plugins/dso/workflows/mutation-testing.yml` MUST follow the DSO repo trigger convention established by `ci.yml`:
| Trigger | Setting | Rationale |

| `pull_request` | `types: [synchronize, opened]`; no `branches:` filter | Covers per-story PRs whose base is a session branch, not `main` (bug 3914-0848-faad-4f6a). Restricting to `branches: [main]` would silently skip mutation testing on every story PR. |
| `pull_request_target` | Not used | Not needed — mutation testing reads only the PR diff and does not require fork-secret access. Avoids the known `pull_request_target` security pitfall. |
| `push` | Not used | Mutation testing is PR-time only by design (per Out-of-Scope: "nightly batch runs"). Push-trigger would duplicate cost on story-branch pushes that already have an open PR. |
`concurrency.group` keyed to `github.head_ref` (per SC2) already prevents in-flight duplication.

Verification (in-session, at sprint Phase I): `grep -A 20 '^on:' plugins/dso/workflows/mutation-testing.yml` shows `pull_request` block with no `branches:` key, no `pull_request_target` block, and no `push` block.
### State Lifecycle Owner Block (Probe-3 remediation)
| Variable | CREATE | UPDATE | CONSUME | RETIRE |

| `mutation.<stack>.enabled` (dso-config.conf) | `/dso:onboarding` (SC6) or `create-dso-app.sh` (SC7) at setup | `/dso:onboarding --mutation-off`; operator edit | `mutation-testing.yml` matrix gate | Stack removed; operator |
| `mutation.<stack>.tool_version` | Template default; onboarding | Operator edit; `create-dso-app.sh` | `mutation-testing.yml` tool-install step | Stack disabled |
| `mutation.<stack>.fallback_versions` | Template default | Operator edit | `mutation-testing.yml` install-fallback chain | Stack disabled |
| `mutation.<stack>.timeout_seconds` | Template default (per SC3 values) | Operator edit | `mutation-testing.yml` per-stack timeout | Stack disabled |

| `mutation.threshold.<stack>.min_kill_rate` | Operator, AFTER `mutation-calibration-review` story closes (SC4 → SC5) | Operator edit | `mutation-testing.yml` Phase-4 enforcement | Stack disabled OR `mutation.calibration.completed=false` flip |

| `mutation.calibration.completed` | Operator, when committing thresholds (SC5) | Operator (flip-back to false to re-calibrate, per Out-of-Scope) | `mutation-testing.yml` Phase-4 gate; SC4 config-consistency annotation | N/A — persistent project-state key |
| `mutation.max_files_per_run` | Template default = 100 | Operator edit | `mutation-testing.yml` pre-flight skip-check | N/A — persistent |

| Accumulated PR telemetry | Each workflow run uploads findings JSON as GHA artifact (per SC2) | Append-only via GHA artifact retention | SC4 calibration-floor scan over recent runs | Governed by GitHub Actions artifact retention (repo setting; default 90d) — anchors telemetry to GHA artifacts, NOT the tickets branch |
| Story tag `mutation-calibration-review` | SC4 auto-creation flow | Stable | SC4 pre-flight dedup | Persists through story close; new instance per calibration cycle |
| Bug tag `mutation-breach-<sha>` | SC5 auto-bug-creation flow | Stable | SC5 pre-flight dedup | Persists on bug ticket; new instance per unique surviving-mutant hash |
Verification (in-session, at sprint Phase I):
- `grep -E '^mutation\.' .claude/dso-config.conf` enumerates every key listed above (defaults present).
- `grep -nE 'mutation\.(enabled|tool_version|fallback_versions|timeout_seconds|threshold|calibration|max_files)' plugins/dso/workflows/mutation-testing.yml` confirms every CONSUME reference resolves.
- `grep -n 'actions/upload-artifact' plugins/dso/workflows/mutation-testing.yml` confirms telemetry CREATE path.
Closes the audit's named gaps: telemetry CREATE/RETIRE owner = GHA artifacts + retention; `mutation.calibration.completed` RETIRE = N/A (persistent, with operator flip-back path).
### External-dependency verification — addressable touchpoints (Probe-6 partial remediation with explicit override, 2026-05-18 follow-up)

The 2026-05-16 audit flagged probe 6 over four external touchpoints. Three are in-session-verifiable via fixtures + CLIs; one (4-week wall-clock telemetry emergence) is genuinely external. Adding the structured block with explicit override on the time-elapsed touchpoint.
| Touchpoint | In-session verification | Disposition |

| SC2: workflow RUNS in real GHA on real PRs | Covered by SC11 (self-use) — the 411b sprint deploys mutation-testing.yml AND at least one sprint PR triggers a successful run with the MUTATION_TESTING_FINDINGS_ marker. | IN-SESSION ✓ |

| SC4: 4-week-elapsed real-time telemetry-floor gate | Verified via SC9(c) fixture: a pre-built 20-PR + 4-week-elapsed telemetry fixture is replayed during the sprint and the calibration-review story-ticket auto-creation logic is exercised end-to-end. The CAPABILITY (gating logic + auto-creation flow) is verifiable in-session; the EMERGENCE (4 real weeks of real telemetry) is operational and not gated. | IN-SESSION (capability) ✓ + OPERATIONAL RESIDUAL (real emergence) |

| SC6: consuming projects install Python/Ruby/JS/Go toolchains in CI | Verified via a per-stack fixture project at `tests/fixtures/consuming-project-<stack>/` containing the manifest file (pyproject.toml / Gemfile / package.json / go.mod) and a stub `.github/workflows/`. The sprint runs `/dso:onboarding --fixture=tests/fixtures/consuming-project-python/` (etc. for each stack) and asserts that mutation-testing.yml is copied AND the relevant `mutation.<stack>.enabled=true` key is written. Real consuming projects installing in real CI is operational. | IN-SESSION (per-stack fixtures) ✓ + OPERATIONAL RESIDUAL (real projects) |

| SC7: create-dso-app.sh scaffolding lands in a new project | Sprint runs `create-dso-app.sh --target=$(mktemp -d)` against a temp directory and asserts mutation-testing.yml + dso-config.conf keys are present in the scaffolded output. Real new-project adoption is operational. | IN-SESSION (scaffolder fixture) ✓ + OPERATIONAL RESIDUAL (real new projects) |
### Explicit override note

Three of four touchpoints are now fully in-session-verifiable via fixtures (SC2 via SC11; SC6 + SC7 via per-stack fixture projects + temp-dir scaffolder runs). The fourth (SC4's 4-week-elapsed real-time emergence) is genuinely external; the spec's existing SC9(c) fixture provides in-session verification of the GATING CAPABILITY, while the real-world telemetry accumulation is acknowledged as operational and not gated. This is the same "capability verified in-session; real-world emergence is operational" pattern documented for SC11's dogfooding loop and the workflow-trigger-filter enumeration. Sprint closure gates on the capability checks; the emergence is observed post-ship without gating.

The audit's "structured External Dependencies block" pattern is honored in substance with each row's ownership (operator who runs the check) and access (gh CLI / `/dso:onboarding` / `create-dso-app.sh`, all available in-session) implicit in the verification command. Override applied because the genuinely-external piece is bounded to a single time-elapsed gate whose capability is independently verified.
## Dependencies
HARD:

- 136b-6758-ba12-47fc (Consolidate project-setup skills into resume-aware /dso:onboarding) — required for SC6. Phase 5's onboarding integration consolidates onto the unified /dso:onboarding rather than fragmenting across /dso:onboarding + /dso:init separately. Phases 1-4 ship independently while 136b-6758 is implemented in parallel.
SOFT (coordination, not blocking):
- a03c-d55e — closure-checks-aware verifier consumes 411b's auto-created bugs.
- 94ed-f55c — surviving-mutant findings can optionally map back to intent_id via the manifest for downstream analysis; not required for the core gate.
- d566-afa6 — indirect downstream consumer via 69e8's negative-example graduation.
- 69e8-af39 — auto-created bugs are 69e8's input signal; 69e8 extracts negative-example patterns from these bugs.

- d765-a3b6-84bd-4816 — create-dso-app.sh rewrite coordination. If d765-a3b6 ships first, 411b's additions integrate on top of its rewrite; if 411b ships first, d765-a3b6's rewrite must preserve 411b's mutation-testing hooks. Coordination via ticket comment on d765-a3b6 at Phase 3 ticket integration.
## Planning Intelligence Log

- Web research (Step 2): not triggered. Sufficient context inherited from d566-afa6 brainstorm's three-stream research synthesis (Meta TestGen-LLM 2025, Stryker --incremental, mutmut, PIT scmMutationCoverage, mull, go-gremlins, OOPSLA 2025 PBT evidence).

- Scenario analysis (Step 3): triggered (SCs >= 5); 20 red-team scenarios surfaced; 13 mitigated-by-spec after blue-team filter; 7 surviving (most partial-mitigations on inherent runtime/cost residuals and moderate-severity items deferred).
- Cross-epic scan (Step 2.25): 1 conflict (136b-6758 hard dep, expected); 2 considerations (d765-a3b6 coordination, 69e8 consumer); 3 benign.

- Bot-psychologist (Step 5): triggered (LLM-instruction signal — modifies /dso:onboarding via 136b-6758 consolidation, create-dso-app.sh, and adds LLM-consumed bug-blurb content). Five risks folded: anti-sycophancy tradeoffs-first onboarding (SC6), single-stack auto-default (SC6), p25 anti-anchor reference table with explicit column headers (SC4), bash scope-seal block + reviewer assertion (SC8), 4-field structured auto-bug blurb max 60 words (SC5).
- Fidelity review (Step 4): Agent Clarity (5, 4), Scope (4, 4, 4, 4), Value (4, 4). All dimensions >= 4 after one revision cycle.
- Scale context (Step 0): small-to-medium per-PR; mutation runs scoped to diffed lines only.
- Session-signal override for complexity routing: success_criteria_count = 10 (>= 7 threshold) — would route to /dso:preplanning full mode if invoked; preplanning explicitly deferred this session.
- User-directed design decisions during brainstorm:
- Polyglot first-class for Python, Ruby, JS/TS (including NextJS), Flask, Go; bash explicitly out of scope due to ecosystem-tool absence.
- CI parallel with llm-review; not a required merge check.
- Calibration-first delivery; thresholds set by human after telemetry-floor auto-surfaces a review ticket.
- Threshold breach auto-creates a bug ticket with explanatory blurb context for the investigating agent.
- CI-installs-on-demand (no project-side dependency-manifest changes; no local-env weight).
- Onboarding-side integration consolidated onto 136b-6758's unified /dso:onboarding rather than fragmenting across init+onboarding separately.
- dso setup script (create-dso-app.sh) updated for new-project scaffolding to include mutation-testing configuration.
## Closure Checks
- WHAT — one sentence on what mutation testing caught
- THRESHOLD — specific threshold that fired plus current kill rate
- NEXT_STEP — instructs investigating agent: investigate surviving mutants; do NOT adjust the threshold

content.text: ## Description

**What**: Wire the `semgrep.fail_on` config key through the CI template so the Semgrep invocation uses `--severity ERROR` when fail_on=error and `--severity WARNING --severity ERROR` when fail_on=warning, and ensure the Semgrep job is a required PR status check whose pass/fail is determined solely by Semgrep's exit code.

**Why**: Story 4c44-9805 confirms the non-zero-exit-on-findings invariant but does not pin (a) the conditional severity-flag construction driven by semgrep.fail_on, (b) the required-status-check wiring that makes the gate blocking, or (c) the decoupling of the blocking gate from SARIF upload success. Without these DDs, the user-facing fail_on knob from SC-3 has no observable runtime effect, and the gate could be accidentally weakened by a SARIF-upload failure.
**Scope**:
- IN: Template-level (examples/ci.example.yml) plus any helper logic constructing severity flags from dso-config.conf; integration-style tests for both fail_on values; SARIF-decoupling invariant test
- OUT: dso-config.conf schema changes (owned by c9aa-abda); SARIF jq post-processing logic (owned by 4c44-9805)
## Done Definitions
- When this story is complete, with semgrep.fail_on=error, the CI template renders/runs `semgrep scan --error --severity ERROR ...` and exits non-zero only on ERROR-severity findings

← Satisfies: sc-4  (sc-4: "CI step runs semgrep scan --error --severity ERROR — or --severity WARNING --severity ERROR when semgrep.fail_on=warning — causing exit code 1 when findings exist at or above the configured threshold")

- When this story is complete, with semgrep.fail_on=warning, the CI template renders/runs `semgrep scan --error --severity WARNING --severity ERROR ...` and exits non-zero on WARNING-or-higher findings
← Satisfies: sc-4

- When this story is complete, the Semgrep job in examples/ci.example.yml is configured so its conclusion (success/failure) is determined solely by Semgrep's exit code; a simulated SARIF-upload failure (upload-sarif step failing) does NOT change the Semgrep job's conclusion, demonstrating the blocking gate is decoupled from SARIF upload
← Satisfies: sc-4  (sc-4: "blocking gate depends on Semgrep's exit code, not on SARIF upload success")
- When this story is complete, examples/ci.example.yml documents (in comments and/or README cross-reference) that the Semgrep job is intended to be wired as a required status check for PR protection
← Satisfies: sc-4
- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic
## Considerations
- [Design] The conditional flag construction belongs in a small helper (shell function or generator), not inline in YAML, so it is testable
- [CI] `continue-on-error: true` must remain on the upload-sarif step (already required by sc-1) and must not propagate to the Semgrep scan step
- [Docs] Cross-reference 67b1-7f95: the README's fail_on threshold section should describe the runtime severity-flag behavior this story enforces

- [Required-checks] Whether the required-status-check is enforced by branch protection (project-side config) vs. asserted in the template is a project policy detail; the template can declare intent and provide the job name
## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.

content.text: Create tests/scripts/test-suggest-test-index.sh with RED tests for CI failure suggestion script (SC3, SC4).
## Test Cases
- test_creates_suggestion_on_failure: given failing test + changed source file where test fuzzy-matches source, appends suggestion to .test-index-suggestions
- test_dedup_against_test_index: suggestion already in .test-index → not appended
- test_dedup_against_suggestions: suggestion already in .test-index-suggestions → not appended
- test_creates_file_if_absent: .test-index-suggestions does not exist → created on first write
- test_multi_file_emits_per_pair: 3 changed files, 1 failing test fuzzy-matches 1 source → only 1 suggestion
- test_ambiguous_omitted: failing test matches no source file by fuzzy match → no suggestion emitted
- test_rebase_head_filter: during rebase, files from incoming branch excluded from suggestions
- test_format_matches_test_index: output line matches source/path.ext: test/path.ext format
## Test Approach

Each test creates temp .test-index, temp .test-index-suggestions (or absent), temp changed files list, and temp failing test output. Runs suggest-test-index.sh with these inputs and asserts file contents and exit codes.

content.text: Add a convention where consuming projects can place `<skill>-local/SKILL.md` files in their repo, and dso skills detect and reference them at runtime when present (no-op when absent). Today dso overrides happen via CLAUDE.md prose or plugin forks — neither is a clean per-skill extension point. Scope: define the lookup contract, pick 1-2 pilot skills (e.g. code-reviewer, triage rubric), document the override surface, and ensure absent/frontmatter-only companions are treated as no-op.

content.text: ## Context

Project agents (reviewers, fix-bug, retro) currently operate against static defense artifacts (rubrics, planning gates, tests) in a non-static bug-class space. There is no artifact that asserts every known bug class is named in some defense layer, and no feedback loop turning escaped bugs into rubric/test/observability extensions. Discovery-channel data from `docs/observed-failure-patterns-4-26.md` (repo-root-relative, read-only historical artifact) shows 16 of 22 recent closed bugs were caught at the release gate while code review caught only 3 of 37. Affected users: DSO maintainers and the agents themselves (orchestrator, /dso:fix-bug, /dso:retro, code-reviewer agents). Problem today: when a bug is caught downstream of review, no durable signal flows back to the rubric/test/observability layers. Outcome: shift bug detection earlier in the defense stack by making the bug-class map auditable, durable, and operationally connected. Replaces the original narrow scope of 4911-c7ba (six specific rubric items) with a categorical solution that subsumes those items as registry entries.
## Approach

Markdown registry seeded with a 27-slug, 9-group taxonomy (groups A-I: specification defects, environment portability, coupling and contract integrity, state and concurrency hazards, failure-mode and boundary defects, defense-system integrity, LLM/agent-orchestration defects, release and deploy hazards, operational state defects). Bash audit test asserts entry count, required fields, and defense_artifact_ref resolution. Haiku classifier sub-agent dispatched at /dso:fix-bug Phase G writes bug-type-<slug> tag with byte-exact schema validation and explicit failure-marker fallback. One-shot 60-day backfill script with single-run lock and tickets-branch assertion. /dso:retro adds aggregation step with MUST-surface labeled findings and positive-confirmation when no triggers fire.
## Success Criteria

1. Registry artifact at `plugins/dso/docs/bug-classification-registry.md` containing 27-slug 9-group taxonomy. Each entry has: slug (kebab-case), one-sentence classification question, primary defense layer (enum: planning_review, code_review, matrix_ci, coupling_test, concurrency_test, failure_path_test, defense_manifest_test, release_e2e, operational_process, prose_manifest_test), defense_artifact_ref with explicit prefix discriminator (`repo:`, `plugin:`, or `absolute:`), example tickets (>=2 where evidence exists), applies_to_project_classes enum (`all` or `agent_orchestration`).

2. Audit test parses the registry and asserts: (a) parsed entry count equals declared total (27 at seed time), (b) every entry has all required fields populated, (c) every `defense_artifact_ref` resolves (file present, named rubric section grep-matched, or test directory present). A mutation test confirms detection: a deliberately broken ref causes audit failure with a clear error identifying the broken slug.

3. `/dso:fix-bug` Phase G — Bug Classification (MANDATORY on `Fixed:` closure). The orchestrator MUST dispatch the bug-classifier-haiku agent on every closure with `--reason="Fixed:..."`. The sole exception is defined in the Skip block immediately below; no other skip exists. **Skip**: when the ticket was closed with `--reason="Escalated to user:..."` (keyed to reason prefix, NOT to whether code changed). Dispatch input: registry slug list with classification questions (unordered, one per line), bug title and description, fix diff summary. Output validation: orchestrator trims whitespace then byte-for-byte compares against `registry_slugs union {"uncategorized"}`; ANY deviation is schema failure (no fuzzy/normalization). Valid output writes `bug-type-<slug>` via the ticket tag CLI. Failure (schema/timeout/dispatch-error): MUST write BOTH `bug-type-uncategorized` AND `bug-type-classifier-failed-<reason>` where `<reason>` is one of `timeout`, `schema`, `dispatch-error` (dash-delimited, no colons). If a tag-write CLI call fails, retry once; on second failure, post a comment to the ticket recording the failure and treat the run as a protocol violation. Classifier prompt instructs: "Return a registry slug only if you would answer yes to its classification question with no caveats or conditionals; otherwise return `uncategorized`. Partial match is not a match."

4. Backfill script `backfill-bug-types.sh` iterates all bug tickets closed in the prior 60 days and applies the same classifier. Asserts tickets-branch presence at entry; uses a single-run lock under `.claude/locks/`; empty-list is a graceful no-op; idempotent re-run skips tickets already carrying any `bug-type-*` tag. Post-run, every closed bug in the 60-day window carries exactly one `bug-type-*` tag (the classifier-failed co-tag does not count toward the one-tag-per-bug rule). Backfill is implementation-splittable into a deferred-ok child task during preplanning if it complicates the registry + Phase G + retro delivery.

5. `/dso:retro` Bug Classification step (MANDATORY on every retro invocation). Calls `bug-classification-stats.sh --window-days <bug_classification.retro_window_days>` (default 60, aligned with the backfill window). Stats script uses `.claude/scripts/dso ticket list` (excludes deleted tickets) to aggregate `bug-type-*` tags. Config keys: `bug_classification.recurrence_threshold` (default 3), `bug_classification.retro_window_days` (default 60). Retro MUST surface EACH of these as a distinct, explicitly-labeled finding when its trigger fires; MUST NOT merge or inline into general retro prose:
- (a) `bug-type-uncategorized` count >= threshold: "Uncategorized bug count: N. Consider proposing a new registry slug or revisiting existing slug definitions."
- (b) any registry slug's count >= threshold: "Slug recurrence: <slug> has N occurrences in the window. Revisit mitigation strategy."

- (c) ANY `bug-type-classifier-failed-*` tag present in the window (fires when count >= 1; threshold fixed at 1, NOT configurable): "Classifier failures detected: N tickets carry bug-type-classifier-failed-*. Run diagnostic."

When no trigger fires, MUST emit explicit positive confirmation: "Bug classification health: no threshold breaches in this window." Silence is not acceptable. Within-session validation: post-backfill retro run on real backfilled data fires >=1 surfacing prompt OR emits the "no threshold breaches" confirmation; operator confirms before sprint closure.
6. **SC6 (self-use, Probe-1 remediation, architecture-vs-evidence audit 2026-05-16):** The 4911 sprint exercises both delivered orchestration surfaces against real data before sprint close.

**(a) Phase G classification** — the sprint's run of `backfill-bug-types.sh` against the 60-day window writes at least one valid `bug-type-<slug>` tag through the dispatched bug-classifier-haiku agent (proves the classifier dispatch + schema-validation + tag-write path is live end-to-end). If any bug is closed with `--reason="Fixed:..."` during the 4911 sprint itself, that closure ALSO triggers Phase G classification (proves the orchestrator-side dispatch hook fires on live closures, not only via the backfill script).

**(b) Retro aggregation** — the 4911 sprint's end-of-session `/dso:retro` invokes `bug-classification-stats.sh --window-days 60` and emits EITHER ≥1 MUST-surface labeled finding (a, b, or c per SC5) OR the explicit `"Bug classification health: no threshold breaches in this window."` line (proves the retro aggregation path is live end-to-end).
**Verification (in-session, at sprint Phase I):**

- `.claude/scripts/dso ticket list --type=bug --format=llm | python3 -c "import json,sys; ts=json.load(sys.stdin); print(sum(1 for t in ts for tag in (t.get('tags') or []) if tag.startswith('bug-type-')))"` returns ≥1.

- The retro session output (transcript or written retro artifact) contains exactly one of the substrings `"Slug recurrence:"`, `"Uncategorized bug count:"`, `"Classifier failures detected:"`, or `"Bug classification health: no threshold breaches"`.
## Out of Scope
- Code-reviewer agent rubric alignment with registry slug values (filed as follow-on a47f-b451-8f4c-46b1).
- Replay-corpus mechanical validation (a72d-df57-ac6e-4073, follow-on, depends_on this epic).
- Closed-loop automated rubric expansion (level c, not yet scheduled).
## Delivery checklist (not SCs)
- Registry + audit test ship in the same PR (no commit-order window).
- New `.sh` files chmod'd at creation.
## Coordination notes (relates_to)
- a72d-df57 — Level-b replay corpus follow-on; depends_on this epic.
- a47f-b451 — Code-reviewer rubric alignment follow-on; scrutiny:pending stub.
- 1de7-50d4 — Resolution-enum epic; both add fields at /dso:fix-bug Phase G. Coordinate ordering: resolution writes a closure field, this epic writes a tag; both are additive.
- 99f1-153c — fix-bug recurrence prevention; bug-type-* tags feed antipattern detection.
- 371f-cfc3 — DSO ticket system packaging; audit test depends on stable ticket CLI contract.
- 5df7-63ac, 853a-c719 — observability epics; stats-script patterns may converge.
- 7575-5a90 — static-analysis defense layer; audit test registers with framework if/when it lands.
- cfb3-3f53 — ticket compaction; retro step ordering (classification before snapshot).
- w21-bsnz — legacy-code remediation; taxonomy alignment opportunity.
## Reframe note

This epic was originally scoped as "Reviewer rubric expansion: platform, runner, hermeticity, config, pipefail dimensions" — adding six specific named rubric items. During the 2026-05-11 brainstorm session, scope was broadened to a categorical solution (this spec). The original six items become registry entries under groups B (environment-portability, strict-mode-survival), C (paired-artifact-coupling), and F (defense-integrity), where the audit test asserts each has a primary defense layer with a resolved defense_artifact_ref.
## Provenance

See docs/observed-failure-patterns-4-26.md, docs/process-gaps-4-26.md, docs/proposed-mitigations-4-26.md, docs/new-epics-4-26.md for the original failure-pattern analysis and gap discovery. The categorical reframe and 27-slug taxonomy emerged during the 2026-05-11 brainstorm session (broadened from the original 6 mitigations into 9 groups covering polyglot bug classes).

content.text: ## Context

Seven deterministic ticket validation and classification scripts live outside the ticket system despite performing pure ticket operations — checking ticket health, scoring clarity, validating acceptance criteria, assessing dispatch readiness, classifying tasks for agent routing, generating summaries, and purging stale bridge data. Each script already uses the ticket CLI for data access but is not part of the ticket system itself. Absorbing them makes the ticket system opinionated — able to answer "is this ticket ready for dispatch?" and "how should this task be routed?" — rather than being a passive data store that external scripts interrogate.
## Success Criteria

- Seven new ticket CLI subcommands exist and are callable via the ticket CLI dispatcher: validate (health diagnostics with --quick/--full/--fix/--json/--terse flags and 5-tier scored exit codes 0-4 — replaces validate-issues.sh), classify (deterministic keyword scoring accepting ticket ID, outputting JSON with model/subagent/class/complexity/priority fields — replaces classify-task.sh/py), clarity-check (heuristic clarity scoring — replaces ticket-clarity-check.sh), check-ac (acceptance criteria block validation — replaces check-acceptance-criteria.sh), quality-check (readiness validation for issue-as-prompt dispatch — replaces issue-quality-check.sh), summary (one-line ticket summary with blocking status for one or more ticket IDs — replaces issue-summary.sh), and purge-bridge (removal of inbound bridge tickets not matching a specified project key — replaces purge-non-project-tickets.sh)

- Each new subcommand has an integration test in tests/ exercising the subcommand through the ticket CLI dispatcher against a synthetic fixture, asserting output equivalence (same exit codes, same JSON keys and values, same text format) with the script it replaces
- classify uses the existing deterministic keyword-matching logic from classify-task.py (no LLM); the poetry environment resolution requirement is documented in the subcommand's implementation
## Done Definitions

- When this epic is complete, developers can validate ticket health via `ticket validate` with --quick/--full/--fix/--json/--terse flags and the same 5-tier scored exit codes (0-4) as validate-issues.sh
← Satisfies: "validate (health diagnostics with --quick/--full/--fix/--json/--terse flags and 5-tier scored exit codes 0-4)"

- When this epic is complete, developers can classify tasks via `ticket classify <id>` and receive JSON with model/subagent/class/complexity/priority fields using the deterministic keyword scoring engine from classify-task.py (no LLM)
← Satisfies: "classify (deterministic keyword scoring accepting ticket ID, outputting JSON with model/subagent/class/complexity/priority fields)"

- When this epic is complete, the ticket system answers "is this ticket ready for dispatch?" (quality-check), "is the AC block valid?" (check-ac), and "how should this task be routed?" (classify) through its own CLI — callers no longer invoke separate scripts for these questions
← Satisfies: "seven new ticket CLI subcommands exist and are callable via the ticket CLI dispatcher"
- When this epic is complete, each of the seven new subcommands has an integration test asserting output equivalence (same exit codes, JSON keys/values, text format) with the script it replaces
← Satisfies: "Each new subcommand has an integration test in tests/ exercising the subcommand through the ticket CLI dispatcher against a synthetic fixture, asserting output equivalence"
## Scope

- IN: Seven ticket-*.sh/py subcommands, dispatcher integration, integration tests against synthetic fixtures, poetry environment resolution documented for classify, preservation of validate's 5-tier exit-code contract and full flag surface

- OUT: Refactoring callers of the absorbed scripts to use the new CLI (caller migration is Epic e1b2-2653's concern); removing or deprecating the original scripts (they remain as thin wrappers if still called anywhere); any LLM-based classification
## Considerations
- [Maintainability] Seven new ticket-*.sh/py scripts follow the existing ticket dispatcher pattern — consistent with sibling subcommands
- [Reliability] validate MUST preserve the full --quick/--full/--fix/--json/--terse flag surface and the 5-tier scored exit code contract (0=OK, 4=critical) — downstream callers branch on exit code
- [Reliability] classify MUST preserve classify-task.py's deterministic keyword scoring — no LLM, no behavior change, only a CLI wrapper change
- [Reliability] purge-bridge is LOCAL-ONLY (no Jira API calls) — MUST validate tracker is mounted AND writable before any deletion to prevent destructive operation against an unmounted tracker
- [Testing] Each subcommand requires integration test via CLI dispatcher against synthetic fixture; output equivalence with the replaced script is the pass condition
- [Maintainability] classify's poetry environment resolution (for the Python scoring engine) must be documented in the subcommand implementation so callers understand the environment requirement
## Dependencies
None (purely additive — no existing scripts are removed or refactored in this epic; can proceed in parallel with Epic 2c28-e5b9)
## Approach

One ticket-*.sh or ticket-*.py script per subcommand, dispatched from ticket-cli.sh. classify wraps classify-task.py's scoring engine. validate preserves the full --quick/--full/--fix/--json/--terse flag surface and 5-tier exit code contract. purge-bridge performs local-only cleanup (no Jira API calls) — validates tracker is mounted AND writable before any deletion.
## Research Findings
- Dispatcher pattern: ticket-cli.sh routes subcommands to ticket-<subcommand>.sh/py — 7 new subcommands follow the existing sibling pattern; no new architecture

- 5-tier scored exit code convention: validate-issues.sh established 0-4 tier semantics (0=OK, 1=info, 2=warn, 3=important, 4=critical) — downstream callers branch on exit code; contract preservation is critical

- Poetry environment resolution: classify-task.py runs under the plugin's poetry environment; `ticket classify` must resolve the same environment (documented in subcommand implementation) — pattern matches existing Python-backed subcommands
- LOCAL-ONLY purge pattern: purge-non-project-tickets.sh operates on the local .tickets-tracker/ only; no Jira API calls; mount-check guard prevents destructive ops against an absent tracker

- Output equivalence testing: integration tests use synthetic .tickets-tracker/ fixtures (same pattern as test-sprint-next-batch.sh); byte-for-byte output comparison for text; JSON key/value match for structured output
## Scenario Analysis

- validate drops a tier semantic in the port (high, correctness): downstream callers branch on exit code 0-4; any behavioral drift breaks caller logic silently — contract preservation explicitly tested via integration test with exit-code assertions for each tier
- classify poetry environment not resolved in test fixture (medium, testing): fixture needs reproducible poetry env; integration test documents environment prerequisite or uses env-var override
- purge-bridge tracker-mount check too permissive (high, safety): check must verify actual .tickets-tracker/ existence AND writability, not just path presence; false-negative permits destructive ops

- summary on a ticket with circular blocks relationship loops (medium, correctness): summary generation must detect cycles (reuse existing cycle-detection from deps command); bounded traversal prevents infinite loop

- Output format drift between text and JSON modes (medium, correctness): each subcommand's --json flag must produce structurally consistent output; integration test covers both text and JSON modes for each subcommand

- Missing poetry env for classify at runtime (medium, deployment): when poetry env is missing (e.g., CI without poetry install), classify must emit diagnostic and exit non-zero, not silently fallback; documented requirement in subcommand help

- Thin-wrapper compatibility broken for existing callers (high, integration): original script names (validate-issues.sh etc.) must remain callable as thin wrappers until Epic e1b2-2653 migrates callers; wrapper preservation tested
### Planning Intelligence Log
- **Web research (Step 2.6)**: not triggered — bright-line none (absorbing existing deterministic scripts into the ticket system; no external integration, no novel pattern)
- **Scenario analysis (Step 2.75)**: triggered
- Scenarios surviving blue team filter: 7
- **Practitioner-requested additional cycles**: none
- **Follow-on scrutiny (Step 0)**: not triggered
- **Feasibility resolution (Step 2.5)**: not triggered
- **LLM-instruction signal (Step 5)**: not triggered — subcommand additions only, no agent/skill file modifications (caller migration is e1b2-2653's concern)
- **Scale context (Step 0)**: small scale (default) — per-ticket validation/classification invocation; not volume-sensitive

**What**: Extend tests/scripts/test-create-dso-app-real-url.sh (opt-in via RUN_REAL_URL_E2E=1; runs daily in CI) with failing integration tests for the new flow. Cover: Rails default end-to-end (working app + USWDS + SDK gem in Gemfile + DSO overlay files + tickets orphan branch + post-build SDK functional check); --template=nextjs scaffold without SDK gem; --template=flask scaffold without SDK gem; --no-sdk skip; --no-overlay skip; --port=8080 propagates to upstream app_local_port; --auto-install-prereqs unattended; A2-idempotency assertion (zero diffs on dso-config.conf, ARCH_ENFORCEMENT.md, project-understanding.md Strata Posture section against A2's onboarding-time idempotency check).
This is the **integration RED test story** for an external-API epic. Tests must fail before any implementation story (S1-S8, S10) lands.
**Why**: Real-URL behavioral test is the contract that the rewrite preserves user-visible scaffolding behavior; it gates the fork archive.
**Scope**:
- IN: New test cases extending the existing file; opt-in env var preserved; CI daily schedule preserved; A2-idempotency cross-check assertion.
- OUT: Implementing the installer phases (other stories).
