content.text: ## Background

Closure of bug 0ac3-dab8-abfd-4359 ("[tests/scripts/test-write-cycle-ledger.sh]: intermittent failures") revealed a process-level defect in how umbrella tickets get split into child tickets during cluster-investigation triage.
## Symptom

A ticket can be split out of an umbrella inheriting an "intermittent failure" symptom-claim that has **no captured CI evidence** anywhere — yet still consume ADVANCED-tier investigator budget (two opus investigators, one full hour) before the absence-of-evidence is detected.
## Concrete example (0ac3-dab8-abfd-4359 → 53f9-a218-8799-49be)
1. Umbrella 53f9 was filed 2026-05-17 citing same-commit-run-A-vs-B evidence for test-merge-to-main*.sh (4 specific assertion failures, 2 CI run links).

2. The umbrella's **TITLE** mentions test-write-cycle-ledger.sh — but the umbrella's **Actual Behavior** section enumerates only test-merge-to-main*.sh failures. No same-commit-A-vs-B evidence for test-write-cycle-ledger.sh is cited anywhere in the umbrella.

3. The cluster-investigation comment classified the umbrella as bundling 4 sub-tracks; Track B = "test-write-cycle-ledger.sh intermittent failures → DISPROVED as state-file race; separate investigation needed." The DISPROVED→separate-needed pattern carried the attribution forward without ever requiring an evidence link.
4. BASIC tier then offered a hypothesis ("most likely the concurrent-write test ... non-atomic assertion window") for the inherited (un-evidenced) symptom.

5. On user direction, the umbrella was split into 4 child tickets, one per track. Track B became 0ac3-dab8-abfd-4359 — inheriting the symptom-claim verbatim into the new ticket's description ("fails intermittently in CI. Same commit, same code — pass on one run, fail on the next.") despite zero captured CI evidence of that pattern for THIS test file.

6. ADVANCED-tier investigation (two opus investigators, code-tracer + historical) ran for ~58 minutes total and converged with HIGH confidence on: no defect exists; B3 lock correctly serializes concurrent writers; A2's race is benign; **and** no CI evidence of a same-commit-A-vs-B failure for test-write-cycle-ledger.sh exists in git history or in the umbrella's cited runs.
## Root cause (process)

Cluster-investigation and umbrella-split-out logic accepts attribution-by-title as sufficient grounds to propagate a symptom-claim into a child ticket. There is no evidence-link requirement on the propagation step. The pattern "DISPROVED as X; separate investigation needed" reinforces this — it carries the symptom-claim forward as established fact while simultaneously disproving the first explanatory hypothesis, locking in a phantom-symptom inheritance.
## Proposed fix
Before splitting an umbrella into a child ticket, require **at minimum one of**:
1. A specific CI run URL + failing test/assertion name observed in that run for the child's affected file, OR

2. An explicit `attribution_basis: speculative` flag in the child ticket header, with the BASIC-tier scoring rubric routing speculative-attribution tickets to a separate, lighter triage path (e.g., manual confirmation before any investigation budget is spent) instead of the standard tier-based investigation routing.
## Affected files
- plugins/dso/skills/fix-bug/SKILL.md (Cluster Investigation Mode logic)
- plugins/dso/skills/fix-bug/prompts/cluster-mode-protocol.md (or equivalent — split-out instructions)
- Possibly: plugins/dso/skills/create-bug/SKILL.md (require evidence link before creating a bug whose source is "split from umbrella X")
## Detected_by
User reflection on the 0ac3 closure question "if no defect exists, what caused the symptom reported in the bug?" — the answer "there was no documented symptom" surfaced the process-level pattern.

content.text: ## Context

DSO's per-step HARD-GATE workflows (COMMIT, REVIEW) currently express compliance as prose inside the workflow docs. A bot-psychologist Probe B (sycophancy probe against a fresh sub-agent) confirmed the gate is reachable when an agent is challenged but is not load-bearing during silent autonomous execution: agents batch steps, skip advisory breadcrumb writes, drop classifier-flagged overlay dispatches (bug 94e8-9f91), pipe validation output through truncating filters that mask diagnostics, and never write the breadcrumb log (bug 7b41-3061). A user reporter on a host .NET project experienced this across multiple sessions before catching it manually. The same psychology was hardened on the reviewer surface in closed epic db68-ca95; this epic is its orchestrator-side counterpart.

The single outcome of this epic is: ship a load-bearing pre-commit verifier gate that is safe to deploy in production sessions — meaning (a) the gate enforces the right thing, (b) agents cannot silently bypass it, (c) the gate has a sane override path so legitimate commits aren't permanently blocked when the gate is wrong, (d) the gate has zero false positives on existing valid commit paths.
## Success Criteria

- SC1 — Verifier as load-bearing pre-commit gate. A new pre-commit hook (parity tier with existing test-gate / review-gate) reads the breadcrumb log and wrapper-written validation artifacts for the worktree where the commit is being made and refuses the commit when (a) any expected artifact is missing for a step that should have run under the active enforcement.strategy and SKIP_REVIEW state, or (b) the classifier flagged one or more REVIEW overlays without their corresponding findings artifacts. Test fixtures: synthetically removing a wrapper artifact triggers the block; synthetic missing overlay findings file (with classifier-flagged overlay) triggers the block. Regression tests reproduce the failure surfaces of bugs 94e8-9f91 (overlay flags ignored) and 7b41-3061 (empty breadcrumb log) and confirm both are mechanically prevented as a direct consequence of SC1's enforcement.

- SC2 — Truncation-masking immunity. Validation commands (test, format, lint, classifier dispatch, reviewer dispatch) run through wrappers that capture full output into result artifacts. The verifier reads from the artifact, not from the agent's terminal stream. Test fixture: an agent invoking the wrapper with `2>&1 | tail -3` (or any other agent-side output filter) does not change what the verifier sees and does not allow a hidden lint/test failure to slip through.

- SC3 — Per-commit interactive override path (release-blocking precondition for SC1). A hard-blocking gate is unsafe to deploy without a sane escape hatch for legitimate commits the gate gets wrong. Override is reachable only via explicit `dso commit-override --reason="<text>"` invoked by the user (not the agent). Override applies to exactly one commit attempt and writes a durable audit record (in $ARTIFACTS_DIR and as a comment/trailer on the commit) listing the missing artifacts and the user's reason. Test fixture: a single override clears the next commit; a second attempt without re-authorization is blocked again. Cross-epic constraint: when dso-fbky autonomous mode is active, dso commit-override returns an error and the hook still blocks.

- SC4 — Worktree-context safety in all three execution contexts. Verifier and wrappers behave correctly when commit runs in (a) the main repo, (b) a session worktree, (c) an isolated sub-agent worktree harvested back via the existing harvest-worktree.sh / record-test-status.sh --attest paths. Verifier reads artifacts only from the worktree where the commit is being made; sub-agent artifacts reach it only through the existing harvest path. A wrapper invoked from a CWD that does not match the worktree it would write to fails fast with a clear error rather than silently writing to a sibling worktree's artifacts dir. Test fixtures cover all three contexts plus the misconfigured-CWD failure mode.

- SC5 — Conditional-step skip markers and zero false-positive baseline. Legitimately-skipped steps (e.g., enforcement.strategy=ci, SKIP_REVIEW=true, commands.test_changed unset) emit explicit `skipped:<reason>` artifacts that the verifier accepts. A passing run of validate.sh --ci and a clean DSO-self-commit on this epic demonstrate the verifier introduces zero false positives on existing valid commit paths — the gate fires only on actual non-compliance.
## Dependencies
None blocking.

This epic blocks: af26-dd5a-df6d-4f81 (forbidden-action HARD-GATE follow-on; reuses the override-path infrastructure, artifacts-dir resolution, and audit-trail pattern delivered here) and f61f-7e0a-36d3-4e7d (per-story PR review with incremental attestation; f61f's attestation strategy must build on this epic's verifier — clarified during f61f's own brainstorm).
Subsumed: bugs 94e8-9f91 (overlay flags silently dropped) and 7b41-3061 (breadcrumb log empty) close as a direct consequence of SC1 — no separate work axis.
Related, not blocking: closed epic db68-ca95 (reviewer-side AI-blindspot hardening — same psychology, different surface).
## Approach

Wrapper-driven artifact verification (Option A from Phase 2). Each per-step validation command (test, format, lint, classifier dispatch, reviewer dispatch) is invoked through a thin wrapper (`.claude/scripts/dso commit-step <name>`) that runs the underlying command, captures the full output, and atomically writes a result artifact alongside the breadcrumb. A new pre-commit hook reads the artifacts (not agent stdout) and refuses commits with missing artifacts, missing overlay findings, or visible truncation markers. Override is reachable only via `dso commit-override --reason="..."` invoked by the user. The verifier resolves artifacts via get_artifacts_dir() of the worktree where commit happens; cross-worktree artifact transfer remains via the existing harvest-worktree.sh / --attest mechanism — no new cross-worktree paths.
## Cross-Epic Interactions

- Resource: per-commit override mechanism. Interaction: dso-fbky autonomous mode must NOT bypass this epic's verifier or override path. Gate: when autonomous mode is active, dso commit-override returns an error and the hook still blocks on missing artifacts.

- Resource: artifacts-dir / harvest atomicity. Interaction: 70f6-05f1 parallel-worktree review introduces N concurrent harvests. Gate: harvest into a target worktree's artifacts dir is atomic per-target; verifier does not race when multiple sub-agent worktrees harvest concurrently.

- Resource: reviewer-findings artifact family. Interaction: dbbc-cf67-8cfc-4b4d stateful re-review persists multi-cycle review state. Gate: overlay-dispatch verification reads the latest cycle's classifier output and findings files; multi-cycle state does not produce false-positive missing-findings blocks.

- Resource: test step execution path. Interaction: a524-fded migrates test execution to a background primitive. Gate: the wrapper for the test step captures full output regardless of whether the underlying test command runs synchronously or backgrounded.

- Resource: skipped-step structural records. Interaction: a154-98de PRECONDITIONS degradation channel introduces structural attestation for graceful-degradation paths. Gate: SC5 skipped:<reason> markers conform to the same schema as PRECONDITIONS attestation records, or the schemas are explicitly aligned in a follow-up.

- Resource: silent-skip detection psychology. Interaction: e884-d0ad PostToolUse forced next-step reminder targets the same root-cause failure mode at a different point in the loop. Gate: pre-commit verifier and PostToolUse reminder do not double-fire on the same skip event; one is authoritative for any given skip class.

- Resource: commit message construction order. Interaction: 170b-2ac9 commit-level source attribution via git-native trailers. Gate: artifact verification runs before trailer injection; ordering documented in COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md.

- Resource: breadcrumb log format. Interaction: 5df7-63ac integrated observability. Gate: breadcrumb log entries written by wrappers include observability-compatible fields (timestamp, step name, agent context, optional cost hooks) so 5df7-63ac can consume the same log without duplicating infrastructure.

- Resource: wrapper-written artifact metadata. Interaction: e407-d35c source attribution. Gate: wrapper artifacts include attribution metadata fields (skill name, agent ID, sub-agent context) that e407-d35c can read without separate metadata files.

- Resource: classifier / reviewer dispatch interface. Interaction: f9f8-a15c-79e0-4dc3 add Gemini provider to CI LLM review provider abstraction. Gate: wrapper output capture for classifier and reviewer dispatch is provider-agnostic; the artifact contract does not depend on a specific provider.

- Resource: hook installation pipeline. Interaction: 87e9-0bc8 polyglot test gate modifies reinstall-hooks.sh. Gate: the new pre-commit verifier registers via the same install path; hook execution order documented so polyglot test-gate and verifier compose deterministically.

- Resource: pre-commit gate execution order. Interaction: 88d2-6756 / jira-dig-1671 required CodeQL + code-quality scanning gates. Gate: artifact verification, CodeQL scanning, and other pre-commit gates each run as discrete steps that compose; no implicit dependence on each other's output beyond pass/fail signaling.

- Resource: reviewer override semantics. Interaction: jira-dig-1673 reviewer override discipline. Gate: dso commit-override composes with — does not bypass — reviewer override discipline; user-invoked override does not silently dismiss reviewer findings; produces an audit record both gates can consume.

- Resource: REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md overlay-dispatch verified-artifact set. Interaction: cbea-3722 ACCESSIBILITY_REVIEWER agent integration. Gate: when accessibility reviewer is dispatched as part of REVIEW Step 4b, its findings file is part of the verified-artifact set; missing accessibility-findings.json (when accessibility was flagged) triggers the same block as missing security-redteam-findings.json.
## Scenario Analysis
11 surviving failure scenarios from red/blue team filter (16 raised; 5 filtered as speculative or already-handled).
Critical:

- CWD mismatch fast-fail triggers inside legitimate sub-agent worktrees during harvest — wrapper's CWD check must compare resolved target artifacts dir's worktree root, not process CWD, or every harvest invocation rejects.
- New pre-commit hook not executable after fresh clone or plugin sync overwrites it — git silently skips non-executable hooks; entire load-bearing gate is bypassed without error.
High:
- Artifact write and pre-commit hook read race under parallel sub-agent harvest; spurious gate failures during in-flight harvests.
- Wrapper artifact write swallowed when underlying command times out (~73s ceiling); missing artifact with no diagnostic trail.
- a524-fded background test primitive output not captured when test runs detached; empty/stub artifact misinterpreted as test failure.
- ARTIFACTS_DIR undefined in CI environment causes hook to crash or resolve to wrong path.
- Hook added after existing pre-commit hook causes silent override of prior hook chain in host projects.
- First-run artifact directory missing causes hook to block all commits before any wrapper has run.
- commands.test_changed unset causes wrapper to emit no artifact and hook to block instead of skip.
- review.max_resolution_attempts exhaustion + verifier block produces deadlock — agent has no automated path to unblock.
- Breadcrumb log path diverges between wrapper write and hook read when worktree uses non-default branch name with special characters.
### Planning Intelligence Log

- Bright-line conditions that fired: none (no third-party API, no new dependency, no auth/credentials, no migration; wrapper pattern is established internally via existing test-gate / review-gate)
- **Scenario analysis (Step 2.75)**: triggered
- Scenarios surviving blue team filter: 11 (of 16 red team findings)

- **Practitioner-requested additional cycles**: cross-epic scan re-triggered via gate (manual triage initially; full classifier dispatch on practitioner authorization, surfacing 1 additional ambiguity (f61f-7e0a-36d3-4e7d) and 8 additional considerations injected as Cross-Epic Interactions ACs)
- **Follow-on scrutiny (Step 0)**: triggered — depth: 0 (forbidden-action HARD-GATE follow-on stub created as af26-dd5a-df6d-4f81; scrutiny intentionally skipped at practitioner's direction)
- **Feasibility resolution (Step 2.5)**: not triggered

- **LLM-instruction signal (Step 5)**: triggered — keyword: hook behavioral logic (bot-psychologist Probe B during pre-Phase 1 covered the orchestrator behavioral surface; concrete prompt edits will go through plan-review during /dso:preplanning)
- **Scale context (Step 0)**: not applicable (developer-tooling feature; per-invocation overhead matters but no record/traffic axis)

DIG-4393.summary: Make HARD-GATE per-step workflow compliance load-bearing via wrapper-driven artifact verification

content.text: ## Context

The DSO ticket system has accumulated 113 non-closed orphan story/task tickets (16 stories + 97 tasks) because skill files and sub-agent dispatch prompts do not reliably thread parent_id through ticket create calls. The 2026-05-12 audit reports a 1/5 health score with 106 warnings dominated by "orphan ticket: no epic parent". DSO maintainers cannot trust dependency graphs, sprint scoping, or epic completion semantics. Sprint orchestrators and sub-agents that consume the dependency graph to scope work and determine epic completion are also impaired — incorrect parent linkage causes misordered batches and premature epic closure. Hard-fail at ticket creation is rejected — capturing ticket data must take precedence over enforcing structure — so remediation is primarily structural: the orchestrator writes a literal --parent=<id> at every ticket create story|task call site (including literal injection into sub-agent dispatch prompts before dispatch), and a CI test enforces this structurally by scanning every SKILL.md and dispatch prompt. The existing bug-template enforcement pattern at ticket-create.sh lines 279-328 is retained as a backstop — the CLI exits 0 and emits a structured stderr ERROR with explicit "To fix:" command — with the stderr-capture+ticket edit --parent remediation snippet applied only at the orchestrator-context shell sites where bash stderr capture is reliable. The standalone ticket tag marks tickets that intentionally have no parent; standalone-tagged tickets are excluded from orphan warnings.
## Success Criteria

- validate-issues.sh --quick --terse reports 0 orphan story/task warnings AND no non-closed story/task in the live tracker has parent_id=null, EXCLUDING tickets tagged standalone (intentional opt-out) and tickets tagged defer or dso-cleanup-pending (owned by 7271-e463). Before/after diff produced inside the sprint session by running validate-issues.sh --quick --terse immediately after orphan-cleanup.sh completes.

- ticket-create.sh emits "ERROR: <type> ticket <id> created without --parent" to stderr followed by "To fix: ticket edit <id> --parent=<parent-id>" whenever a non-bug, non-standalone-tagged ticket is created without --parent; exit code remains 0 (shell unit test).

- ticket-link.sh retries up to 3 times with exponential backoff (configurable via ticket_link.retry_base_ms=250 and ticket_link.retry_max_ms=2000 with documented defaults), appends a structured JSON entry to the tracker link-failures log on persistent failure (fallback to ${REPO_ROOT}/.dso/link-failures.log when the tracker directory is absent), and emits structured ERROR to stderr (shell unit test).

- PRIMARY (load-bearing): A CI test under plugins/dso/tests/ scans every SKILL.md under plugins/dso/skills/ AND every agent dispatch prompt under plugins/dso/agents/ for ticket create story|task invocations and fails the build when any such invocation does not include an inline --parent= argument in the same command. All flagged sites are remediated within this epic's scope (not deferred). Three pre-existing missing-parent example sites are explicitly remediated: interface-contracts SKILL.md lines 82-87, tickets-health SKILL.md lines 113 and 116, preplanning/prompts/ui-designer-dispatch-protocol.md line 298.

- BACKSTOP: Every orchestrator-context shell block calling ticket create story|task captures stderr via mktemp and runs ticket edit <id> --parent=<id> when "created without --parent" signal observed. Applied only at sites where literal-parent injection at the call site is unreliable (orchestrator constructs parent ID dynamically from session state); site list finalized in preplanning.
## Operational Constraints (Architecture-vs-Evidence Audit Remediation, 2026-05-16)
### State Lifecycle Owner Block (Probe-3 remediation)
| Variable | CREATE | UPDATE | CONSUME | RETIRE |
| `ticket_link.retry_base_ms` (default 250) | `/dso:onboarding` / dso-config.conf template | Operator edit | ticket-link.sh exponential-backoff loop | N/A — persistent config |
| `ticket_link.retry_max_ms` (default 2000) | Same | Same | Same | N/A — persistent |

| `.dso/link-failures.log` (structured JSON, fallback path) | ticket-link.sh on first persistent failure (mkdir -p + append) | Append-only per failure | Human review; debug-everything for `link-failures` pattern | Rotation: operator manual. Log grows until operator archives/deletes; recommended trigger: >1000 entries OR >1 MiB → archive via `mv .dso/link-failures.log .dso/link-failures-$(date +%Y%m%d).log`. No auto-rotation in v1. |

| `dso-cleanup-pending` tag | orphan-cleanup.sh opus residual step (Step 5) | Stable (no in-place mutation) | 7271-e463 future epic (residual handoff target); validate-issues.sh exclusion | Removed by 7271-e463 worker after processing — explicit untag via `dso ticket untag <id> dso-cleanup-pending` once the residual has been resolved (reparented, retyped, or closed). Closes the audit's named gap. |

| `standalone` tag | Author at ticket creation (intentional opt-out) | Stable | validate-issues.sh exclusion from orphan warnings | Operator untag when the ticket gains a real parent OR closes; manual lifecycle |

| `orphan-cleanup.lock` (flock target in tracker dir) | orphan-cleanup.sh acquires at start | Held for run duration | The script itself (concurrency guard) | Released automatically on script exit (normal or crash); stale lock detection via flock timeout or PID check at next invocation |
Verification (in-session, at sprint Phase I):
- `grep -E '^ticket_link\.retry_' .claude/dso-config.conf` shows both keys with defaults documented.
- `test -d "$(dirname .dso/link-failures.log)" || mkdir -p .dso` runs cleanly (path creation handled).

- `.claude/scripts/dso ticket list --has-tag=dso-cleanup-pending --format=llm | python3 -c "import json,sys; print(len(json.load(sys.stdin)))"` — value recorded as sprint baseline for the 7271-e463 handoff.
- The 7271-e463 ticket carries an explicit comment referencing this RETIRE contract (untag once processed).
## Dependencies
- 5efb-06ea (blocker) — provides the ticket reparent primitive used by the retro cleanup pipeline and (when stderr-capture backstop fires) by the remediation snippet

- Relates to 7271-e463 (/dso:cleanup skill) — orphan partition boundary: 7271-e463 owns defer/dso-cleanup-pending-tagged orphans; this epic owns all others; RESIDUAL handoff via dso-cleanup-pending tag
- Relates to 83e2-04ae (Jira bridge parent sync) — re-parenting from the cleanup pipeline must be visible to the bridge
- Relates to af26-dd5a (load-bearing HARD-GATEs in same SKILL.md files) — coordinate edit order; CI grep test accepts gate-added invocations with --parent
- Relates to b36c-3e66 (worktree-isolation guard in 44 implementer agents) — canonical dispatch prompt slot order: SUB_AGENT_ROOT guard first, then parent ID injection
## Approach

Mirror the bug-template enforcement pattern (ticket-create.sh lines 279-328) for parent_id on story/task, but with the load-bearing enforcement moved from runtime stderr-capture (per bot-psychologist behavioral review: unreliable at 13 mixed-context sites) to a static CI grep test that asserts every ticket create story|task invocation in SKILL.md and dispatch prompts includes an inline --parent= argument. The CLI stderr ERROR is retained as a backstop signal with skill-side capture+remediate applied only at orchestrator-context shell sites where bash stderr capture is reliable. orphan-cleanup.sh implements a 5-step retro pipeline (explicit-ID reparent / bug retype / test-fixture close / duplicate close / opus batch-of-10) over all live orphans at execution time using the ticket reparent primitive from 5efb-06ea, with flock concurrency guard, capability probe for 5efb-06ea, re-query between steps, and dso-cleanup-pending tagging of residuals for handoff to 7271-e463.
## Scenario Analysis
- Concurrent orphan-cleanup.sh runs produce duplicate reparent operations (high, runtime) — addressed by flock guard
- Opus batch dispatched against stale orphan snapshot (high, runtime) — addressed by re-query before each step
- stderr capture silently drops signal on non-zero sub-process exit (high, runtime) — backstop scope limited to orchestrator shell sites
- 5efb-06ea reparent primitive not merged when orphan-cleanup.sh executes (critical, deployment) — capability probe at startup
- Tracker directory not checked out in working tree (high, deployment) — fallback to .dso/link-failures.log
- standalone tag undefined (medium, configuration) — defined in Context and pipeline skips
- Exponential backoff defaults undocumented (medium, configuration) — config keys with explicit defaults
- Assumption: shell context applies to all 13 sites (critical, assumption) — addressed by R2 redesign: primary enforcement is structural literal injection
- Assumption: PARENT_TICKET_ID always known at sub-agent dispatch time (high, assumption) — addressed by R5 (literal parent ID injection by orchestrator before dispatch)
- Assumption: all 113 orphans have recoverable parent mappings (high, assumption) — addressed by RESIDUAL reporting and dso-cleanup-pending handoff
- Assumption: validate-issues.sh orphan definition matches ticket-create.sh enforcement (medium, assumption) — preplanning task to verify alignment of the two definitions
## Closure Checks

- orphan-cleanup.sh runs the 5-step pipeline over all live orphans at execution time and exits 0 with a summary report counting each remediation type: (1) explicit-ID reparent using ticket reparent from 5efb-06ea, (2) bug retype via ticket edit --ticket_type, (3) test-fixture close, (4) duplicate-of-non-orphan close, (5) opus sub-agent batch-of-10 recommendation+execution. The script (a) acquires an exclusive flock on a tracker-side orphan-cleanup.lock to prevent concurrent invocations; (b) probes for the ticket reparent subcommand at startup and exits with a clear error if 5efb-06ea is not yet merged; (c) re-queries the live orphan list before each step rather than using the snapshot from step 1; (d) skips tickets tagged defer, dso-cleanup-pending, or standalone; (e) opus residuals (no confident parent) are tagged dso-cleanup-pending for handoff to 7271-e463 and reported under "RESIDUAL" in the summary rather than auto-closed.

- **SC (self-use, Probe-1 remediation, architecture-vs-evidence audit 2026-05-16):** During the 7510 sprint, the new CI grep test (scanning `plugins/dso/skills/` and `plugins/dso/agents/` for ticket-create-without-`--parent`) is active and fires on at least one sprint PR (synthetic or organic). Verification (in-session, at sprint Phase I): `gh run list --workflow=ci.yml --branch=<sprint-branch> --json conclusion,jobs | jq '.[].jobs[] | select(.name | test("orphan|parent"))'` shows the job ran; the three pre-existing missing-parent sites enumerated in the primary SC (interface-contracts:82-87, tickets-health:113/116, ui-designer-dispatch-protocol:298) are confirmed remediated by `grep -nE 'ticket create story|ticket create task' <those files> | grep -v -- '--parent='` returning 0 results.

DIG-4394.summary: DSO orphan story/task prevention: literal --parent injection + CI structural enforcement + stderr backstop + retro cleanup

content.text: ## Context

Pre-commit hooks today are syntactic only (paths, schemas, ticket IDs, executable bits). Several recurring failure classes have no static-detection gate and recur across the codebase weeks/months apart in different files, indicating a missing systematic check rather than per-script oversights. The release gate (`scripts/release.sh` precondition #8 → `validate.sh --ci`) catches these post-merge; the pre-commit stack admits them.

This epic adds four new pre-commit hooks that statically scan for known antipattern classes, each with a baseline-file mechanism so existing violations do not block rollout (descriptive-first ratchet, modeled after the 26-file SIGPIPE remediation series).
See `docs/observed-failure-patterns-4-26.md`, `docs/process-gaps-4-26.md`, and `docs/new-epics-4-26.md` for the full review and mitigation provenance.
## Cited evidence
**Pattern 1 — Environment hermeticity violations (~25% of recent fixes):**
- `fe45-0b58` (commit `dcbe98f3ef`): `skip-review-check.sh` references `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` under `set -u` → unbound variable → 27/56 tests fail in clean env
- `09d8-11f0`, `a190-d780` (commit `e913a71d5a`): `pre-commit-format-fix.sh` same pattern — 5/11 tests fail; identical root cause to `fe45-0b58` two months earlier
- `82ad-7bb3` (commit `f5a055d1fa`): `bash-runner.sh` does not export `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` before sourcing suite-engine
- `97a7-4504` (commit `495c8c4b4f`): `bash-runner.sh` fallback path needed annotation under plugin-self-ref check
- `4191-9096`, `0a47-9631` (commits `2261fcc83b`, `0968b46917`): `declare -A` (associative array) in scripts that must run on bash 3.2 (macOS default)
- `a40e-ab52` (in flight): `check-tickets-boundary.sh` resolves `BASH_SOURCE` via pre-commit's symlinked temp path → silent docs/ exclusion failure
**Pattern 4 — `set -o pipefail` + SIGPIPE on `… | grep -q` (~8%, Linux-strict):**
- `e241-41b2`: 50+ instances replaced with here-strings (`grep -q "$y" <<< "$x"`) across 26 files in commits `b9358f95eb` + `0113ab66d9`
- `999e-cf69`: a 27th instance later discovered in `ticket-push-rebase-conflict` after the 26-file sweep

- Current state: a fresh `grep -r "echo .* | grep -q" plugins/dso/ --include="*.sh" -l | wc -l` returns **42 files** still containing the antipattern, including `pre-commit-review-gate.sh:259` (a hook script — production code path)
**Pattern 7 — Spec / documentation gaps:**
- `a190-d780`: `commands.test_dirs` config key undocumented; CI's `test-config-keys-documented.sh` caught this post-merge
**Pattern 3 — Identical-root-cause regressions (~10%, cross-cuts Pattern 1):**

- The CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT chain `09d8-11f0` → `fe45-0b58` → `82ad-7bb3` → `97a7-4504` is at least four separate tickets with identical mechanical fixes; each was treated as a single-file fix and excluded from prior-art search by `prior-art-search.md:79-88` ("Routine exclusions: single-file logic fixes...")
**Gap evidence:**
- G1 (no hermeticity gate): all 18 hooks in `.pre-commit-config.yaml` are syntactic; `check-portability.sh` flags only `/Users/`, `/home/` hardcoded paths
- G6 (prior-art search excludes single-file fixes): verified at `prior-art-search.md:79-88`
- G11 (config keys decoupled from docs): no hook in `.pre-commit-config.yaml` cross-references config keys against `CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md`
- G12 (SIGPIPE has no static-detection gate): shellcheck does not flag this pattern; 42 files currently in violation
## Mitigations included

- **G1-M1** — `check-hermeticity.sh` pre-commit hook scanning staged `.sh` files for: (a) unguarded `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` references when `set -u` is active; (b) `declare -A` in scripts under directories the platform matrix targets (`plugins/dso/scripts/`, `plugins/dso/hooks/`, `.claude/scripts/`); (c) `BASH_SOURCE` resolution that does not flow through `readlink -f` or equivalent

- **G6-M2** — `check-known-antipatterns.sh` reading regex/AST queries from `plugins/dso/config/known-antipatterns.yaml`; append-only registry populated over time as new antipatterns are discovered (E receives them from fix-bug)
- **G11-M1** — `check-config-key-docs.sh` cross-referencing `dso-config.conf` keys against `CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md` (parses both, fails on missing entries)
- **G12-M1** — `check-pipefail-grep.sh` flagging `echo … | grep -q` and `printf … | grep -q` under scripts with `set -o pipefail` or `set -euo pipefail`; ships with baseline of existing 42 instances
## Proposed success criteria
1. Four new pre-commit hooks ship in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, ordered between `shellcheck` and `pre-commit-review-gate`
2. Each hook supports a baseline file mechanism so existing violations do not block rollout; new violations are blocked
3. Hooks emit per-file diagnostics with the exact remediation string and a citation back to the originating ticket (`e241-41b2`, `a190-d780`, etc.)
4. `plugins/dso/config/known-antipatterns.yaml` is created, append-only, and documented in `CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md`
5. Suppression annotations follow the precedent of existing hooks (`# bash4-only:`, `# antipattern-ok: <reason>`); each annotation requires a justification token

6. Test coverage: each hook has a fixture-based test asserting (a) the antipattern is detected on staged content, (b) baselined existing violations do not fire, (c) new instances of the antipattern are blocked
## Coordination notes
- Coexists with `cf7b-86a9` (which adds shellcheck/ruff parity) — different layer, different antipattern class
- Sets up the registry that **New Epic E** (fix-bug recurrence) populates over time
- Reviewer rubric items in **New Epic B** (G1-M2, G11-M3, G12-M2) are the human-loop counterpart to these mechanical hooks
## References
- `docs/observed-failure-patterns-4-26.md` Patterns 1, 3, 4, 7
- `docs/process-gaps-4-26.md` G1, G6, G11, G12
- `docs/proposed-mitigations-4-26.md` G1-M1, G6-M2, G11-M1, G12-M1
- `docs/new-epics-4-26.md` § New Epic A

content.text: ## Testing Mode GREEN ## Story 0263-62ba — Migrate 4 consumers to PRECONDITIONS, add compaction on epic-closure with ordering contract ## Objective Write a fault-injection test harness that verifies the retry-once contract: when `_read_latest_preconditions` encounters a transient ENOENT (file disappears during compaction atomic rename), it retries once and succeeds on the second attempt. Also assert that a second failure causes a clean exit 1 with a diagnostic message (no silent swallowing). ## Test File to Create `tests/integration/test-preconditions-fault-injection.sh` (new) ## .test-index entries required - `plugins/dso/scripts/ticket-lib.sh: tests/integration/test-preconditions-fault-injection.sh [test_retry_once_succeeds_on_second_attempt]` - `plugins/dso/scripts/ticket-lib.sh: tests/integration/test-preconditions-fault-injection.sh [test_retry_once_fails_with_diagnostic_on_persistent_miss]` ## Test Approach (Given/When/Then) **test_retry_once_succeeds_on_second_attempt:** - Given: a wrapper script that intercepts the first file-read call and removes the PRECONDITIONS file; then re-creates it before the retry interval elapses - When: `_read_latest_preconditions <ticket_dir>` is called via the wrapper - Then: exits 0; returns valid JSON payload from the second attempt; no partial data **test_retry_once_fails_with_diagnostic_on_persistent_miss:** - Given: a temp ticket dir that appears to have a PRECONDITIONS file (directory listing shows it) but the file is always missing when read (simulated via a named pipe or immediate removal) - When: `_read_latest_preconditions <ticket_dir>` is called - Then: exits 1; stderr contains a diagnostic message (not silent failure); does not hang indefinitely ## Implementation Note for Fault Injection The test harness can simulate transient ENOENT by: 1. Creating the ticket dir with valid events 2. Using a bash function override (`_read_latest_preconditions`) to stub the first call to return ENOENT then the real function on second call OR 3. Using a subshell with file manipulation timed to the 50ms sleep window ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] `tests/integration/test-preconditions-fault-injection.sh` exists and is executable   Verify: test -x tests/integration/test-preconditions-fault-injection.sh - [ ] Both test functions present   Verify: grep -c "^test_retry_once" tests/integration/test-preconditions-fault-injection.sh | awk '{exit ($1 < 2)}' - [ ] Both tests pass   Verify: bash tests/integration/test-preconditions-fault-injection.sh - [ ] .test-index updated with both entries   Verify: grep -c "test-preconditions-fault-injection.sh" $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/.test-index | awk '{exit ($1 < 2)}' ## Retry Budget MAX_ATTEMPTS: 3 (sonnet model) On 3 consecutive sonnet failures: escalate to opus with full diagnostic context (all 3 failure messages) On 3 consecutive opus failures (6 total): escalate to user with full failure history If MAX_AGENTS: 0 at sonnet→opus escalation time: skip opus step, escalate to user immediately

DIG-4402.summary: As a detector author, I have a published namespaced-array schema contract

content.text: ## Context

The ticket CLI adds 300–500ms of per-call overhead that is paid by every interactive DSO skill invocation. A typical /dso:sprint, /dso:brainstorm, or /dso:preplanning turn makes 5–40 ticket CLI calls — producing 2–20 seconds of avoidable latency per orchestrator turn on top of the actual Claude processing time. The overhead is structural: a 3-process bash chain (shim → dispatcher → subcommand), redundant `git rev-parse` calls, two Python processes for path canonicalization and sync-marker hashing in `_ensure_initialized`, a fresh `python3` import of the `ticket_reducer` package on every read, and three more Python processes inside `write_commit_event` for every write. None of this is serving the operation; it's all startup cost. Every interactive practitioner using DSO pays this latency. The same overhead also slows the test suite (~60 ticket-calling test files), but the primary value is interactive workflow latency.
## Success Criteria

1. Write-path operations (ticket create, link, transition, comment, tag, untag, edit) complete in <0.05s per call, measured wall-clock from a fresh Bash invocation using hyperfine or equivalent over 10 warm runs.

2. Read-path operations (ticket show, list) complete in <0.15s per call under the same measurement conditions (the ~80ms reducer Python import is the remaining floor; accepted to rule out a persistent helper).
3. The CLI dispatcher (plugins/dso/scripts/ticket) sources the library and delegates all covered operations to library functions — no logic duplication between dispatcher path and sourced path.

4. Sourcing the library is side-effect-free to the caller's shell: no `set -euo pipefail` propagation, no `exit` termination, no `trap EXIT` leakage, no mutation of GIT_DIR / GIT_INDEX_FILE / GIT_WORK_TREE / GIT_COMMON_DIR env vars.

5. Flock contract preserved verbatim per plugins/dso/docs/contracts/ticket-flock-contract.md: single global per-worktree lock at `.tickets-tracker/.ticket-write.lock`, LOCK_EX semantics, 30s timeout × 2 retries. Concurrent-write safety validated by the existing concurrency test suite.

6. All existing ticket-CLI test assertions (including tests/scripts/test-ticket-subprocess-count.sh) pass unmodified. A new regression test suite measures per-call latency for each covered operation and fails if SC1/SC2 regress by >10%.

7. A representative /dso:sprint workflow trace — 20–40 ticket CLI calls with a ~50% read/write mix matching typical sprint-turn usage — demonstrates ≥60% aggregate ticket-CLI wall-clock reduction compared to the current dispatcher, measured end-to-end in a single orchestrator turn. The benchmark script is checked in, runnable via one command, and before/after results are captured in the closing comment.

8. The library operates correctly across platforms — Linux (bash ≥4), macOS (bash ≥3.2, default install), and Alpine/BusyBox CI containers — with documented fallbacks when coreutils features differ; tickets containing shell-special characters (quotes, backslashes, newlines, unicode) round-trip correctly through all write and read operations; and a `DSO_TICKET_LEGACY=1` env flag reverts to the pre-refactor Python-backed path, available for at least the first release cycle after rollout.
## Dependencies
None.
## Approach

A sourceable ticket-lib-api.sh (extending the existing ticket-lib.sh rather than creating a parallel file) exposes each covered operation as a bash function. The CLI dispatcher becomes a thin wrapper that sources the library and dispatches to the appropriate function based on argv. `_ensure_initialized`'s two Python processes are replaced with bash-native equivalents (realpath + sha1sum + mtime). `write_commit_event`'s three Python processes are replaced with `flock(1)` + `printf`-based JSON generation (escape-safe) + direct `git commit`. Read operations reduce from 2–4 `python3` invocations per call to exactly one (invoking `ticket_reducer` once, preserving its `.cache.json`). Subshell isolation `( ... )` is used for any function body that needs `set -e` / `exit` / `trap EXIT` locally without leaking to the caller's shell.
## Scenario Analysis
Runtime:
- printf-JSON escaping failures on ticket content containing quotes, backslashes, or control characters (high)
- sha1sum + file-mtime sync marker drift from Python canonicalization under clock skew or same-second writes (high)
- Sourcing ticket-lib-api.sh pollutes caller's function namespace and can shadow existing functions (medium)
- Subshell isolation for `set -e` / `trap EXIT` loses `$?` propagation and breaks error-reporting (high)
- flock(1) behavior differs between util-linux flock and macOS/BSD, breaking 30s × 2 retry contract (critical)
- realpath not available or behaves differently across platforms for path canonicalization (high)
- Read-path reducer cache (.cache.json) race condition under concurrent reads during a write (medium)
Deployment:
- First-install worktree with no existing `.tickets-tracker/.ticket-write.lock` causes flock to fail (medium)
- Existing subcommand scripts sourcing ticket-lib.sh break when ticket-lib.sh is extended with functions using different var-naming conventions (medium)
- CI containers lacking coreutils (realpath, sha1sum, flock) fail at library load (high)
Configuration:
- Bash version drift — associative arrays and `printf %q` behavior differ between bash 3.2 (macOS default) and bash 5.x (high)
- Sourcing library in scripts that already have `set -euo pipefail` inherits the library's unset-variable assumptions (high)
- Concurrent sprint sub-agents sharing a worktree hit the single global lock, serializing writes and reintroducing latency (medium)
- No opt-out flag for users who need the Python-backed path during debugging (medium — addressed by SC8's DSO_TICKET_LEGACY flag)
## Cross-Epic Interactions
- Resource: write_commit_event event JSON schema
Interaction: consumed by 170b-2ac9 (commit trailers), 736d-b957 (stage-boundary preconditions), 86c8-2d40 (file-impact event field)
Gate: bash-rehomed write_commit_event MUST emit events in the existing JSON schema; schema-coupled consumers must continue to read correctly
- Resource: ticket CLI dispatcher extensibility point
Interaction: 2c28-e5b9 (next-batch, list-descendants, list-epics, exists) and 4931-f639 (validate, classify, purge-bridge) add new subcommands; e1b2-2653 refactors boundary-enforcement callers
Gate: sourceable library design MUST expose a conventional extension pattern so downstream epics can add new ops as bash functions with minimal LOC per function
- Resource: ticket show/list output format
Interaction: d94f-b734 (TOON format optimization) wraps library output
Gate: library read functions MUST produce a stable, documented output shape that output-formatting epics can wrap without monkey-patching
- Resource: ticket CLI dispatcher + ticket-lib.sh (merge ordering)
Interaction: 6f7a-4ba6 (ticket delete subcommand) modifies the same files
Gate: coordinate merge order — whichever lands second rebases onto the other's final library structure
## Research Findings
### Performance: Python interpreter cold start
- Trigger condition: Performance or scalability
- Source URLs: https://dev.to/methane/how-to-speed-up-python-application-startup-time-nkf ; https://byteiota.com/python-lazy-imports-speed-up-startup-with-pep-810/

- Key insight: Python interpreter cold-start for small packages is ~80ms. Lazy-import refactoring of `ticket_reducer` (PEP 810 in Python 3.14, expected 2026) is a potential follow-on optimization but out of scope for this epic. The <0.15s read target accounts for this floor.
### Bash sourceable library side-effect isolation
- Trigger condition: Agent-judgment (relevant to SC4)
- Source URLs: http://redsymbol.net/articles/unofficial-bash-strict-mode/ ; https://olivergondza.github.io/2019/10/01/bash-strict-mode.html

- Key insight: Sourced scripts inherit their parent's `set -e/u/pipefail` and trap state. The existing ticket-lib.sh correctly avoids `set -euo pipefail` and uses `local` throughout — validated practice for sourceable libraries. Subshell isolation `( ... )` is the standard mechanism for local use of set-e/trap without leakage.
### Planning Intelligence Log
- Web research (Step 2.6): triggered
- Bright-line conditions that fired: performance or scalability
- Scenario analysis (Step 2.75): triggered
- Scenarios surviving blue team filter: 14
- Practitioner-requested additional cycles: none
- Follow-on scrutiny (Step 0): not triggered
- Feasibility resolution (Step 2.5): not triggered
- LLM-instruction signal (Step 5): not triggered
- Scale context (Step 0): small scale — dev-time CLI latency; ~60 ticket-calling test files; primary value is workflow latency 2–20s per orchestrator turn

- Cross-epic scan (Step 2.25): 5 batches over 90 candidate epics; 1 conflict + 1 ambiguity signal were overridden as consideration-tier by practitioner judgment (bug 74ab-fa76 filed on classifier over-reach); 8 consideration signals retained as Cross-Epic Interactions entries

content.text: ## Context

When document-creation stories are created (e.g., 'Update project docs', 'Add CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md entry'), there is currently no explicit signal for whether the change warrants an ADR (Architecture Decision Record). This leads to either: (a) ADRs silently skipped for decisions that deserve documentation, or (b) ADR bloat from decisions too minor to record.
## Goal
Establish clear criteria for when ADR creation should be triggered alongside a document-creation story. This should be resolved via brainstorm before implementation.
## Placeholder Notes
- Candidate trigger signals: new config key introduced, behavior change with observable side effects, agent routing change, new skill or phase added
- Anti-triggers (no ADR needed): cosmetic rewording, adding examples to existing docs, formatting fixes
- Should integrate into preplanning or sprint doc-story dispatch so the ADR trigger is automatic, not manual
## Success Criteria (to be refined in brainstorm)
- Criteria exist that determine when an ADR is required vs optional vs not needed for any document-creation story
- The criteria are enforced or at minimum surfaced as a checklist item during preplanning or sprint doc-story dispatch
- Document-creation stories that trigger ADR criteria produce a linked ADR ticket as a dependency

content.text: ## Description

**What**: Add java-maven (pom.xml at root) and java-gradle (build.gradle at root) as distinct stack values to detect-stack.sh. Document the equivalence contract (scripts that treat java-maven and java-gradle as equivalent vs. differently). Update CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md to include both values in the accepted values list.

**Why**: Java projects currently fall through to 'unknown' stack detection, receiving no test/lint/format gates and no routing. This story establishes the detection foundation that all subsequent Java stories depend on.
**Scope**:

- IN: detect-stack.sh: add java-maven detection (pom.xml at root → 'java-maven'), java-gradle detection (build.gradle at root → 'java-gradle'); java-maven takes priority when both pom.xml and build.gradle present; Java detection ordered below Python/Rust/Go/Node/Ruby (not above); CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md: add java-maven and java-gradle to the stack accepted values list; equivalence contract documented in a comment block or adjacent doc: scripts treating both as equivalent (gate-2b, gate-2d, project-detect) vs. differently (commands.* writes, wrapper detection)
- OUT: onboarding commands.* defaults (Story F2), gate extensions (Story F3), project-detect.sh (Story F4), stretch SCs (Stories F5, F6)
## Done Definitions
- When this story is complete, detect-stack.sh returns 'java-maven' on a project with pom.xml at the repo root and no build.gradle
← Satisfies: "detect-stack.sh adds java-maven (pom.xml at root)"
- When this story is complete, detect-stack.sh returns 'java-gradle' on a project with build.gradle at the repo root and no pom.xml
← Satisfies: "detect-stack.sh adds java-gradle (build.gradle at root)"
- When this story is complete, detect-stack.sh returns 'java-maven' on a project with BOTH pom.xml and build.gradle (java-maven takes priority)
← Satisfies: "java-maven takes priority when both present"
- When this story is complete, detect-stack.sh returns the expected non-Java stack for Python/Ruby/Node projects (regression test — Java detection does not shadow existing stacks)
← Satisfies: "Java detection below Python/Rust/Go/Node/Ruby"
- When this story is complete, CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md lists both java-maven and java-gradle in the stack accepted values section
← Satisfies: "CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md stack accepted values list updated to include both"

- When this story is complete, the equivalence contract is documented: gate-2b, gate-2d, project-detect treat java-maven and java-gradle as equivalent; commands.* writes and wrapper detection treat them differently
← Satisfies: "scripts treating both as equivalent vs. differently documented via equivalence contract"
- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all detection cases (pom.xml only, build.gradle only, both present, Python/Ruby/Node regression)
## Considerations
- [Reliability] Root-only detection: only detect pom.xml/build.gradle at the repository root (not in subdirectories) — consistent with how Python/Ruby/Node detection works in detect-stack.sh

- [Maintainability] The equivalence contract must be machine-readable enough for future stories (F3, F4) to reference — consider a comment block in detect-stack.sh or a companion .md file in plugins/dso/docs
## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.

content.text: As an implementation-plan agent, I can invoke ref-library-loader.sh to annotate generated tasks with up to 6 relevant reference citations from a merged corpus+URL reference set.
Done definitions:
- ref-library-loader.sh calls `dso ref-query --top-n=8` with 30s subprocess timeout and explicit PID tracking (no zombie processes on timeout)

- Calls confluence-fetch.sh per URL reference; caps post-tag-filter set at 12 with consistent budget accounting (failed fetches excluded; retry quota re-filled from next candidate with fixed-point condition: retry until 12 tag-passing references OR exhausted candidate pool OR max-3 retry rounds)

- Merges both sets with local-first precedence + slot-reallocation rule: URL slots expand to fill unused corpus budget ONLY when corpus returns fewer than 8 AND merged-set cap of 20 has remaining capacity
- LLM relevance judgment per-entry (not batched); UTF-8-safe 200-char truncation at Unicode code point boundary (not grapheme cluster, not byte); concurrent-invocation cap of 3
- Selects top 6 entries by relevance score for citation annotation (MAX_CITATIONS_PER_TASK=6)
- Emits citations in URL-sourced OR corpus-sourced format based on entry source
- Unit tests pass
Considerations:
- [Reliability] PID tracking on ref-query child — ensure kill on timeout, no zombies accumulating over N tasks
- [Performance] Concurrent-invocation cap of 3 balances throughput and rate limits
- [Security] No shell injection in task title/description passed to ref-query subprocess or tag filter
- [Testing] Mock LLM client for per-entry judgment
- [Correctness] UTF-8 truncation operates on Unicode code points; never splits multi-byte UTF-8 sequences; fixture includes boundary cases at code-point-N where code point N+1 is multi-byte
- [Reliability] Budget re-fill fixed-point condition prevents infinite retry loop when most candidate URLs fail the tag filter

content.text: ## Description

**What**: Extend `check_usage.py` to expose per-session token delta (not just bucket percentages). Planning skills (brainstorm, preplanning, implementation-plan) call this at their own start and end to compute tokens_estimated and write it to the parent epic/story.

**Why**: Planning-phase tokens are the "overhead" of the sprint — separating them from execution tokens lets users see planning-cost-vs-execution-cost ratio. Currently `check_usage.py` returns only rolled-up 5hr/7day percentages; it needs a session-delta mode.
**Scope**:
- IN: Add a `--session-delta` mode to `check_usage.py` that returns tokens used by the current session only.
- IN: Brainstorm, preplanning, implementation-plan invoke it at skill entry and exit to compute their own token spend.
- IN: Write the delta to the parent epic/story via `ticket-edit.sh --tokens_estimated=` (additive on existing value).
- OUT: Retroactive estimation.
- OUT: Measurement of execution tokens — separate story.
## Done Definitions
- When this story is complete, running `/dso:brainstorm` on an epic increments the epic ticket tokens_estimated by the skill session token delta.
← Satisfies: "Estimate planning token use on the parent ticket"
- When this story is complete, the same behavior applies for `/dso:preplanning` and `/dso:implementation-plan`.
← Satisfies: "Estimate planning token use on the parent ticket"
- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic.
## Considerations
- [Reliability] If `check_usage.py` session-delta is unavailable (e.g., offline), skip the write silently rather than blocking skill execution.
- [Maintainability] The planning-skill integration is a single source line per skill — handle it in a shared helper so the pattern is DRY.

content.text: ## Context

ADR 0013 (docs/adr/0013-verifier-severity-authority.md) defines a named exception to CLAUDE.md Rule 11 for code-reviewer-verifier. Prong 2 of the exception authorizes ruling enum: only downgrade-to-minor and drop.

The new code-reviewer-arbiter (epic b575-ac1c-f720-4839, story 0652-809a-d1fc-4d36) also emits DROP as a cycle-end ruling. Both the verifier and the arbiter are consumed by plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/runner.py.
## Analysis (from 16f1 task review)
- BLOCK ruling: merge gate only, does NOT modify any finding's severity field. Rule 11 not triggered. No conflict.
- DEFER ruling: continuation signal, does NOT modify any finding's severity field. Rule 11 not triggered. No conflict.

- DROP ruling: removes a finding from consideration. ADR 0013 prong 2 explicitly names drop as an authorized ruling — but only for code-reviewer-verifier. The arbiter's DROP is structurally identical in effect. If consumed by runner.py without explicit ADR coverage, the arbiter's DROP is technically outside the exception scope defined in ADR 0013.
## Required Amendment
Add code-reviewer-arbiter as a second authorized DROP authority in ADR 0013, either:
(a) Extend prong 1 (sub-agent identity) to list both code-reviewer-verifier and code-reviewer-arbiter as authorized agents for their respective ruling enums, OR

(b) Add a separate section covering code-reviewer-arbiter with its own prongs (identity, ruling enum: BLOCK/DEFER/DROP, dispatch surface: runner.py at cycle-end, feature-flag: review.verifier_enabled or new flag)
## Not In Scope
Resolving the amendment is not in story 0652 scope. This ticket tracks the identification and filing of the conflict so a future sprint can amend ADR 0013.

content.text: ## Context

Test creation calibration today has no signal for "did we add tests for new intent items?" Test-writing sub-agents can produce many tests that pass review but do not cover newly-introduced SC/DoD/AC entries — and the failure is invisible until production. Today there is no per-PR or per-epic metric that distinguishes "suite grew because behavior was added" from "suite grew due to test inflation." Users affected: DSO maintainer, sprint orchestrators, test-writing sub-agents, code-reviewer-test-quality, completion-verifier, and downstream calibration consumers (411b-a047 mutation infrastructure once brainstormed, 69e8-af39 feedback loop). After this epic ships, when a sprint agent closes a story that has an SC with no test_artifact registered in the manifest, the completion-verifier emits a non-empty "Intent Allocation Findings" section naming the uncovered SC — where today closure is silent.

This epic delivers the first version of suite-growth metrics: (a) manifest-claim breadth + (a+) header-vs-source import check, both implemented as deterministic scripts. Stronger signals (intent-anchored line coverage, manifest-claim depth) are deferred to fb3e-b01b at P4 until the simpler signals' real-world catch rate is known.
## Success Criteria

SC1: plugins/dso/docs/contracts/intent-coverage-findings.md published with a jsonschema. Seven finding types: intent_with_no_test, test_artifact_missing_on_disk, test_artifact_fails, header_source_mismatch, dynamic_import_inconclusive (fail-open, warn), source_files_unresolved (warn; both manifest entry's source_files field AND parent ticket file_impact absent/empty), file_impact_likely_stale (warn; source_files resolved from file_impact but referenced files don't exist on disk). Severities: warn (default), block (reserved for intent_with_no_test at closure-time only). contract_version=1. Each consumer validates incoming findings JSON against the published jsonschema before processing.

SC2: plugins/dso/scripts/intent-coverage-check.sh implements (a) — manifest-claim breadth. Reads the 94ed manifest via intent-allocation-read.sh. For each end-state intent_id: (i) entry presence in the merged manifest; (ii) test_artifact.path realpath() normalization THEN file existence on disk; (iii) test pass/fail. Pre-commit invocation runs ONLY steps (i)+(ii) — fast checks. Test-pass validation step (iii) runs in CI workflow OR at closure-time on ticket-transition — NOT on every commit, eliminating pre-commit latency. Findings written to file via `--output-file` flag (ARG_MAX-safe; not passed as command-line argument or env var). Exit codes: 0 = no findings; 1 = warn-only; 2 = at least one block-mode finding.

SC3: plugins/dso/scripts/intent-header-source-check.sh implements (a+) — header-vs-source import check. ONLY applies to test files that have an intent-claim header per d566-afa6 Rule 6; files without a header are skipped (header presence is d566's reviewer concern, not 7f42's). For each test file with a header: (i) extract intent_id; (ii) resolve source_files via manifest entry's source_files field if present → else parent ticket's file_impact array → else emit source_files_unresolved (warn, fail-open; skip check for that intent); when file_impact is used, additionally check disk presence of each referenced file and emit file_impact_likely_stale (warn) for missing entries; (iii) parse the test file with sg (ast-grep); when sg unavailable OR no parser for the test language, emit dynamic_import_inconclusive (warn, fail-open) — NO grep fallback (grep fallback produces false positives); (iv) emit header_source_mismatch when test file contains no reference to any source_files entry. Dynamic-import patterns detected for fail-open: Python importlib.import_module with variable arg; JavaScript eval/Function/dynamic require with computed string; Ruby send/public_send. Findings written via `--output-file` (ARG_MAX-safe).
SC4: Multi-surface consumption — three consumers, one published contract:

- (a) plugins/dso/hooks/pre-commit-intent-coverage-gate.sh invokes only the FAST checks (file existence + header parsing). NO test-runner invocation in pre-commit. Block-mode reserved for intent_with_no_test at closure-time only, detected via ticket-transition hook.

- (b) 94ed-f55c's manifest-aware default validator (already registered with a03c-d55e's pluggable end-state-item-validator hook) ingests the findings JSON. ALL seven finding types (intent_with_no_test, test_artifact_missing_on_disk, test_artifact_fails, header_source_mismatch, dynamic_import_inconclusive, source_files_unresolved, file_impact_likely_stale) are explicitly enumerated as a contract requirement for 94ed's validator output mapping — the validator must register each type for rendering in the completion-verifier "Intent Allocation Findings" section.

- (c) .github/workflows/intent-coverage.yml invokes both scripts AND the (a)-step-iii test-pass validation step at CI time. Posts findings as PR comment via upsert-by-marker pattern: finds prior bot comment by the stable marker `COVERAGE_FINDINGS_<epic-id>` and edits it in place; if absent, posts new. One comment per PR, never a thread. Fallback when comment-write is unavailable (e.g., fork PRs with read-only GITHUB_TOKEN): write findings to the GHA job summary so the signal is not silently dropped.
SC5: Multi-language synthetic end-to-end test covering nine fixture scenarios:
- (a) HAPPY PATH: Python + bash test fixtures with valid intent-claim headers and manifest entries pointing at them. Both scripts return zero findings.

- (b) INTENT_WITH_NO_TEST: fixture epic with 2 SCs, only one has a manifest entry. intent-coverage-check.sh surfaces intent_with_no_test for the uncovered SC. completion-verifier dispatch produces a non-empty "Intent Allocation Findings" section naming it.

- (c) HEADER_SOURCE_MISMATCH: fixture Python test + fixture bash test both with valid intent-claim headers but no source-file symbol references. intent-header-source-check.sh surfaces header_source_mismatch for each.

- (d) SOURCE_FILES_UNRESOLVED: intent_id whose manifest entry has no source_files field AND whose parent ticket file_impact is empty. intent-header-source-check.sh surfaces source_files_unresolved (warn, fail-open) and skips the (a+) check for that intent.

- (e) FILE_IMPACT_LIKELY_STALE: parent ticket file_impact references a path that doesn't exist on disk. intent-header-source-check.sh surfaces file_impact_likely_stale (warn) but still attempts source-symbol matching against the surviving file_impact entries.
- (f) DEFERRED_TEST OVERRIDE: manifest entry with deferred_test: true set. Closure attempt on the parent ticket does NOT block on intent_with_no_test for that intent.

- (g) MISSING_SG: simulate sg absence on the runtime PATH. intent-header-source-check.sh emits dynamic_import_inconclusive (warn) for all test files; NO grep fallback is executed; pre-commit does NOT block.

- (h) BACKWARD_COMPAT_94ED_LEGACY: manifest entry without source_files field AND without deferred_test field (pre-extension legacy schema). Scripts handle gracefully: source_files resolution falls back to parent ticket file_impact; absent deferred_test treated as false. Verifies the additive 94ed schema extension preserves backward compatibility for existing consumers.

SC6: Dynamic-import fail-open verification per language. Python importlib.import_module with variable arg; JavaScript eval/Function/dynamic require with computed string; Ruby send/public_send. Each emits dynamic_import_inconclusive (warn); pre-commit does NOT block; completion-verifier surfaces as informational finding (not blocking closure).
## Approach
Four sequential phases, each independently mergeable:
- Phase 1: SC1 (findings jsonschema contract) + SC2 (intent-coverage-check.sh; manifest-claim breadth check).
- Phase 2: SC3 (intent-header-source-check.sh; header-vs-source via sg) + SC6 (dynamic-import fail-open pattern detection per language).
- Phase 3: SC4 (multi-surface wiring — fast-only pre-commit hook, 94ed validator finding-type mapping, CI workflow upsert-by-marker with GHA-summary fallback).
- Phase 4: SC5 (nine-scenario multi-language synthetic end-to-end test).

7f42's sg usage is internal to intent-header-source-check.sh; this epic does not introduce a shared AST contract. If a Polyglot Test Gate epic later requires polyglot AST traversal, it will own that capability independently. The two epics' sg invocations are not coupled.
## Scenario Analysis (Blue Team surviving)

- Stale file_impact arrays produce false-positive header_source_mismatch (high/correctness): partially mitigated by SC1's new file_impact_likely_stale finding type — staleness is surfaced as warn rather than masquerading as a genuine mismatch.

- Tautological import satisfies (a+) symbol-reference check despite zero behavioral catch power (high/correctness): accepted as known by-design residual; reserved for 411b-a047's mutation-kill verification.
- ARG_MAX exceeded for large epics' findings JSON (high/runtime): mitigated by SC2/SC3's --output-file flag — findings written to disk, not passed via shell arg or env var.

- CI findings comment on fork PRs triggers no-permission error (low/deployment): mitigated by SC4(c)'s GHA-summary fallback — signal survives even when comment-write is unavailable; documented as a known limitation pending fork-PR security work.
## Out of Scope

- Intent-anchored line coverage and manifest-claim depth metrics: deferred to fb3e-b01b at P4. Stronger signals require polyglot per-test line-coverage infrastructure (coverage.py + bashcov + istanbul/nyc) and per-test attribution storage; the ROI on those vs 411b-a047's mutation-kill is poor.
- Behavioral adequacy of imports: a test that imports a source module but doesn't actually exercise the SC behavior satisfies (a+). Reserved for 411b-a047's mutation-kill verification.
- Polyglot Test Gate AST traversal patterns: 7f42 does not introduce a shared sg invocation contract. Polyglot Test Gate (if pursued) owns its own AST traversal.
- Fork-PR-friendly findings posting: deferred to CI security work; SC4(c)'s GHA-summary fallback is the interim signal.
## Operational Constraints (Architecture-vs-Evidence Audit Remediation, 2026-05-16)
### State Lifecycle Owner Block (Probe-3 remediation)
| Variable | CREATE | UPDATE | CONSUME | RETIRE |

| `source_files` (94ed manifest entry field) | Planner-agent during `/dso:implementation-plan` when filling 94ed manifest | Re-runs of `/dso:implementation-plan` on revised SCs | SC3 `intent-header-source-check.sh`; 94ed's manifest-aware validator | Implicit with manifest entry — when the intent_id is removed (SC removed from epic) |

| `deferred_test` (94ed manifest entry field, bool) | Planner-agent or operator during `/dso:implementation-plan` when test is intentionally deferred | Operator flips to `false` once the deferred test is registered | SC4(a) pre-commit gate; closure-time block-check | Implicit with manifest entry; operator may zero out the override post-registration |

| `COVERAGE_FINDINGS_<epic-id>` PR-comment marker | SC4(c) `intent-coverage.yml` first run on a PR posts the comment with this marker | Subsequent runs upsert-by-marker (find + edit in place) | The upsert workflow itself reads its own marker to find prior comment | N/A — scoped per-PR; PR closure implicitly retires its comment thread (GitHub does not require active cleanup). The marker is a discriminator within a single PR's comment list, NOT a global registry. |

| `contract_version=1` (published JSON schema) | SC1 publishes `contract_version=1` in the schema | Breaking changes bump to `contract_version=2` with formal versioned migration | Each consumer validates incoming findings JSON against the schema before processing | Persistent — version field lives with the schema; older versions deprecated through formal version bump, not deletion |
Verification (in-session, at sprint Phase I):
- `grep -nE 'source_files|deferred_test' plugins/dso/docs/contracts/intent-allocation-manifest.md` shows both fields documented in the 94ed manifest schema.
- `grep -n 'COVERAGE_FINDINGS_' plugins/dso/workflows/intent-coverage.yml` (or `.github/workflows/`) confirms marker construction.
- `grep -n 'contract_version' plugins/dso/docs/contracts/intent-coverage-findings.md` confirms field publication.
Closes the audit's named gaps: PR-comment marker RETIRE = scoped per-PR (PR closure implicit cleanup); `deferred_test` RETIRE = operator flips or implicit with manifest entry removal.
### External-dependency verification (Probe-6 remediation, 2026-05-18 follow-up)

The original 2026-05-16 remediation pass deferred probe 6 because the audit's suggestion was framed as an External Dependencies block gating closure on external state. Reframing: the in-session sprint environment has `gh` CLI access, which makes GitHub PR-comment and GHA-summary state directly verifiable. Adding the in-session checks here:
| Resource | In-session verification command | Expected |

| Upsert-by-marker PR comment posts successfully | After SC4(c) workflow runs on a sprint PR: `gh api /repos/$OWNER/$REPO/issues/<pr>/comments --jq '[.[] \| select(.body \| contains("COVERAGE_FINDINGS_"))] \| length'` | ≥1 |

**What**: Extend `post-all.sh` hook to extract per-turn token counts from the Claude Code hook payload and write them to an active ticket via `ticket-edit.sh --tokens_measured=`.

**Why**: Without automatic extraction, every agent and skill would need to manually emit token counts, which they will not do reliably. The hook runs on every tool call completion and can accumulate per-session token deltas.
**Scope**:
- IN: Parse `post-all.sh` hook payload for token count fields (input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_creation_tokens).
- IN: Active-ticket detection — read a session-local file (e.g. `/tmp/dso-active-ticket-<pid>`) or env var that skills set when beginning work on a specific ticket.
- IN: Accumulate tokens for the session and write periodically (every N tool calls or at session end) to the active ticket.
- OUT: Retroactive token attribution for past sessions.
- OUT: Planning-vs-execution separation — planning skills emit tokens_estimated in their own story.
## Done Definitions
- When this story is complete, a sprint session with an active ticket accumulates `tokens_measured` on that ticket visible via `ticket show`.

← Satisfies: "Measure execution token use on the worked ticket"
- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic.

content.text: ## Context

The Jira bridge (`plugins/dso/scripts/bridge/`) tracks only four fields in EDIT events: `priority`, `assignee`, `title`, `description` (see `_handle_edit.py:73-88`). Three DSO-local fields with direct Jira analogs are never synced: `parent_id` (Jira Epic Link), `tags` (Jira Labels), and `blocks`/`depends_on` link relations (Jira Issue Links of type "Blocks"). This leads to silent divergence where a local reparent or retag is invisible in Jira, and vice versa. Additionally, the new `supersedes` relation (scoped in Epic 6f7a-4ba6 expansion) must sync lossily as Jira "Relates" with a local-richer-wins precedence rule on inbound. This epic closes all four bridge sync gaps in one coherent remediation.
## Success Criteria

- `parent_id` synced bidirectionally via Jira Epic Link field. Outbound: local parent-child changes write the Epic Link on next sync. Inbound: Jira Epic Link changes write a local EDIT(parent_id) event. Reducer EDIT handler extended.
- `tags` synced bidirectionally via Jira Labels. Outbound: tag add/remove writes Jira label update. Inbound: Jira label change writes local EDIT(tags) event.

- `blocks` and `depends_on` link relations synced bidirectionally via Jira Issue Links of type "Blocks". Outbound: new LINK event triggers Jira issue-link create. Inbound: new Jira Issue Link triggers local LINK event. UNLINK symmetric.

- `supersedes` relation synced lossily as Jira "Relates" (no native Jira supersedes type). Local `supersedes` value is authoritative: on inbound, if a Jira "Relates" link matches an existing local `supersedes`, local wins; other "Relates" links are imported as local `relates_to`.
- Bridge EDIT event tracking extended in `_handle_edit.py` from 4 fields to 7 (adding parent_id, tags, link-deltas). Comprehensive integration tests covering all four sync directions pass.
- Conflict handling: on simultaneous local + remote change to the same field, bridge raises BRIDGE_ALERT for human resolution (existing pattern).
## Approach

Extend `_handle_edit.py` to track `parent_id`, `tags`, and link-deltas in EDIT tracking. Extend `_outbound_handlers.py` to write Jira Epic Link, Labels, and Issue Links. Extend `_inbound_api.py` to read these Jira fields and emit local EDIT/LINK events. Add precedence rule for `supersedes`-over-`relates` in link handler. Coordinate with Epic 6f7a-4ba6 to ensure `supersedes` relation exists before this epics supersedes-sync work lands.
## Dependencies
- Depends on Epic 1de7-50d4 (resolution/reporter — reducer schema prerequisite for clean EDIT event extension).
- Serialized after Epic 6f7a-4ba6 (extended `ticket link` for `supersedes` relation must exist before this epic can sync it). Overlaps bridge files with 6f7a-4ba6 expansion.
## Out of Scope
- Jira custom field mapping beyond parent/labels/links
- Agent-specific Jira accountId provisioning
- Jira permission escalation handling (operational concern)

content.text: ## Story S2: Per-session isolation via session-start hook + session_id sanitization + CI fallback
### Description

**What**: Extend the DSO session-start hook to capture the Claude Code `session_id` from hook input, sanitize to `[a-f0-9-]+` (non-conforming inputs are hashed into a conforming key), and write `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dso-test-run/.current-session`. `test-run.sh` reads this file to scope all state under `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dso-test-run/<session_id>/`. When `.current-session` is missing, the launcher falls back to `$GITHUB_RUN_ID` → `$CI_JOB_ID` → `sha256(cwd)[:16]` in that precedence order. Never uses a silent shared default.

**Why**: Cross-session concurrency (two Claude sessions running tests simultaneously in different worktrees or the same worktree) requires per-session state keying. CI runs are not Claude sessions and need a deterministic fallback.
**Scope**:
- IN: session-start hook update, session_id sanitizer, `.current-session` marker, per-session state dir layout, CI fallback chain
- OUT: same-session duplicate-launch guard (S3), cleanup of orphaned state dirs (operational — not in this epic)
### Done Definitions
- When this story is complete, session-start hook writes the sanitized session_id to `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dso-test-run/.current-session`
← Satisfies: "session-start hook captures the Claude Code session_id, sanitizes to [a-f0-9-]+, and writes ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dso-test-run/.current-session"
- When this story is complete, two Claude sessions with different session_ids invoke `test-run start` simultaneously without shared-state collision (state dirs are distinct)
← Satisfies: "Two Claude sessions running in different worktrees (or the same worktree) can invoke test-run start simultaneously without any shared-state collision"
- When this story is complete, a CI run (no `.current-session` present) derives a session key from `$GITHUB_RUN_ID`, `$CI_JOB_ID`, or `sha256(cwd)` in that precedence order

← Satisfies: "When .current-session is missing (CI runs, session-start hook failed to fire, upgraded plugin with stale hooks), the launcher falls back to a deterministic key derived from $GITHUB_RUN_ID, $CI_JOB_ID, or a cwd-hash in that precedence order — never silently using a shared default"
- When this story is complete, a session_id containing `/`, `..`, or whitespace is rejected-and-hashed rather than used directly in a path
← Satisfies: "sanitizes it to [a-f0-9-]+ (rejecting any input containing /, .., whitespace, or path-traversal sequences — fall back to a hash of the raw session_id when the input is non-conforming)"
- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic
### Considerations
- [Security] path-traversal sanitization is a security-relevant boundary — verify with adversarial inputs in unit tests
- [Reliability] session-start hook registration must survive plugin upgrades; if hook fails to fire, the CI fallback chain keeps the launcher functional
## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.

content.text: ## Continuous Monitoring and Observability

Deploying code is only half the battle; knowing how it behaves in the wild is the other. Observability involves instrumenting systems with logs, metrics, and traces to understand their internal states.
**The Impact:** It drastically reduces Mean Time to Recovery (MTTR) by allowing teams to pinpoint and fix the root cause of production failures quickly.
## Scope

Integrate observability considerations into the preplanning and implementation-plan workflows so that logging, metrics, and tracing are planned and implemented as first-class concerns alongside feature code — not bolted on after deployment. Preplanning should generate stories that include observability requirements, and implementation-plan should produce tasks that cover instrumentation alongside functional implementation.
