content.text: ## Context

The CI LLM review runner (`ci-llm-review-runner.sh` plus `llm-api-call.sh`) is bash + 5+ inline `python3` heredocs with regex-fallback JSON parsing, three near-identical curl blocks for specialists + a fourth for arch synthesis. Adding a third provider is O(N) shell complexity — each new provider requires a new bash branch, a new heredoc, and a new response-extraction regex. Unit testing requires `PATH`-mocked curl driving the whole script; there are no unit-testable functions. This epic migrates orchestration to a Python package (`plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/`) and adopts LiteLLM as the provider abstraction. Anthropic and OpenAI both ship in this epic. Provider/tier fallback ships in this epic too — fallback is fundamentally a LiteLLM-substrate concern, not a downstream loop concern. Tool-use loop and prompt caching follow in a downstream epic; Gemini follows in a placeholder follow-on epic. Both downstream epics are blocked by this one. Doing the migration in isolation produces a stable Python foundation for those downstream epics to land on, and a single parity-test cycle to validate that schema and behavior are preserved across the cutover.
## Success Criteria

- New `plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/` Python package replaces bash orchestration. Modules: `runner.py` (entry-point), `classifier.py` (tier selection — pure function), `dispatch.py` (`asyncio.gather` for parallel specialists + overlay calls), `providers/` (LiteLLM-backed clients behind a common interface), `findings.py` (single JSON normalization implementation replacing the 5+ inline heredocs). `ci-llm-review-runner.sh` reduced to ≤50 lines and exists only as a thin shim that resolves `_PLUGIN_ROOT` and execs `python3 -m dso_ci_review.runner`. `llm-api-call.sh` deleted. References in `CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md`, `ci-overlay-flags.md`, and `onboarding/SKILL.md` updated to reflect the new module layout.

- LiteLLM-backed provider abstraction: Anthropic and OpenAI both functional in CI runs, verified by an integration test exercising each provider end-to-end against fixture diffs. LiteLLM is pinned to an exact version (`litellm==<version>`) in the package's lockfile — compatible-release (`~=`) and range pinning (`>=`) are explicitly rejected by a CI lint step that scans the lockfile, to remain immune to the supply-chain attack class confirmed in March 2026 (versions 1.82.7 / 1.82.8). A parity-test gate is required before any LiteLLM version bump is accepted. Adding the Gemini follow-on epic requires only a new entry under `providers/` plus a config key — no changes to `runner.py`, `dispatch.py`, or `findings.py`. Verified by adding a stub `mock` provider in tests as the third implementation.

- Schema-equivalent `reviewer-findings.json` parity across the fixture corpus: same fixture diffs produce findings JSON that conforms to the existing schema and preserves the full set of pre-migration `critical` / `important` / `fragile` findings (additive findings allowed but no critical / important / fragile finding may be dropped). The parity test additionally asserts zero dropped findings relative to the pre-migration baseline on the fixture corpus — eliminating the silent-drop failure mode of the current bash regex-fallback JSON parsing. Parity-test job runs in CI for the duration of the epic and is removed at epic close. Pre-migration baseline captured as a checked-in golden corpus in story 1, before migration begins, and reused by the downstream tool-use epic's before/after grounded-finding comparison.

- `asyncio.gather` partial-failure handling produces a user-observable improvement vs. the current bash behavior: when one specialist or overlay provider call fails with **any LiteLLM exception** (including but not limited to 5xx-class, network failure, timeout, rate-limit/quota, authentication, and content-policy errors), the review degrades to partial findings instead of aborting the whole run, and the engineer sees an explicit error entry for the failed specialist on the PR (current bash runner aborts the entire review on a single error and produces invalid JSON in slot files when the provider returns an error envelope that the regex-fallback parser cannot extract findings from). **Slot files always contain either valid findings JSON or a structured error entry conforming to the findings schema; raw provider error response text is never written to a slot file.** Verified by a test that injects representative exceptions from each LiteLLM exception class (`RateLimitError`, `BadRequestError`, `AuthenticationError`, `ContentPolicyViolationError`, `InternalServerError`, `Timeout`) into one specialist call and asserts the resulting `reviewer-findings.json` includes (a) the surviving specialists' findings and (b) an explicit error entry for the failed specialist that surfaces in the PR review summary; in particular, the slot file passes JSON schema validation in every error case.

- Per-module unit tests using `respx` / `httpx.MockTransport`-style provider mocks (no `PATH`-mocked curl in unit tests). Integration tests exercise both Anthropic and OpenAI end-to-end. Story 1 transport-verification acceptance criterion: instantiate a LiteLLM client in the same configuration `providers/` will use and assert its internal HTTP transport is `httpx`-based for the Anthropic and OpenAI provider paths. If `aiohttp` is detected on any path, substitute `pytest-httpx` for `respx` as the test mock — do not rely on `DISABLE_AIOHTTP_TRANSPORT` or the `httpx_client` parameter as a forcing mechanism, as both have open reliability bugs across providers (LiteLLM #12581, #13049). Document the detected transport per provider before any provider unit tests are written. CI install pipeline uses `actions/setup-python` (or platform equivalent) with `cache: 'pip'` against a checked-in lockfile so cold-runner pip install does not regress CI run duration. CI run duration neutral-or-better: post-migration p50 and p95 CI review-job duration on the fixture corpus is no greater than the bash-baseline duration captured before migration begins; verified by comparison script at epic close. All existing CI invocation surfaces (`ci-llm-review-runner.sh` shim, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `templates/ci-dso-staged.yml`, `tests/scripts/test-ci-llm-review-job.sh`, `test-ci-llm-review-runner.sh`) continue to work without per-platform conditionals.

- Provider chain + tier-upgrade fallback via LiteLLM, with `fallback_exhausted` signal. Every `litellm.completion(...)` call in `dso_ci_review/dispatch.py` is constructed with `streaming=False` (avoiding LiteLLM streaming-mode fallback bugs #22296, #6532) and: `fallbacks=[...]` rendered from `dso-config.conf` key `ci_review.provider_chain` (ordered provider list, e.g., `[anthropic, openai]`) × the agent's declared `model:` field expressed against each non-primary provider — gives cross-provider fallback on any LiteLLM exception; `context_window_fallbacks=[...]` rendered from the agent's `model:` field upgraded through `[haiku, sonnet, opus]` on the agent's primary provider until the top of the ladder — gives same-provider tier upgrade on `ContextWindowExceededError`. Agents already at `opus` (deep arch, overlay reviewers) get an empty list (no upgrade available); the opus terminal case for `ContextWindowExceededError` is documented operator-facing as falling through to `fallback_exhausted` rather than escalating cross-provider. When LiteLLM exhausts both lists, the dispatcher catches the terminal `litellm.exceptions.OpenAIError`-class exception and (1) writes a `fallback_exhausted` entry into `reviewer-findings.json` (atomic write via temp-file + rename; per-agent file ownership documented to prevent parallel-write corruption when deep tier dispatches 3 specialists + arch synthesis) conforming to a documented schema (`docs/contracts/ci-review-fallback-exhausted.md`) with fields: `agent_id`, `primary_model`, `attempted_cross_provider[]`, `attempted_context_models[]`, `final_exception_class`, `final_exception_message` — schema is the consumption contract for the downstream Copilot-reviewer-gate epic; (2) renders any successful fallback hops as one-line notes in the PR review summary in stable format `[fallback: <agent> <primary_model> -> <fallback_model> (<exception_class>)]`. Startup precondition: dispatcher refuses to run with a clear error when any provider in `ci_review.provider_chain` lacks credentials in the runtime environment, so credential drift between local config and CI does not silently mask rate-limit failures as auth errors in `final_exception_class`. `provider_chain` parsing is strict: lowercase canonical LiteLLM provider names only; whitespace trimmed; unknown providers reject at config-load time. A test asserts `streaming=False` is preserved through every fallback hop (defending against LiteLLM router defaults or per-entry `stream: true` overrides). Verified by: (a) unit test injecting `RateLimitError` from primary, asserting next provider answers, hop rendered, review completes; (b) unit test injecting `ContextWindowExceededError` from primary tier-model, asserting next tier-model on same provider answers, hop rendered, review completes; (c) unit test injecting failure on every chain entry, asserting `fallback_exhausted` JSON entry written with all six fields populated and surviving agents' partial findings preserved per SC4; (d) contract conformance test loading the schema against the JSON; (e) test asserting `streaming=False` preservation across hops; (f) test asserting startup-time rejection when a chained provider's credential is absent.
## Cross-Epic Interactions
- Resource: reviewer-findings.json schema and CI / local review parity

Interaction: 4b8f-924d (Severity-only review schema) removes the scores object and `REVIEW_RESULT` / `MIN_SCORE` lines; this epic's `findings.py` is where the CI half of that schema change must propagate. This epic blocks 4b8f-924d.

Gate: schema collision resolved via the `blocks` dependency + 4b8f-924d's description has been updated to apply the schema removal across both the CI path (post-this-epic) and the local `/dso:review` path.
- Resource: ci-llm-review-runner.sh shim invocation surface

Interaction: 1083-fb3d (Local workflow simplification -> enforcement.strategy=ci) flips strategy and exercises the shim invocation surface; this epic reduces the shim to <=50 lines while preserving the invocation surface byte-for-byte.
Gate: 1083-fb3d's PR-mode integration test must verify the new shim correctly dispatches to the `dso_ci_review` module.
- Resource: REVIEW-DEFENSE comments in CI review scripts
Interaction: 5018-64ce (Evaluate REVIEW-DEFENSE comments) audits review-defense annotations including those in `ci-llm-review-runner.sh`; this epic rewrites those scripts.
Gate: coordinate timing — either 5018-64ce captures defenses pre-rewrite, or this epic ensures defenses migrate into the Python module as needed.
- Resource: tool-use authorization layer (separate from runtime adapter)

Interaction: 2239-1545 (Cross-runtime support via harness adapter) addresses AI tool runtime event normalization (Claude Code vs. Cursor vs. OpenCode vs. Codex hook stdin); this epic's LiteLLM provider abstraction is at the LLM API layer, not the runtime layer. They do not share infrastructure; 2239-1545 remains an open, distinct epic.
Gate: documented distinction; 2239-1545 stays open.
- Resource: `fallback_exhausted` JSON shape in `reviewer-findings.json`

Interaction: A future Copilot-reviewer-terminal-gate epic (not yet created) consumes this entry as the trigger to require Copilot review approval before merge. The schema (`docs/contracts/ci-review-fallback-exhausted.md`) is the consumption contract; the future epic blocks on this one.
Gate: schema is the contract; future epic blocked by this one.
- Resource: cross-provider switch wastes Anthropic prompt cache built up earlier in a run

Interaction: 2fa0-a2d9-35b7-4101 (context-augmentation loop + prompt caching + turn-budget exhaustion) builds a multi-turn cached prefix on the primary provider; when this epic's SC6 fallback fires mid-run, the alternate provider sees a cold prefix and the cached prefix is wasted, producing a per-run cost cliff.

Gate: mitigation deferred to integration time once both epics are merged — candidate mitigations include fallback-after-N-turns demotion to fail-closed, or a per-run cost ceiling. Tracked as a follow-up bug if the cost cliff is observed in production.
## Scenario Analysis

- Shim <-> Python entry-point PATH / venv mismatch in CI (high, deployment): the shim invokes `python3 -m dso_ci_review.runner`; CI runners may have multiple python3s and the package may not be importable from the shell's `python3` unless installed or path-injected. Mitigation: the shim resolves the package path explicitly and the CI install step uses `actions/setup-python` with cached pip and an editable install (`pip install -e .`) before the runner is invoked.

- llm-api-call.sh deletion breaks out-of-tree consumers (high, deployment): host projects calling the deleted script break without a deprecation window. Mitigation: deprecation announcement in release notes; consider a thin compatibility wrapper in the shim that warns and forwards to the Python entry-point for one minor version.

- LiteLLM version drift breaks tool-use schema (high, runtime): LiteLLM's mapping for tool / response shapes has changed across minor versions and the parallel-tool-use translation has documented production issues (LiteLLM #26529, discussion #18271). Mitigation: pin LiteLLM to a tested minor version in the package lockfile; require a parity-test pass before accepting any LiteLLM version bump; add a renovate / dependabot policy enforcing that gate.

- asyncio.gather partial-failure swallows specialist exceptions (high, runtime): without `return_exceptions=True` and per-task error capture, one transient provider error aborts the whole review. Mitigation: SC4 explicit partial-failure handling.

- Findings parity test masks semantic regressions (high, runtime): shape-only parity passes despite severity downgrades or critical findings dropped. Mitigation: SC3 parity test compares both schema conformance and preservation of every pre-migration critical / important / fragile finding by id / title; additive findings are allowed but no critical / important / fragile finding may be dropped.

- Provider auth secrets not provisioned for OpenAI path on day one (high, deployment): rollout requires `OPENAI_API_KEY` in org / repo secrets before merge. Mitigation: secrets-provisioning step is part of the rollout plan and listed as a story precondition.

- Provider routing config has no fail-safe default (medium, configuration): missing or malformed `providers/` config silently switches model. Mitigation: missing config refuses to run with a clear error; default is fail-loud rather than fall back to a provider that may not be authorized.

- Provider chain credential drift between local and CI (high, deployment): `ci_review.provider_chain` in `dso-config.conf` is checked into the repo, but API keys are environment-injected in CI. If a developer's local config lists `[anthropic, openai]` but only `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set in the CI environment, the cross-provider fallback hop will fail with an auth error rather than the intended rate-limit fallback, and the `fallback_exhausted` entry will report the auth error as `final_exception_class` — masking the original 429. Mitigation: SC6 startup precondition check that all providers in the chain have credentials available, with a clear error when not.

- `fallback_exhausted` partial-write corruption (high, runtime): `reviewer-findings.json` may be written by parallel tier reviewers (deep tier dispatches 3 specialists + arch synthesis), or the dispatcher may crash mid-write. Without atomic write the consumer Copilot-reviewer-gate epic will see malformed JSON. Mitigation: SC6 atomic write (temp file + rename) and per-agent file ownership documented in `docs/contracts/ci-review-fallback-exhausted.md`.

- `streaming=False` contradicted by LiteLLM router defaults or per-entry overrides (medium, configuration): SC6 mandates `streaming=False`, but LiteLLM router-level configs and some provider plugins can re-enable streaming via fallback chain entries that carry their own params. Mitigation: SC6 test that asserts `streaming=False` is preserved through every fallback hop.

- Opus-tier `ContextWindowExceededError` terminal case is silently undocumented (medium, configuration): SC6 says agents already at opus get an empty `context_window_fallbacks` list; on context overflow, opus agents fall through both lists directly to `fallback_exhausted` since cross-provider on context-window errors is not part of the routing. Operators may assume opus is protected by tier upgrade. Mitigation: SC6 documents the opus terminal case operator-facing.

- `provider_chain` string parsing strictness (medium, configuration): `dso-config.conf` is KEY=VALUE plain text. Typos (e.g., `Anthropic` vs `anthropic`, alias `claude`) silently produce empty fallback chain (since rendered fallbacks list filters unknown providers), defeating SC6. Mitigation: SC6 strict parsing — lowercase canonical LiteLLM provider names only; unknown providers reject at config-load time.
## Dependencies
- Blocked by: 5d6e-86a9 (CI LLM-review parity port — must be fully merged to main before this epic starts).
- Blocks: 4b8f-924d (Severity-only review schema removal must propagate through the new `findings.py`).
- Blocks: 2fa0-a2d9-35b7-4101 (context-augmentation loop + caching + exhaustion epic operates on this epic's merged Python module + LiteLLM abstraction including fallback).
- Blocks: f9f8-a15c-79e0-4dc3 (Gemini placeholder follow-on epic — Gemini provider entry depends on this epic's LiteLLM provider abstraction).
- Blocks: future Copilot-reviewer-terminal-gate epic (not yet created — consumes `fallback_exhausted` schema from SC6).
## Research Findings

- External Integration: LiteLLM provider abstraction — Parallel tool calls supported across Anthropic + OpenAI via OpenAI-format function-calling schema; passthrough adapter active. Key insight: LiteLLM as provider router is well-supported, but minor-version pinning is required because the Anthropic / OpenAI tool-use translation has changed across releases (issues #26529, #18271). Sources: https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/providers/anthropic , https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/26529 .

- Performance: LiteLLM caching translation — Auto-injection supported for Anthropic; OpenAI prefix caching is automatic. Known LiteLLM bug on Gemini multi-cache mapping (issue #17201). Key insight: confirms Gemini deferral; Anthropic + OpenAI caching is unaffected and will land in the downstream tool-use + caching epic. Source: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/17201 .

- Operational: CI dependency caching — `actions/setup-python` with `cache: 'pip'` reduces cold pip install from 60-90s to ~2-5s with a checked-in lockfile; `uv` brings sub-second installs. Key insight: cold-install cost is a solved problem in CI; mitigation is SC5 cached install pipeline.

- External Integration: LiteLLM SDK-level `fallbacks` and `context_window_fallbacks` — VERIFIED-WITH-CAVEATS for non-streaming + plain-text completion paths against Anthropic + OpenAI. `fallbacks` triggers on any exception (non-streaming); `context_window_fallbacks` triggers specifically on `ContextWindowExceededError` and composes with `fallbacks`. Streaming-mode fallback has confirmed open bugs (LiteLLM #22296 broken for 429 + sync streaming, #6532 not triggered for `InternalServerError` overload), driving the `streaming=False` mandate in SC6. Terminal exception on dual exhaustion re-raises the last provider exception (non-streaming); catch `litellm.exceptions.OpenAIError` base. Zero popular OSS examples of SDK-level fallback found — the documented happy path but less battle-tested than the LiteLLM Router path. Sources: https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/completion/reliable_completions , https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/tutorials/model_fallbacks , https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/22296 , https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/6532 , https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/10793 .
## Approach

Single-epic cutover: a new `plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/` Python package replaces bash orchestration in one merge with a parity-test gate that runs for the duration of the epic and is removed at epic close. LiteLLM provides the provider abstraction; Anthropic and OpenAI both wired in this epic. Provider/tier fallback (SC6) ships as part of the substrate via LiteLLM's `fallbacks` and `context_window_fallbacks` SDK parameters with `streaming=False`, surfaced through a `fallback_exhausted` entry in a documented schema for downstream consumption. Tool-use loop and prompt caching deliberately deferred to the downstream context-augmentation epic (2fa0) so this epic is a pure substrate refactor with a clean parity gate.
### Planning Intelligence Log
- Web research (Step 2.6): triggered

- Bright-line conditions that fired: external integration (LiteLLM new dep + LiteLLM SDK-level fallback parameters), novel architectural pattern (Python module replacing bash orchestration), performance (prompt caching considerations carried into downstream epic)
- Scenario analysis (Step 2.75): triggered
- Scenarios surviving blue team filter: 15 across original folded epic; 7 redistributed to this epic plus 5 new fallback-related scenarios surviving Blue Team in re-brainstorm
- Practitioner-requested additional cycles: re-brainstorm to add SC6 (provider/tier fallback) per user direction that fallback is a LiteLLM-substrate concern rather than a downstream loop concern
- Follow-on scrutiny (Step 0): triggered — depth: 0 (downstream context-augmentation epic and Gemini placeholder; future Copilot-reviewer-gate epic)

- Feasibility resolution (Step 2.5): triggered — cycles: 2, gaps: (1) aiohttp-vs-httpx transport ambiguity in LiteLLM Router (#12581) plus exact-version pinning posture for supply-chain attack class (LiteLLM 1.82.7/1.82.8 March 2026) — resolved by SC2 (==-pinning + lint) and SC5 (Story 1 transport-verification gate); (2) LiteLLM SDK-level `fallbacks` / `context_window_fallbacks` reliability across non-streaming plain-text paths — VERIFIED-WITH-CAVEATS, mandating `streaming=False` and `litellm.exceptions.OpenAIError` base catch
- LLM-instruction signal (Step 5): not triggered (substrate refactor; reviewer agent prompts not modified by this epic)
- Scale context (Step 0): small scale (default — bounded fixture corpus; CI run volume governed by PR throughput, not user-traffic scale)

content.text: ## Context

DSO plugin hooks use 3 inconsistent error handling patterns: silent fail-open (5 post-* dispatchers), logging fail-open with copy-pasted JSONL traps (~24 inline occurrences), and no trap at all (7 pre-* dispatchers). Host project users who encounter a hook crash in a pre-* dispatcher get blocked with no diagnostic information. The logging trap is duplicated across hooks with only the hook name changed. New hook authors have no clear template.
## Success Criteria
- A shared _dso_hook_err_handler function exists in hooks/lib/hook-error-handler.sh that all fail-open hooks use
- All 7 pre-* dispatchers (pre-bash, pre-all, pre-edit, pre-write, pre-enterplanmode, pre-exitplanmode, pre-taskoutput) and all 5 post-* dispatchers have fail-open ERR traps using the shared handler

- All ~24 existing copy-pasted logging traps migrated to shared handler (targets: hooks/lib/pre-bash-functions.sh, pre-edit-write-functions.sh, pre-all-functions.sh, session-misc-functions.sh, review-gate-bypass-sentinel.sh; top-level: session-safety-check.sh, taskoutput-block-guard.sh, plan-review-gate.sh, track-cascade-failures.sh, title-length-validator.sh, track-tool-errors.sh, review-stop-check.sh, check-validation-failures.sh)

- Error logs written to ~/.claude/logs/dso-hook-errors.jsonl with enriched fields: timestamp, hook name, line number, repo root, plugin version, bash version, OS. Legacy path deprecated; all readers and test fixtures updated to new path
- Enforcement hooks explicitly excluded with machine-enforced boundary (header convention + pre-commit check)
- All existing tests pass
- At least one new test verifies ERR trigger produces correctly-structured JSONL entry with all enriched fields
## Scenario Analysis
- Shared handler source failure drops ERR traps (high): guard with || true and inline fallback
- ERR trap fires on intentional enforcement returns (medium): shared handler must not interfere with trap - ERR; return 2 pattern
- JSONL log grows unbounded (medium): handler should include size guard
- Dual competing log files during migration (high): readers must be updated atomically with writers
- Partial migration inconsistency (medium): migrate all ~24 sites in one epic
- Enforcement boundary is ambiguous (high): add convention + check
## Approach

Create _dso_hook_err_handler() in hooks/lib/hook-error-handler.sh. Handler disables ERR trap inside body, uses only builtins, caches plugin version on first source, falls back gracefully for git/path failures. Includes log size guard. Migrates all ~24 trap sites and all readers atomically. Adds enforcement hook boundary convention enforced by pre-commit check.
## Dependencies
None. Note: epic 0df8-1c8c (code quality) should complete first if it touches the same hook files.

content.text: Enforce a size constraint on session state files to keep session resumption fast and reliable.
## Reference: get-shit-done STATE.md

get-shit-done (47k stars) enforces a strict constraint: STATE.md must stay under 100 lines. When state exceeds this limit, it is digested — key decisions and current position are preserved, but verbose history is moved to separate summary files. This keeps session resumption fast because the state file stays small and coherent.
## Problem

DSO's MEMORY.md and session context can grow unbounded. Long sprints accumulate checkpoint notes, ticket comments, and investigation history. When a session resumes (or context compacts), the agent must process all of this to understand where it left off. Large state files lead to:
- Slower session resumption
- Earlier context compaction
- Loss of coherent context when compaction drops important details
- Sub-agents receiving bloated dispatch prompts
## Implementation

1. **Size constraint on MEMORY.md** — enforce a maximum line count (configurable via dso-config.conf, default 100 lines). When exceeded, digest the content: preserve current position, active decisions, and blockers; move completed work summaries to separate files.
2. **Session state digest format:**
- Current phase/step and what's in progress
- Active decisions that affect next steps
- Blockers and open questions
- Pointer to detailed history (file path or ticket ID)
- Performance metrics (plans completed, time elapsed)
3. **Automatic digestion trigger** — when MEMORY.md exceeds the limit, the /dso:end session close or context compaction should automatically digest rather than truncate.
4. **Sprint orchestrator integration** — between sub-agent batches, the orchestrator should digest accumulated state rather than appending indefinitely.
5. **Resume fast-path** — when resuming a sprint or debug-everything session, the digested state file should provide enough context to resume without re-reading all ticket comments and git history.

content.text: Integrate the mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md Accessibility Reviewer agent (https://github.com/mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md/blob/main/agents/ACCESSIBILITY_REVIEWER.md) into DSO's code review pipeline as a dedicated accessibility overlay.
## What the Agent Does
An IAAP CPWA-certified accessibility auditor agent that uses a four-phase adversarial Red Team / Blue Team pipeline:
- **Phase 1 (Red Team — Functional Friction):** Simulates 6 disability personas on Critical User Journeys:
1. Screen Reader Navigator (Non-Visual)
2. Power Keyboard User (Motor Limit)
3. Magnification Expert (Low Vision, 400% zoom)
4. Cognitive Strategist (Neurodivergent)
5. Vestibular User (Motion Sensitivity)
6. Distracted/Fatigued User (Situational Limit)

- **Phase 2 (Red Team — Semantic Audit):** Code-aware manual audit targeting the ~60-70% of WCAG 2.1/2.2 AA that requires human reasoning (1.3.2, 1.1.1, 2.4.4, 3.3.3, 3.3.4, 3.3.7, 3.3.8, 2.5.7, 4.1.3).
- **Phase 3 (Deterministic Integration):** Consumes Axe Core automated tool output as ground truth for mechanical compliance.
- **Phase 4 (Blue Team — Synthesis):** Merges findings, scrubs false positives, resolves conflicts via web research, and escalates severity when issues cluster on critical user journeys.
## Integration Points
1. Add as a review overlay in the code review workflow — activated when the complexity classifier detects UI/frontend changes (similar to security and performance overlays)
2. Output format: structured Markdown with Finding Title, Severity, Persona Impact, Evidence (DOM snippet), WCAG Mapping, and Technical Remediation
3. Integrate with Axe Core output in CI for Phase 3 deterministic input
4. Add to preplanning as an accessibility reviewer perspective using the 6 persona framework
5. Create a standalone /dso:accessibility-check skill for on-demand audits
## Key Design Principles to Preserve
- Prioritizes functional task success over checkbox compliance
- Cumulative severity escalation: multiple Low issues on the same critical path = Critical barrier
- Strict hallucination guardrail: no invented DOM elements
- Actionable remediation only: must cite specific ARIA attributes, HTML changes, or CSS adjustments
- Division of labor: automated tools handle mechanical checks, LLM handles contextual reasoning
Source: https://github.com/mgifford/ACCESSIBILITY.md

content.text: Placeholder epic tracking patterns where CI (Ubuntu/Linux) catches failures that the local test gate (macOS) misses. Patterns identified from session analysis:

1. **Platform portability (macOS vs Linux)**: mktemp template format (GNU mktemp requires trailing X's for -t; BSD mktemp is lenient), sed -i '' vs sed -i, bash version differences (macOS ships bash 3.2), grep/awk flag differences, stat/date flag differences. Example CI-only failure: tests/hooks/test-hook-inline-trap-consolidation.sh failed on CI because 'mktemp -t prefix' without X's errors on Linux but returns a valid path on macOS.

2. **Script CWD assumptions**: Plugin scripts that assume they run from a specific directory; relative path constructions like '../lib/deps.sh' that fail when CWD changes. Example CI-only failure: plugins/dso/scripts/recipe-executor.sh, scaffold-adapter.sh, and update-shim.sh broke under CI because their '../' relative path resolution was fragile. Local tests pass because local test harness runs from the plugin directory; CI invokes scripts from REPO_ROOT.

3. **ARTIFACTS_DIR context mismatch**: Reviewer sub-agents dispatched into worktrees compute a different ARTIFACTS_DIR (/tmp/lockpick-test-artifacts-<worktree-basename>) than the orchestrator reading from the session branch, causing hash mismatches in the review gate. Systemic gap: no local test reproduces the worktree-vs-session ARTIFACTS_DIR divergence.

4. **Missing Linux-only test coverage in local suite**: CI runs shellcheck (severity=warning) on plugins/dso/scripts/*.sh and hooks, plus ruff check + ruff format --check. The local test gate does NOT run shellcheck on staged shell files and does NOT run ruff across the full Python scope CI checks. Validate.sh runs ruff on app/ only, not on plugins/dso/scripts/*.py. Files like plugins/dso/hooks/*.sh are only shellchecked in CI.

5. **Stale agent worktrees polluting scan results**: scan-config-keys.sh and other static scanners scan .claude/worktrees/ agent directories on local runs, picking up fixture config keys from test files. CI does not have stale worktrees, so scans return cleaner results there. Locally-clean scans can pass CI-dirty scans.
**Concrete gap summary**:
- CI shellcheck coverage: plugins/dso/scripts/*.sh + plugins/dso/hooks/*.sh + **/*.sh -- not run locally in pre-commit or record-test-status flows
- CI ruff scope: plugins/dso/scripts/*.py + tests/**/*.py -- validate.sh only runs ruff inside app/
- CI Linux mktemp/sed/grep flavor: not reproduced by any local test
- Local test gate fuzzy-match only associates tests with source via name similarity — no test exists that validates cross-platform portability of the source under test

**Recommended highest-impact fix**: Add 'shellcheck staged shell files' and 'ruff plugins/dso/scripts+tests' to validate.sh (or a new local-ci.sh script) and wire them into the same pre-commit gate. This would eliminate ~80% of CI-only failure surface area without requiring actual Linux test runners.
See session notes for full details. Priority: investigate systemic patterns and add CI-equivalent local tests.

content.text: Document how DSO's sprint and fix-bug workflows implement the Ralph Wiggum autonomous loop pattern — the dominant community pattern for autonomous AI agent execution. This documentation positions DSO's existing capabilities within the broader ecosystem's vocabulary and helps users and contributors understand DSO's architectural alignment with industry-standard patterns.
## Background: The Ralph Wiggum Pattern
The Ralph Wiggum autonomous loop is the most popular pattern in the Claude Code ecosystem (dedicated subcategory in awesome-claude-code, 5+ projects, Anthropic-cited). It describes an agent that:
- Runs autonomously in a loop until work is complete
- Has circuit breakers to prevent runaway execution
- Includes safety gates that pause for human input at high-stakes decisions
- Manages context window exhaustion through compaction or fresh-context strategies
- Can resume from interruption
## How DSO Already Implements This
### /dso:sprint (Epic Execution Loop)
- **Loop structure:** Phase 3 (batch preparation) → Phase 4 (sub-agent dispatch) → Phase 5 (post-batch validation) → Phase 6 (score check) → back to Phase 3 if incomplete
- **Circuit breakers:** Max 5 concurrent sub-agents; commit+push between batches; 5 cascading failure limit triggers /dso:fix-cascade-recovery

- **Safety gates:** Escalation policy (Autonomous / Escalate-when-blocked / Escalate-unless-confident) set at preplanning; completion verifier dispatched as independent anti-bias check at story/epic closure
- **Context management:** Proactive /compact at 70% context usage; involuntary compaction triggers graceful shutdown; batched test runner prevents timeout
- **Resumability:** CHECKPOINT 1/6-6/6 protocol on sub-agents; ticket comments preserve state; --resume flag reads checkpoints to fast-close near-complete tasks
### /dso:fix-bug (Investigation-Fix Loop)
- **Loop structure:** Classify → Investigate (tiered: BASIC→INTERMEDIATE→ADVANCED→ESCALATED) → Hypothesis validation gate → RED test → Fix → Verify
- **Circuit breakers:** 3-strike escalation on investigation failure; RED-before-fix gate blocks code changes without failing test; max_fix_validate_cycles config bound
- **Safety gates:** Intent search gate (is this intentional behavior?); reversal check (does the fix undo a prior decision?); user approval of root cause before implementation
- **Context management:** Investigation dispatched to sub-agents (fresh context); intent search budget capped at configurable tool calls
- **Resumability:** Bug ticket comments record investigation findings; CHECKPOINT protocol on investigation sub-agents
### /dso:debug-everything (Health Restoration Loop)
- **Loop structure:** Bug-Fix Mode (iterate through open bugs) or Diagnostic Mode (scan → triage → fix pipeline); inner fix→validate loop bounded by debug.max_fix_validate_cycles
- **Circuit breakers:** Session lock prevents concurrent debug sessions; oscillation guard detects ping-pong between fix attempts; file-overlap detection for conflicting agent edits
- **Safety gates:** Safeguard analysis flags bugs in protected files; interactivity mode defers blocking gates as machine-parseable comments in non-interactive mode
- **Resumability:** Session lock + epic ticket state; graceful shutdown with summary note
## Documentation Deliverables

1. **Architecture doc** — plugins/dso/docs/AUTONOMOUS-LOOP-ARCHITECTURE.md mapping DSO's loop patterns to the Ralph Wiggum vocabulary (loop structure, circuit breakers, safety gates, context management, resumability)
2. **README update** — reference the pattern in the project README so ecosystem users recognize DSO's approach

3. **Comparison table** — DSO vs. ralph-orchestrator vs. GSD vs. ECC loop implementations, highlighting where DSO is more comprehensive (two-layer enforcement, sub-agent isolation, anti-bias completion verification)
4. **Differentiator documentation** — explicitly call out what DSO adds beyond the basic pattern:
- Two-layer defense-in-depth (git hooks + tool-use hooks) — most Ralph implementations have soft gates only
- Anti-bias completion verification via independent sub-agent — no other implementation does this
- Event-sourced ticket system as inter-agent coordination bus — most use file-based state
- TDD enforcement with RED markers — most have optional testing
- Tiered model escalation (haiku→sonnet→opus) — most use a single model

content.text: ## Context

The DSO ticket system appends events indefinitely. A long-lived ticket with dozens of transitions, comments, links, and bridge syncs accumulates a large directory that slows reducer replay and bloats the `tickets` branch disk footprint. The `.claude/scripts/dso ticket compact` command exists today for single-ticket compaction but is not routinely applied, has no automatic trigger, and loses comment body detail when it snapshots. The beads project applies summarizing compaction to old closed tickets — collapsing the full history into a concise summary. This epic introduces analogous automatic policy-driven compaction for DSO while preserving full audit integrity via the REVERT mechanism and bridge event preservation.
## Success Criteria
- Compaction policy: closed tickets older than N days (configurable, default 90) are eligible. Archived tickets eligible immediately.
- `ticket compact --all --dry-run` lists eligible tickets and projected space savings without writing any events.

- `ticket compact --all` runs policy-driven compaction producing a single SNAPSHOT event plus a summary COMMENT that records: final status, resolution value, closing reason, number of comments/links replaced, and a brief LLM-generated summary of the ticket journey.
- Bridge-origin events (SYNC, BRIDGE_ALERT) are NEVER compacted — they remain queryable even after compaction of surrounding events.
- Compaction is reversible: the compaction event itself is logged so `ticket-revert.sh` can undo a specific compaction if needed.
- Scheduled maintenance mode integrates with existing `/dso:end-session` or a new periodic hook; running `--all` completes within 5 minutes for a repo with 2,000+ tickets.
## Approach

Extend `ticket-compact.sh` with an `--all` flag that iterates over net-eligible tickets (closed + age >= N days, excluding archived-only tickets with existing snapshots). Each compaction writes one SNAPSHOT event capturing compiled state plus a summary COMMENT — this preserves searchability by `ticket show`. Use the existing SNAPSHOT event format; no new event types needed. LLM summary generation is delegated to a lightweight prompt via the haiku model; if unavailable, fall back to a structured deterministic summary (no LLM).
## Dependencies
No upstream dependencies. Independent housekeeping epic.
## Out of Scope
- Full tickets-branch git GC (separate concern)
- Deletion of tickets (tombstoning is Epic 6f7a-4ba6 scope)
- Remote-side Jira history compaction

content.text: ## Context

DSO's ci-pr workflow mode currently has incoherent LLM review semantics for operators running /dso:sprint and /dso:debug-everything. Sprint Phase A (session-init, creates a long-lived session→main draft PR) opens the session PR correctly, but Phase F (per-story commit + merge) opens story PRs with base=main and auto-merges each one to main directly — orphaning the session draft PR and triggering full-PR llm-review re-reviews of code already cleared by per-story review on every story push. In a representative 5-story sprint, this produces ~3 redundant whole-PR re-reviews on already-approved hunks. /dso:debug-everything Phase F/G (per-tier and per-bug-batch sub-branches) reviews them via local /dso:review sub-agent dispatch, diverging from sprint's CI-driven flow.

This epic refactors both skills onto a unified architecture: when dso.workflow=ci-pr, all sub-branches (story/**, fix/**, bug-batch/**) open PRs against the session branch, gated by a Per-Branch LLM Review CI workflow under GitHub Rulesets (preferred over classic branch protection for session-* pattern scoping per Research Findings). A single session→main PR is the lone path to main; its required check is provenance verification (3-signal cross-check, pinned check-name) plus a narrow integration LLM review whose scope is un-provenanced commits ∪ files modified in ≥2 sub-branches.

Phase definitions: Sprint Phase A = session-init (create-sprint-draft-pr.sh); Sprint Phase F = post-story merge step (changes PR base to session); Debug Phase F = tier 0-1 auto-fix sub-branches; Debug Phase G = tier 2-7 fix-batch sub-branches.

Depends on 3b8b-d7e1-eeff-4796 (dso.workflow config consolidation). Supersedes 8ee4-c51c-c546-4d4e (cycle-tracking) and cafb-4b97-1703-41e3 (squash SHA-rewrite class). Coordinates with b575-ac1c-f720-4839 (cycle-end arbiter — both edit ci.yml llm-review) and 0cf2-42b5-8840-48a1 (sprint SKILL.md refactor — both edit Phase F) via named-step contracts. Reverse depends_on: af26-dd5a-df6d-4f81 (HARD-GATE enforcement) will be blocked by this epic.
## Success Criteria

1. Provenance integrity: every commit in main..session-HEAD on the session→main PR traces to a sub-branch PR whose Per-Branch LLM Review (matching pinned dso.review.check_name) returned SUCCESS, or is reported with its SHA and routed into the integration review's scope. Verified by a fixture sprint where (a) all commits are provenanced (verifier exits 0) and (b) a synthetic direct-to-session commit is injected (verifier exits non-zero, reports the SHA, and the injected commit appears in the integration scope's input file).

2. No re-review of per-branch-approved code: integration LLM review input contains zero hunks for files confined to a single sub-branch with passing review. Verified by inspecting the integration review's input on a fixture sprint where 3 stories touch disjoint files — the input contains zero matching paths for those files.

3. Cross-story integration coverage: integration review scope includes files modified by >=2 sub-branches in the current session. Verified by a fixture sprint where Story A and Story B both modify lib/helper.py — the integration review's input contains the cumulative diff for lib/helper.py.

4. Workflow + branch protection enforced end-to-end: sub-branch PRs base on session-branch; per-branch-review.yml fires for story/fix/bug-batch pushes; Rulesets on session-* reject direct pushes; Phase A preflight asserts (a) Ruleset exists and matches session-*, (b) pinned check name appears in required_status_checks.checks, (c) required_linear_history is false. Verified empirically: a representative sprint produces sub-branch PRs with the expected base; gh run list --workflow=per-branch-review.yml returns >=1 run per branch pattern; an attempted direct push to session is rejected with the expected branch-protection error; the preflight exits non-zero on missing or misconfigured Ruleset.

5. Skill convergence in ci-pr; local mode preserved byte-identical: sprint Phase F + debug Phase F/G in ci-pr mode both invoke per-branch-review.yml; their SKILL.md files reference no local /dso:review in ci-pr branches. Local mode byte-identical to a pre-epic baseline (commit-breadcrumbs.log + git log --pretty=format output diff). Deprecated path sprint-story-review.yml is renamed to per-branch-review.yml; all named consumer files updated: plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/runner.py, plugins/dso/skills/sprint/SKILL.md, tests/workflows/test-sprint-story-review.sh (renamed), tests/workflows/test-sprint-story-review-defenses.sh (renamed), tests/hooks/test-validate-review-output.sh, tests/scripts/test-ci-defense-pipeline.sh, tests/skills/dso_ci_review/test_dispatch_schema_correction.py, and docs/findings/sprint-resume-state.md. Verified by grep -rn 'sprint-story-review' returning zero matches outside explicit deprecation notes.

6. Superseded bugs closed with reproducers passing: bug 8ee4-c51c-c546-4d4e closed with DSO_REVIEW_CYCLE>=2 computed correctly on the session→main PR and prior defenses in TrackerDefenseStore suppressed in the integration review (reproducer: write a defense via defense_store_write, push a triggering commit, observe the cycle-2 review skipping the defended finding). Bug cafb-4b97-1703-41e3 closed with the new API-based provenance check accepting a squash-merged sub-branch's commits as provenanced (reproducer: create a sub-branch PR, squash-merge it into session, run the provenance verifier on a session→main PR including that squash commit — verifier exits 0).
## Operational Constraints

- Provenance retry/backoff: provenance verifier uses exponential backoff (initial 2s, doubled per retry, cap 60s) on gh api commits/<sha>/pulls returning 403/429. Per-walk budget ceiling of 200 API calls; on exhaustion, exit non-zero with BUDGET_EXHAUSTED marker. Per-session SHA→PR-number cache stored in artifact to avoid re-querying on re-runs.

- Ruleset provisioning ownership: one-time repo-admin setup of the session-* Ruleset is the documented prerequisite (instructions added to INSTALL.md and to /dso:onboarding for new projects). Phase A preflight (see SC4) detects missing or misconfigured Ruleset and fails fast with an actionable error message linking to setup docs. This epic does NOT mandate that DSO hold administration:write permission at runtime — operators retain control of branch protection administration.

- In-flight migration: when this epic ships, in-flight sprint sessions may have open story PRs targeting main. A one-time migration script (migrate-story-pr-bases.sh) detects these via gh pr list --search 'base:main head:story/', PATCHes their base to the session branch, then issues gh workflow run per-branch-review.yml --ref <head-branch> to re-trigger the required check. Run by operator before first new sprint after this epic merges.

- Exempt direct-push call sites (descoped from SC4's branch-protection rejection): plugins/dso/scripts/onboarding/github-bootstrap.sh:114 (git push origin HEAD:main) is a one-time repo-bootstrap operation that occurs before any session branch exists; Rulesets on session-* do not apply. Tests that push directly to main (test-record-review.sh, test-merge-to-main-portability.sh, test-merge-state.sh, test-merge-to-main-cleanliness.sh, test-claude-safe-post-merge-amend.sh) are test-infrastructure operations against ephemeral fixtures, exempt.
## Scenario Analysis
- Concurrent sub-branch merges race condition (high, runtime): snapshot session-HEAD SHA at job start.
- GitHub API rate limiting (high, runtime): exponential backoff + 200-call budget + SHA→PR cache.
- Custom merge-commit template omits PR number (high, runtime): signals 1+2 (API + check status) are the trusted pair; signal 3 corroborating only.
- In-flight PRs target main at deploy time (high, deployment): one-time migration script.
- Branch protection requires admin pre-setup (high, deployment): documented one-time setup + Phase A preflight.
- Workflow rename breaks required-check reference (high, deployment): pinned dso.review.check_name config.
- SESSION_BRANCH resolution failure (critical, configuration): 3-step fallback (draft PR headRefName → vars.SPRINT_SESSION_ID → fail-fast, never silent default to main).
- dso.workflow=ci-pr unset silent local-mode fallback (medium, configuration): orchestrator warns when .sprint-active or .debug-active is set but dso.workflow != ci-pr.
- Empty integration scope (medium, configuration): job exits 0 cleanly.
- Direct-push commits unmapped by GitHub API (high, assumption): fail-closed; un-provenanced commits route into integration review.
- Squash on session→main collapses history (medium, assumption): documented choice in INSTALL.md; default merge-commit.
- Check-name drift between workflow and Ruleset (high, assumption): pinned config + Phase A preflight.
## Research Findings
### External Integration: GitHub Branch Protection / Rulesets API
- Trigger condition name: External integration
- Query summary: programmatic branch protection configuration, required permissions, merge-style interactions, modern Rulesets alternative

- Source URLs: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/branches/branch-protection, https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/available-rules-for-rulesets, https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/rules

- Key insight: Classic protection (PUT /branches/{branch}/protection) and Rulesets (POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/rulesets) both require admin permissions. required_linear_history=true BLOCKS merge commits — must be false on session-* so merge-commit PR-number references survive. Rulesets (2023+) are the recommended path for dynamic per-sprint branches due to pattern-based scoping (e.g., session-*) and per-session toggleability.
### Migration: Sub-Branch PR Base Re-Targeting
- Trigger condition name: Migration / compatibility
- Query summary: PATCH API for changing open PR base, CI re-trigger semantics, working migration examples
- Source URLs: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/pulls, https://github.com/heroku/main-branch-switch/blob/main/retarget.sh, https://github.com/ethomson/retarget_prs

- Key insight: PATCH /pulls/{n} with a base field retargets cleanly; GitHub recomputes the diff but CI workflows are NOT auto-re-triggered. The migration script must explicitly issue gh workflow run (or workflow_dispatch) after PATCHing the base to re-trigger required checks. Working examples exist; not a capability gap.
## Cross-Epic Interactions
- Resource: .github/workflows/ci.yml (llm-review job + general CI workflow)
Overlapping epics: b575-ac1c-f720-4839, c337-ed61, curly-mount-page, cf7b-86a9, flaw-beach-spice, clay-ditty-meld, 6add-c1fc, 0253-1cee-aa0d-4002, jira-dig-2366, cbea-3722, jira-dig-2371.

Interaction: This epic rewires the llm-review job (provenance verifier + narrow integration LLM review scope). The named epics modify the same job from different angles (arbiter step, provider abstraction, telemetry, quality gates, external-reviewer integration).
Gate: This epic exposes stable named steps (provenance, integration-review) in the llm-review job so other epics' additions compose cleanly; this epic does not assume exclusive ownership of the job.
- Resource: plugins/dso/skills/sprint/SKILL.md Phase F
Overlapping epics: 0cf2-42b5-8840-48a1, dso-fbky, jira-dig-2349, 70f6-05f1.

Interaction: This epic changes Phase F merge target (session vs main), merge-style enforcement, and trailer/branch-protection signal handling. Named epics modify Phase F's structure (refactor), execution-mode semantics (autonomous override), or its PR-handling tail.
Gate: This epic's Phase F edits MUST rebase cleanly on top of any refactor that landed earlier; later epic resolves merge conflicts via rebase.
- Resource: plugins/dso/skills/debug-everything/SKILL.md Phase F/G
Overlapping epics: 0cf2-42b5-8840-48a1, dso-fbky, jira-dig-2349.
Interaction: This epic converges debug-everything's ci-pr branch onto the same per-branch CI gate as sprint. Same coordination constraints from sprint Phase F apply.
Gate: Same as sprint Phase F gate, scoped to debug-everything.
- Resource: plugins/dso/scripts/merge-to-main-pr.sh (provenance + commit metadata)
Overlapping epics: jira-dig-2380.
Interaction: This epic adds PR-number cross-checks as one of three provenance signals on merge commits. jira-dig-2380 writes structured source-attribution metadata on commits.
Gate: Merge commit format MUST accommodate both PR-number provenance reference and source-attribution metadata as orthogonal fields without colliding.
- Resource: code review findings.json pipeline (consumed by replay regression harnesses)
Overlapping epics: astir-sill-twirl, balk-ozone-dip.
Interaction: This epic emits narrow integration LLM review findings on the session→main PR. The replay regression harnesses consume findings.json artifacts for drift detection.
Gate: Integration review writes output to the existing findings.json schema such that consumers do not require schema changes.
- Resource: dso:code-reviewer-* agent registry / dispatch
Overlapping epics: dso-8l5h.
Interaction: This epic's Per-Branch LLM Review uses the existing review-runner dispatch which consumes the dso:code-reviewer-* registry. dso-8l5h reshapes that registry.
Gate: Per-branch review dispatch MUST consume whatever shape the registry has at the time it lands; later epic adopts earlier epic's shape.
## Dependencies

coordinates_with: b575-ac1c-f720-4839, 0cf2-42b5-8840-48a1
supersedes (post-merge close): 8ee4-c51c-c546-4d4e, cafb-4b97-1703-41e3

content.text: ## Context

Placeholder epic capturing what we currently know about Nava Strata's Layer 4 — the "Deployable Microservices" tier of the Strata stack (Layer 1 infra templates, Layer 2 app templates, Layer 3 SDK, Layer 4 microservices). Each Layer 4 service is shipped as its own `strata-template-*` repo containing both an infra module and an app template, installable independently via `platform-cli`. This epic is NOT yet brainstormed; it is a durable capture so the work can be picked up in a future `/dso:brainstorm` session without re-doing the research.
## Layer 4 Service Catalog (as of 2026-05-07)

- **DocumentAI** — AI-powered document classification and extraction. Pilot stage. Stack: FastAPI + AWS Bedrock Data Automation (BDA). Repo: `navapbc/strata-template-documentai-api`. AWS-only; intentionally NOT built on Strata SDK or existing Strata app templates. Naming open question: "IDP" collides with "Identity Provider".

- **Rules Engine** — Eligibility and business rules engine. Pilot stage. Stack: Catala (Apache 2.0) transpiled to Python, served via FastAPI. Repo: `navapbc/strata-template-rules-engine-catala`. Targets means-tested benefit programs (SNAP, Medicaid, WIC, paid leave). Deliberately lightweight; rules editable by non-engineers.

- **QC Preview ("Intelligent Case Review Surface")** — Sidecar quality-review app for SNAP Payment Error Rate. Concept stage. No repo yet. Tied to HR1 SNAP deadline 2026-09-30. Surfaces "Case Criteria" (Status, Confidence, Explanation, Source references) over external case data ingested via batch or API.

- **Payments Service** — Beam-acquisition-derived payments microservice. Concept stage. No repo yet. Multi-provider design (JPMorgan, USIO); scheduling, recipients, funding sources, transaction tracking. Beam disbursed $400M as payment-provider-of-record pre-acquisition.

Common pattern across all four: each Layer 4 service ships as a `<service>-infra-module` (Terraform) plus a `<service>-app-template` (FastAPI / Rails / Next.js as appropriate), installable via `platform-cli`.
## Open questions to resolve in future brainstorm
- Should Layer 4 land as one umbrella epic or as separate per-service epics? Each service is at a different stage and stack.
- Does the AWS-only scope of DocumentAI (BDA) rule out Strata projects on Azure infrastructure? Implication for project-detection logic.
- Where does the Beam-derived Payments service land in the platform-cli lifecycle once it has a repo? Today it has no `strata-template-*` repo.
- How should DSO surface the microservice catalog and install workflow during prototype scaffolding (Epic A) — a single "want any Layer 4 services?" prompt, or deferred to Day-N iteration?
- Catala is currently the only rules-engine language; does future support for OpenFisca or JSON-based engines change DSO's planning context for the Rules Engine?
- The four services span wildly different maturity (Pilot vs. Concept) and stacks; DSO's planning context likely needs per-service detection rather than a single "Layer 4 enabled" flag.
- What is the intersection with Epic B (Strata SDK)? E.g., does an app using DocumentAI also typically use the SDK, or are they orthogonal?
## References
- https://www.navapbc.com/strata
- Layer 4 Confluence briefs (provided 2026-05-07): PLAT-DocumentAI, PLAT-Strata Rules Engine, PLAT-QC Preview, PLAT-Payments Service
- `navapbc/strata` (umbrella repo)
- `navapbc/strata-template-documentai-api`
- `navapbc/strata-template-rules-engine-catala`
- `navapbc/oscer` (real Strata-based app; reference customer for DocumentAI work)
- Related abandoned: `navapbc/strata-sdk-mcp` (research-only, not a dependency)
## Status
This epic is captured for future brainstorming. Do NOT plan or implement until `/dso:brainstorm <epic-id>` has been run interactively. Tagged `scrutiny:pending`.

content.text: ## Context

The DSO plugin emits telemetry events from code review pipelines but has no central data store — `classifier-telemetry.jsonl` and `review-event-schema.jsonl` exist as local-only files with no documented consumer. PR history is per-repo and not queryable across host projects. The umbrella `e7f3-2b45-8d7d-4c68` (grainy-speck-ball) requires a centralized telemetry pipeline supporting cross-reviewer comparison, downstream consumer epics (LAURA, replay-regression-harness, reporting), and zero-friction host-project participation.
This epic builds and deploys the **AWS-hosted, universal-endpoint** telemetry infrastructure plus the deterministic emit utility that downstream adapters consume.
## Scope
**In scope — AWS infrastructure (deployed via idempotent setup scripts using AWS CLI):**
- **Lambda Function URL** as the public POST endpoint (no API Gateway; built-in HTTPS)

- **Lambda function** (Python 3.13 runtime) — validates event JSON against the canonical schema, writes to S3 keyed `${client_id}/${YYYY-MM-DD}/${event_id}.jsonl`, returns 202 Accepted on success / 400 Bad Request on malformed

- **Lambda reserved-concurrency throttle** (default: 10 concurrent executions) — bounds blast radius from abuse / runaway loops. Lambda Function URL does not support direct WAFv2 association; reserved concurrency is the supported throttle mechanism.
- **S3 bucket** — append-only via per-event object writes (no true-append needed); per-client_id key prefix; public access blocked; bucket policy denying non-Lambda writes
- **IAM role for Lambda** — `s3:PutObject` on the bucket only (no read, no list, no delete; defense-in-depth)

- **S3 Lifecycle rule** — transition objects >90 days to **Glacier Instant Retrieval** (90-day minimum storage class). Provides cold-storage cost savings (~6×) while preserving millisecond retrieval for ad-hoc maintainer queries. Never delete by default.
- **CloudWatch log group** — Lambda execution logs at 7-day retention
- **AWS region**: `us-east-1`
**In scope — plugin-shipped CLI setup scripts** (under `plugins/dso/scripts/telemetry/`, idempotent, AWS CLI based):
- `aws-setup-bucket.sh` — creates S3 bucket + lifecycle rule (90d → Glacier IR) + bucket policy + public-access-block; re-runnable

- `aws-setup-lambda.sh` — creates Lambda + execution role + Function URL + reserved-concurrency configuration; re-runnable. **Pre-flight IAM permission check**: script verifies the operator has required IAM permissions (sts:GetCallerIdentity probe + dry-run create-role probe) BEFORE attempting any creation; exits with a clear error listing missing permissions rather than partial-creation state.

- `aws-deploy-handler.sh` — packages and updates Lambda handler code. **Pre-flight ordering check**: verifies the Lambda function exists before attempting update; if not, prints "Run aws-setup-lambda.sh first" and exits 1.
- `aws-status.sh` — reports endpoint URL, bucket name, lifecycle state, reserved-concurrency setting, last 24h event count
- `aws-teardown.sh` — clean uninstall; gated `--user-approved`
- Documented IAM permissions required for the operator running setup (in `plugins/dso/docs/telemetry/aws-setup.md`)
**In scope — `telemetry-emit.sh` utility** (deterministic adapter shim, no LLM cycles):
- Reads `telemetry.endpoint` + `telemetry.client_id` + `telemetry.emit_excerpts` from config (or `DSO_TELEMETRY_*` env vars)

- Generates UUIDv7 `event_id` via Python (`python3 -c "import uuid; print(uuid.uuid4())"` is the v1 implementation since UUIDv7 requires Python 3.13+; sufficient for our identifier needs); auto-populates all 11 common fields from environment (schema_version, event_type, client_id, tool_id, tool_version, timestamp, pr_number, commit_sha, cycle, language)

- Optional `--key <logical-id>` registers the event_id in `${ARTIFACTS_DIR}/event-id-map.json` for cross-event linkage. **Concurrent-write protection**: uses flock (or `mkdir`-based mutex fallback on systems without flock) to serialize event-id-map writes from parallel adapters.
- Optional `--link <key>` looks up event_id by logical-id, populates `finding_event_id` for resolver_outcome / arbiter_ruling events

- **Privacy enforcement with strict empty-string handling**: when `client_id == "dso-self"` AND `emit_excerpts` is unset/false, emit full cited_excerpt. When `client_id` is anything else (including empty string `""` treated as invalid input — error 400) AND `emit_excerpts != true`, strip cited_excerpt to null and emit `cited_excerpt_hash` only. Treat empty `client_id` as a hard error (exit 1 with clear message), not as a default-to-dso-self fallback.

- **Server-side defense-in-depth**: Lambda handler verifies the privacy invariant on every event — if `client_id != "dso-self"` and `cited_excerpt` is present, replace with null server-side before writing to S3. Two-layer enforcement protects against adapter-side bypass.
- Idempotency: maintains `${ARTIFACTS_DIR}/telemetry-submitted.log` keyed by event_id (and by `--key` when supplied); silently no-ops on duplicate
- Submission: curl POST with fail-open `|| true` semantics; logs warnings to stderr
- All adapters (Epic 4) consume this utility — single seam for endpoint logic
**In scope — canonical schema + minor upstream changes:**

- `plugins/dso/docs/contracts/telemetry-event-schema.md` — formal contract documenting 5 event types (`review_finding`, `resolver_outcome`, `arbiter_ruling`, `tool_finding`, `review_cycle`), schema_version=1, all common + per-type fields, defaults, **and the privacy disclosure**: a clearly-labeled section documenting that `telemetry.emit_excerpts=true` on the shared multi-tenant endpoint means verbatim code excerpts from the host project's PRs will be readable by the central-endpoint maintainer. Host project operators must affirmatively opt in to this data-sharing posture.
- Reviewer schema extension: add optional `rule_id` field to reviewer-findings.json in reviewer-base.md (non-breaking — existing findings without it still validate)

- Token-usage capture: tiny reviewer-dispatcher addition to write Anthropic API response `usage.input_tokens` + `usage.output_tokens` to `${ARTIFACTS_DIR}/review-cycle-usage.json` so the `review_cycle` emitter can populate `tokens_used` + `token_cost_usd`
**In scope — plugin config knobs (`dso-config.conf`):**
- `telemetry.endpoint` (default: ships pre-configured to the Joe-hosted Lambda Function URL)
- `telemetry.client_id` (default: `dso-self` for this repo; configurable per host project; empty string treated as hard error)
- `telemetry.emit_excerpts` (default: `false`; opt-in for verbatim sharing for non-dso-self clients; docs document the privacy implications)
**In scope — stats retrieval:**

- `plugins/dso/scripts/telemetry/query-stats.sh` — bash + AWS CLI + DuckDB; 5 validation subcommands: `roundtrip` (smoke test), `counts` (events per tool_id × event_type × day), `recent` (last N events), `missing` (clients silent for N days), `sizes` (bytes per client_id, cost monitoring). **Unknown-subcommand handling**: case-statement default branch prints usage to stderr and exits 1 (not 0).

- **DuckDB prerequisite**: setup docs list DuckDB CLI as required for queries (not auto-installed). Setup script `aws-status.sh` checks `command -v duckdb` and emits a clear install pointer if missing.

- **S3 scan latency mitigation**: query-stats.sh uses **client_id + date-range partitioning** in DuckDB glob patterns rather than full-bucket scans. Documented usage: `query-stats.sh counts --client-id=dso-self --days=7` runs against a 7-day prefix subset, not the entire bucket. Bounds object scan to recent partitions.
- `/dso:review-stats --source=central` skill flag — thin dispatcher to `query-stats.sh`
- Output is validation-grade only; full analytics/reporting deferred to `spiky-stand-chick` placeholder
**Operating model:**
- Joe-hosted AWS account for v1; universal endpoint URL shipped as the `telemetry.endpoint` default
- All DSO projects submit to the same endpoint (multi-tenant from day 1)
- Privacy: plugin-self emits full `cited_excerpt`; host projects emit `cited_excerpt_hash` only by default, can opt in via config (with disclosure)
- Write throttle: anonymous Function URL + Lambda reserved-concurrency cap (10 concurrent); no WAF (Lambda Function URLs don't support direct WAFv2 attachment)
- Read auth: maintainer AWS credentials on the S3 bucket
- Retention: forward-only; lifecycle to Glacier IR after 90 days; never delete by default
**Out of scope (delegated to sibling epics):**
- Telemetry adapters for individual tools (ruff, mypy, eslint, rubocop, etc.) — Epic `da4e-4e9a-250b-4a8b` (seat-oil-flank)
- `dso-llm` and `dso-resolver` emitter wiring into REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md and review-fix-dispatch.md — Epic `da4e-4e9a-250b-4a8b`
- External-reviewer comment ingest (CodeRabbit/Gitar/Copilot) — Epic `f27a-3c6a-1a4e-48ae` (turbid-maze-tread)
- Cycle-K arbiter consuming telemetry — Epic `b575-ac1c-f720-4839` (swap-maple-flyby); hard rule: arbiter reads from `gh api` only, never from this central store
- Full reporting/dashboard UI — placeholder epic `e8ac-6a65-62f6-47b8` (spiky-stand-chick)
- LAURA retrieval over defense corpus — placeholder epic `25b5-78e3-41b3-4ae9` (bland-bag-rind)
- Replay regression harness — placeholder epic `87b1-7fd0-edce-45d0` (balk-ozone-dip)
- Backfill of historical PR data (forward-only from deployment)
- Host-project deployments of their own AWS infrastructure (the design supports it; v1 ships only Joe-hosted)
- Detection of CloudFront-fronted WAF or alternative WAF strategies (rejected — Lambda reserved-concurrency is the v1 throttle)
## Approach

The S3 bucket layout is `s3://<bucket>/<client_id>/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<event_id>.jsonl` — one event per object. DuckDB reads these JSONL objects directly with `read_json_auto('s3://<bucket>/<client_id>/<date-prefix>*/*.jsonl')` using narrow date-range partitioning to bound scan latency. No dedicated query service (Athena/Glue/OpenSearch) needed at v1's volume (~6k events/month plugin-self, ~50 MB/month at 100× host adoption with hash-only emissions; storage envelope re-evaluated if cited_excerpt sizes drive volume past 1 GB/month).

Setup scripts are idempotent: each script begins with AWS resource pre-checks (`aws iam get-role || aws iam create-role` pattern) PLUS pre-flight permission checks (sts:GetCallerIdentity + dry-run probes) to fail fast with a clear missing-permission error rather than partial-creation state. Re-running on an already-provisioned account is a no-op (with the caveat that `aws-deploy-handler.sh` always re-uploads Lambda code regardless of content — Lambda metadata shows a new deployment timestamp on every run; documented in the script header).

The `telemetry-emit.sh` utility is the **only** seam adapters cross. Adapter authors populate type-specific fields; the utility owns event_id generation, HTTP, schema versioning, privacy policy, dedup, concurrent-write protection (flock on event-id-map.json), and fail-open semantics. The Lambda handler enforces the same privacy invariant server-side as defense-in-depth.
Field feasibility was audited (2026-05-14). All schema fields are obtainable from CI + local environments without expensive computation. Two small upstream changes are scoped into this epic:
- Add optional `rule_id` to reviewer-findings.json (reviewer-base.md edit)
- Capture Anthropic API `usage.*` to `${ARTIFACTS_DIR}/review-cycle-usage.json`
## Success Criteria

1. After running `aws-setup-bucket.sh && aws-setup-lambda.sh` against a configured AWS account, the following resources exist and pass an idempotency check (re-running is a no-op): S3 bucket with lifecycle rule (90d → Glacier IR) and public access blocked, Lambda function with Function URL configured, IAM execution role with `s3:PutObject` only, Lambda reserved-concurrency cap, CloudWatch log group with 7-day retention. Verifiable by running each setup script twice and observing no resource changes on the second run, plus `aws-status.sh` returning a JSON summary of all five resources.

2. The Lambda Function URL accepts a canonical event JSON POST and persists it as an S3 object keyed `${client_id}/${YYYY-MM-DD}/${event_id}.jsonl`. Verifiable by `query-stats.sh roundtrip` emitting a test event and observing the event in `aws s3 ls s3://<bucket>/<test-client-id>/`.

3. `telemetry-emit.sh` auto-populates all 11 common fields (schema_version, event_id, event_type, client_id, tool_id, tool_version, timestamp, pr_number, commit_sha, cycle, language) from environment + config, requiring only event-type-specific fields from the caller. Verifiable by invoking the utility with minimal args and observing a complete, schema-valid event in the bucket.

4. **Privacy policy is enforced at TWO layers** for defense-in-depth: (a) `telemetry-emit.sh` strips `cited_excerpt` to null at the adapter when `client_id != "dso-self"` AND `emit_excerpts != true`; (b) the Lambda handler verifies the same invariant server-side and replaces any non-conforming `cited_excerpt` with null before writing to S3. Verifiable by: emitting an event with `client_id=test-host-project --cited-excerpt "verbatim code"` and confirming the bucket record has null `cited_excerpt`; AND directly POSTing a malformed event with a non-self `client_id` and `cited_excerpt` populated and confirming the bucket record also has null `cited_excerpt` (server-side enforcement).

5. Failure of the telemetry endpoint never fails a caller: `telemetry-emit.sh` exits 0 (with a warning to stderr) even when the endpoint returns 5xx, times out, or is DNS-unreachable. Verifiable by pointing `telemetry.endpoint` at an invalid URL and observing the utility exits 0 plus the warning.

6. The canonical event schema is documented at `plugins/dso/docs/contracts/telemetry-event-schema.md` covering all 5 event types, schema_version=1, all 11 common fields, all per-type fields, defaults, the privacy policy, AND a clearly-labeled **Privacy Disclosure** section explaining that `telemetry.emit_excerpts=true` causes verbatim code to be readable by the central-endpoint maintainer. Verifiable by reading the contract document and confirming each section is present.

7. `query-stats.sh` provides 5 validation subcommands (`roundtrip`, `counts`, `recent`, `missing`, `sizes`) executing against the S3 bucket via AWS CLI + DuckDB with date-range partitioning. Unknown subcommand exits 1 with usage. `/dso:review-stats --source=central` dispatches `query-stats.sh`. Verifiable by running each subcommand against a populated bucket and confirming non-error output, plus running an unknown subcommand and confirming exit 1.

8. The reviewer-base.md schema includes an optional `rule_id` field for findings (non-breaking — pre-existing reviewer-findings.json fixtures without `rule_id` still validate). Verifiable by `grep -n 'rule_id' plugins/dso/docs/workflows/prompts/reviewer-base.md` matching the new field documentation and by running existing fixtures through schema validation without modification.

9. **SC9 (self-use, Probe-1 remediation, architecture-vs-evidence audit 2026-05-16):** During the d2f9 sprint, after AWS provisioning is complete, the reviewer-dispatcher emits a real telemetry event to the deployed endpoint and the event is observed landing in S3 — all before sprint close.
Verification (in-session, at sprint Phase I):

- At least one `/dso:review` run during the d2f9 sprint causes the reviewer-dispatcher to POST a real event payload to the deployed Lambda Function URL with a 2xx response (captured in sprint transcript).
- `aws s3 ls "s3://$(grep '^review_telemetry.bucket_name=' .claude/dso-config.conf | cut -d= -f2)/dso-self/$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)/" | wc -l` returns ≥1.

- The most recent object validates against the canonical schema: `aws s3 cp s3://<bucket>/<key> - | python3 -c "import json,jsonschema,sys; jsonschema.validate(json.load(sys.stdin), json.load(open('plugins/dso/docs/contracts/telemetry-event-schema.md')))"` exits 0 (schema reference adjusted to actual JSON schema artifact if different from .md).

10. **SC10 (AWS deployment verification, Probe-6 remediation):** Before the d2f9 sprint can be marked complete, the deployed AWS infrastructure is verified live via AWS CLI. The sprint cannot declare Phase I complete with any of the seven checks below failing. Concrete resource names MUST be written to `dso-config.conf` keys `review_telemetry.lambda_function_name`, `review_telemetry.iam_role_name`, `review_telemetry.bucket_name`, `review_telemetry.endpoint_url` by the `aws-setup-*.sh` scripts (SC1) and consumed by all verification commands below.
| Resource | In-session verification command | Expected result |
| Lambda Function URL | `aws lambda get-function-url-config --function-name $FN_NAME` | Returns 0; `FunctionUrl` populated |
| Lambda execution role | `aws iam get-role --role-name $ROLE_NAME` | Returns 0; trust policy lists `lambda.amazonaws.com` |
| S3 telemetry bucket | `aws s3api head-bucket --bucket $BUCKET_NAME` | Returns 0 |
| S3 bucket encryption | `aws s3api get-bucket-encryption --bucket $BUCKET_NAME` | Returns 0 with SSE configured |
| S3 lifecycle (retention) | `aws s3api get-bucket-lifecycle-configuration --bucket $BUCKET_NAME` | Returns 0 with documented 90d → Glacier IR rule (per SC1) |
| Lambda → S3 IAM permission | `aws iam simulate-principal-policy --policy-source-arn $ROLE_ARN --action-names s3:PutObject --resource-arns "arn:aws:s3:::$BUCKET_NAME/*"` | `EvalDecision=allowed` |

| End-to-end healthcheck | `curl -sf -X POST "$ENDPOINT_URL" -d '{"event":"healthcheck"}' && sleep 60 && aws s3 ls "s3://$BUCKET_NAME/dso-self/" \| grep -q .` | POST 2xx AND object visible within 60s |

Converts the audit's prose-only AWS dependencies into a structured in-session-verifiable contract that gates sprint closure. AWS CLI is available in the sprint environment, so these are all session-completable.
## Scenario Analysis
Surviving red-team scenarios (blue-team filtered; 10 of 14 retained):

- **(`critical`, `configuration`) telemetry.emit_excerpts=true on shared multi-tenant endpoint exposes verbatim code**: addressed by SC4's two-layer privacy enforcement (adapter strip + server-side defense-in-depth) and SC6's explicit Privacy Disclosure documentation.

- **(`high`, `runtime`) DuckDB S3 scan latency grows unbounded as object count increases**: addressed by date-range partitioning in `query-stats.sh` (SC7). Long-term mitigation: if bucket exceeds ~1M objects, introduce monthly-archive consolidation.
- **(`high`, `runtime`) event-id-map.json race under parallel adapter invocations**: addressed by flock-based mutex in telemetry-emit.sh.
- **(`high`, `deployment`) First deployment fails silently on incomplete IAM**: addressed by pre-flight IAM permission probe in setup scripts (sts:GetCallerIdentity + dry-run create-role).

- **(`high`, `configuration`) telemetry.client_id empty string bypasses privacy enforcement**: addressed by treating empty client_id as a hard error (exit 1 with clear message), not a default fallback.
- **(`high`, `assumption`) DuckDB available in operator's environment**: addressed by listing DuckDB as a prerequisite in setup docs + aws-status.sh prerequisite check.

- **(`high`, `assumption`) anonymous write access to Lambda Function URL acceptable**: now mitigated by Lambda reserved-concurrency cap (default 10) bounding blast radius from abuse; server-side schema validation rejects malformed events; documented as accepted-tradeoff in setup docs.
- **(`medium`, `deployment`) aws-deploy-handler.sh run before aws-setup-lambda.sh**: addressed by pre-flight existence check in aws-deploy-handler.sh.
- **(`medium`, `assumption`) ~50 MB/month at 100× adoption is stable upper bound**: addressed by documenting re-evaluation trigger if cited_excerpt sizes drive volume past 1 GB/month.
- **(`medium`, `assumption`) UUIDv7 generation in standard bash**: addressed by using Python uuid module (UUIDv4 sufficient for our identifier needs; ordering not required at v1).
Filtered (4 of 14):
- 2 WAF-related scenarios — WAF removed from architecture
- Lambda cold start — accepted tradeoff with || true fail-open
- query-stats.sh missing-subcommand — addressed by SC7 explicit handling
## Dependencies

None. This epic is foundational. Downstream epics consume its infrastructure: `swap-maple-flyby` (token-usage capture wiring for the arbiter), `turbid-maze-tread` (external-reviewer comment ingest emits to this endpoint), `seat-oil-flank` (adapter starter pack uses `telemetry-emit.sh`), `bland-bag-rind` / `balk-ozone-dip` / `spiky-stand-chick` (placeholders that consume the populated S3 bucket).
## External Dependencies
```yaml
external_dependencies:
- name: "AWS account with IAM credentials (account 820258254566)"
ownership: exists
handling: claude_auto
claude_has_access: yes
verification_command: "aws sts get-caller-identity > /dev/null 2>&1"
- name: "DuckDB CLI"
ownership: exists
handling: claude_auto
claude_has_access: yes
verification_command: "command -v duckdb > /dev/null 2>&1"
