content.text: ## Context

LLM test-writing sub-agents in this project (red-test-writer, sprint task-execution prompt, fix-bug RED phase) routinely produce tests that assert on internal method names, mock-invocation counts, or source-grep patterns rather than on observable system behavior. Research documents this failure mode: ~25% of LLM oracles are wrong-but-confident (Di Grazia et al. ASE 2025), 30-60% of LLM tests fail basic compile/execute floors (Yuan et al. 2024), and LLM tests show Assertion Roulette in 38-49% of class-level tests (Wang et al. 2024). The existing 5-rule behavioral-testing-standard.md describes correct principles but is too abstract to bind at generation time. This epic introduces a structured per-test intent-claim header that test-writers attach to every new or modified test, and extends the existing code-reviewer-test-quality agent with two review dimensions to enforce both assertion shape and articulation during code review. Pre-commit gating is deliberately out of scope — enforcement runs through the review overlay only, with iteration in the wild before any deterministic tooling is added.
## Success Criteria

- SC1: plugins/dso/skills/shared/prompts/behavioral-testing-standard.md gains Rule 6 — every NEW or MODIFIED test in the diff carries a fenced "## Test Intent" header above the test function with fields intent_id (SC|DoD|AC reference from parent ticket subtree, or "UNTRACKED — <one-line rationale>" permitted sentinel) and catches_regression_where (sentence-completion form: "this test turns RED if and only if [specific production-code change]"). Rule 6 includes canonical per-language header fixture examples covering Python (docstring with markdown fence inside), JavaScript/TypeScript (block comment with markdown fence inside), and bash (line-comment block with markdown fence inside). Legacy tests not modified in the diff are exempt.

- SC2: behavioral-testing-standard.md gains Rule 7 — when adding behavioral coverage for an intent_id already claimed by an existing test, add a sibling parameterized case or new sibling test function in the same test file. Do NOT append assertions to an existing test function. Do NOT create a duplicate test function claiming the same intent_id without an orthogonal scenario suffix. Each test function carries at most one "## Test Intent" header. behavioral-testing-standard.md is designated a safeguard file per CLAUDE.md rule 22 — sub-agents may not propose edits that weaken Rule 6 or 7 without explicit user approval.

- SC3: Three test-writing surfaces updated to reference Rules 6 and 7 in their generation guidance: plugins/dso/agents/red-test-writer.md, plugins/dso/skills/sprint/prompts/task-execution.md, and the fix-bug RED-phase prompt (concrete path under plugins/dso/skills/fix-bug/ resolved during implementation-plan). Synthetic verification: a dispatch of dso:red-test-writer against a fixture task containing one AC produces a test file whose header parses under the per-language syntax appendix and whose intent_id field exactly matches the fixture AC identifier; parse success is confirmed by an automated grep that finds the fenced "## Test Intent" block, the intent_id field, and the catches_regression_where field in the output.

- SC4: plugins/dso/docs/workflows/prompts/reviewer-delta-test-quality.md (the build source for the compiled plugins/dso/agents/code-reviewer-test-quality.md agent, regenerated via build-review-agents.sh) gains two new review dimensions. Tier 1 (assertion shape) emits a finding when a test assertion targets internal method names, private state, mock-invocation counts (e.g., mock.called_with), or source-grep patterns against source files; requires assertions to target observable outputs (return values, exit codes, file contents, side effects, emitted events). Tier 2 (articulation) emits a finding when (a) a new/modified test has missing or malformed header, (b) catches_regression_where is tautological, (c) the assertions do not exercise the intent named in intent_id (REQUIRED scaffold: reviewer first lists the observable artifact each assert measures, then lists what intent_id claims is measured, then flags if these two sets are disjoint), (d) catches_regression_where would not in fact cause the test to fail given the assertions present, (e) duplicate intent_id without orthogonal scenario suffix or sibling-case structure per Rule 7. Dimension carries an anti-sycophancy prime: "Identify the single most damaging flaw. If no flaw exists, state 'No findings' explicitly." The build pipeline regenerates code-reviewer-test-quality.md from this delta source as part of the implementation work.

- SC5: A /dso:review run against a synthetic diff containing (a) a new test with no header, (b) a new test asserting only on mock.called_with(...), (c) a new test whose intent_id claims SC-1 but whose only assertion is `assert True == True`, produces a reviewer-findings.json where the findings[] array includes at least one entry with dimension matching "Tier 1 (assertion shape)" or "Tier 2 (articulation)" AND whose source_path:source_line falls inside violations (a), (b), (c) respectively. The same findings[] array contains zero entries with those dimensions whose source_line falls inside any unmodified legacy test block in the same diff.
Each "5-rule" / "five rules" / "Rule 5" reference is updated to version-agnostic phrasing OR extended to enumerate Rules 6 and 7.
- SC7 (dogfood): The tests written for d566's own implementation carry valid Rule 6 headers. A /dso:review run on the d566 implementation PR emits zero Tier 1 or Tier 2 findings on those tests.

- SC8 (explicit descope): plugins/dso/hooks/pre-commit-test-quality-gate.sh and plugins/dso/hooks/semgrep-rules/test-anti-patterns.yaml are explicitly NOT extended by this epic. Rule 6 + Rule 7 enforcement is review-only via the dimensions added to code-reviewer-test-quality in SC4. If future evidence supports adding hook-level enforcement, a follow-on epic will scope it.
grep -rEni '5[-. ]?rule|five[-. ]?rules?|Rule[[:space:]]+5\b|behavioral[-. _]testing[-. _]standard'

Every match is triaged into one of three outcomes: (i) updated to version-agnostic phrasing or extended to reference Rules 6/7, (ii) explicitly descoped with a one-line rationale (e.g., "Rule 5 in this context refers to a different standard"), or (iii) already version-agnostic — no change required. The implementation PR description includes the full final grep output (count and list of matches) plus the triage disposition for each one (file path → outcome i/ii/iii with rationale where required). Pattern validation against the 14 consumers identified during brainstorm confirmed 100% coverage at brainstorm time; this SC ensures any consumer added between brainstorm and implementation is also caught.
## Approach

Inline rule additions to behavioral-testing-standard.md (Rule 6 + Rule 7 + per-language syntax appendix with canonical fixture examples). Prompt updates to three test-writing surfaces. Extension of reviewer-delta-test-quality.md (build source) — rebuild via build-review-agents.sh regenerates code-reviewer-test-quality.md. Pointer updates across the 10 named consumer files in SC6, plus structural sweep per SC9 to catch any unenumerated consumers. No new tooling, no new contracts, no new scripts.
## Scenario Analysis
- Fabricated tautological catches_regression_where (high/correctness): partially mitigated by Tier 2(b) and (d) reviewer checks; residual risk that the reviewer is itself LLM-judgment-based.
- intent_id collision across distinct scenarios sharing an abstract SC (high/correctness): partially mitigated by Rule 7 orthogonal-suffix requirement; "orthogonal" is reviewer judgment.

- Claim-vs-assertion contradiction degrades without manifest (critical/observability): partially mitigated by predicate-listing scaffold in Tier 2(c); semantic drift remains until 94ed-f55c manifest ships.
- Bash test header silent no-match in parser (high/runtime): partially mitigated by canonical per-language fixtures in SC1.
- LLM reviewer sycophancy on fluent headers (high/correctness): partially mitigated by anti-sycophancy prime; instructional primes are a known weak defense.
- Test rename orphans header (medium/configuration): unmitigated; deferred to 94ed/411b.
- Multiple tasks retroactively claim same test for different intent_ids (high/correctness): mitigated by one-header-per-function rule in SC2.
- Agent self-proposes Rule 6 relaxation (medium/configuration): mitigated by safeguard-file designation in SC2.
- Polyglot header embedding inconsistency (medium/runtime): partially mitigated by canonical fixtures.
## Research Findings

Three independent research dispatches during brainstorm surveyed academic literature, open-source tooling, and practitioner thought leaders on the question "at generation time, how do we know whether a candidate test would catch a real regression?" Convergent findings across all streams identified three signal tiers: Tier 1 (assertion shape — observable output vs internal name; cheap floor; 30–60% of LLM tests fail this per Yuan et al. 2024), Tier 2 (articulation — name the invariant and the plausible mutation; medium cost, LLM-friendly; cross-practitioner consensus from Khorikov, Beck, Bach/Bolton, Hughes/Wayne, Fowler), Tier 3 (empirical — mutant kill on the changed line; Meta TestGen-LLM 2025 mutation-guided pipeline; deferred to sibling epic 411b-a047). This epic implements Tiers 1 and 2 only.
## Dependencies

- a03c-d55e (Closure Checks schema migration) — required because intent_id under Rule 6 must reference end-state SC/DoD/AC, which a03c structurally separates from transitional Closure Checks via the new "## Closure Checks" template section and the updated verifiable-sc-check.md end-state-only rule. d566 owns the header schema; a03c's completion-verifier consumes Rule 6 headers for intent_id→test_artifact lookup. Sequential dependency, no conflict.

- 94ed-f55c (Plan-time intent allocation manifest) — required because Rule 6 intent_id field references manifest entries. d566 ships only after 94ed publishes the manifest schema and intent_id format.

- 7f42-e41f (suite growth metrics, sibling) — sequencing: d566 ships first; 7f42 builds on d566's header schema for its per-intent-item growth metrics. To avoid concurrent edits to behavioral-testing-standard.md, 7f42's brainstorm/implementation defers until d566 closes.
## Sibling Calibration Program
- 7f42-e41f: suite growth tracks behavioral coverage (Tier 1+2 metrics).
- 69e8-af39: feedback loop from production bugs and review findings into test-creation prompts.
- 411b-a047: mutation-testing infrastructure (Tier 3 empirical verification).
## Planning Intelligence Log
- Web research (Step 2 of scrutiny pipeline): not triggered — external research was performed at user request during Phase 1 dialogue, prior to Step 2 firing.
- Scenario analysis (Step 3): triggered (SCs ≥ 5); 12 red-team scenarios surfaced, 9 surviving after blue-team filter.

- Cross-epic scan (Step 2.25): triggered against a focused candidate set of 16 test/agent/review-related open epics. 1 ambiguity (a03c-d55e) resolved in Dependencies; 4 consideration signals on sibling/prereq epics; 1 benign signal on kudos.

- Bot-psychologist (Step 5): triggered (LLM-instruction signal: agent definitions + prompt templates). Findings folded into SC1, SC2, SC4 (catches_regression_where rename, UNTRACKED sentinel, predicate-listing scaffold, anti-sycophancy prime, sibling-case rule).

- Fidelity review (Step 4): Agent Clarity pass (5, 4), Value pass (4, 4), Scope (4, 4, 4, 3); consumer_completeness=3 finding structurally resolved by SC9 sweep. Reviewer anti-pattern incident filed as bug 270e-225f-6c72-4f0c.
- Scale context (Step 0): not applicable — development-time tool, per-test-author invocation.
- Session-signal override for complexity routing: success_criteria_count = 9 (≥ 7 threshold) AND scenario_survivor_count = 9 (close to 10 threshold) — routes to /dso:preplanning full mode.

content.text: ## Origin
Placeholder epic converted from bug 0551-3244 (feature request, not defect).
## Problem

Brainstorm and preplanning evaluate features at the capability level but do not surface operational coordination requirements — specifically, the pattern 'Script A creates/updates artifact X, but configuration file Y referencing X is not updated in the same atomic operation.' This gap produced a desync in epic 36a7-dbb5 (plugin release channels) where release.sh created tags + bumped plugin.json but did not update marketplace.json's source.ref in the same run.
## Analogous patterns
- Migration script adding a table without updating a schema registry
- Deployment script bumping a version without updating a manifest referencing it
- Installer adding a plugin entry without updating a required index file
## Proposed scope (not yet brainstormed)
- Operational atomicity check pattern added to brainstorm scrutiny pipeline or preplanning AC generation
- Red-team reviewer (dso:red-team-reviewer) is a candidate insertion point
- For any story touching a script that creates/modifies a versioned artifact, surface the question: 'Is there another file referencing this artifact that must be updated in the same operation?'
- If yes, require explicit AC: '<file> is updated atomically in the same script run/commit as <artifact>.'
## Status
Placeholder — requires /dso:brainstorm session before implementation. Tagged scrutiny:pending.

content.text: ## Context

The current `scripts/create-dso-app.sh` clones a hardcoded fork of Strata's NextJS template with DSO infrastructure baked into the fork's files. The fork is NextJS-only (precluding Strata SDK access, which is Rails-first) and detached from `platform-cli`'s install/upgrade lifecycle, so it drifts from upstream Strata over time. There's no way for a non-technical user to scaffold a Strata Rails+SDK+USWDS prototype with one command. This epic rewrites the installer to invoke `nava-platform app install` against upstream Strata templates (Rails default, pinned to v1.0.0), apply a DSO overlay, and deprecate the fork — using a phased script structure with extracted overlay engine and pre-implementation feasibility spike (already executed and recorded as a baseline at `tests/audits/A1-feasibility-spike-results.md`).
## In Scope

- Restructure `scripts/create-dso-app.sh` into six explicit phases: `parse-args` → `check-prereqs` → `invoke-platform-cli` → `apply-overlay` → `rails-sdk-add` → `emit-summary`. Each phase is a bash function; failures emit `[A1] phase=<name>` tagged errors and a "what to do next" hint.

- New shared script `plugins/dso/scripts/apply-host-overlay.sh` (the overlay engine): walks `plugins/dso/templates/host-project/`, applies `{{PROJECT_NAME}}` substitution per the existing installer convention, copies into target, leaves a one-line audit comment in dso-config.conf. Reusable beyond create-dso-app.sh.

- New in-plugin overlay tree `plugins/dso/templates/host-project/`: canonical DSO files (CLAUDE.md template, dso-config.conf, .pre-commit-config.yaml, project-understanding.md skeleton, design-notes.md skeleton, ARCH_ENFORCEMENT.md skeleton) with `{{PROJECT_NAME}}` placeholders matching the installer's substitution patterns.

- Ship `plugins/dso/scripts/lib/strata-config-defaults.conf` — shared canonical definition file mapping each Strata template variant to its `commands.*` values, Rails-Strata ARCH_ENFORCEMENT footguns, and Strata Posture section template. Single source of truth — sourced by A1's `apply-overlay` phase AND by A2's `prompts/strata/config-writes.md` + `arch-enforcement.md`. A1 MUST NOT independently define `commands.*` keys — sources from this file. A1 writes the FULL Posture section (not a skeleton) using install-time-known `_commit` and `_src_path`, so A2's onboarding-time idempotency check produces zero diffs.
- Tickets orphan-branch creation post-overlay; explicit `git push origin tickets` exit-code check; remote conflict surfaced with clear error and exit non-zero.

- CLI flags: `--app-name=<name>` (positional kept for back-compat plus added as flag), `--port=<num>` (default 3000), `--template=rails|nextjs|flask` (default rails), `--no-sdk` (skips Rails SDK gem add), `--no-overlay` (skips DSO overlay), `--auto-install-prereqs`, `--help`. Phase-tagged errors and recovery hints.

- Defensive guard against unknown Copier vars: at `check-prereqs`, parse upstream `copier.yml` at pinned commit hash (via `gh api`) and diff required-var list (name + type + accepted-values for enums) against hardcoded list in `plugins/dso/scripts/lib/strata-template-vars.sh` (where copier.yml is the source of truth and the hardcoded list is the script's coverage map). If any copier.yml-required var is NOT in the hardcoded list, fail fast with `[A1] copier.yml required var '<name>' not in --data list; update plugins/dso/scripts/lib/strata-template-vars.sh`. At `invoke-platform-cli`, hang detector (5s prompt-pattern + 60s no-output) as defense-in-depth.
- `nava-platform` install command pins to specific upstream tag/commit (per spike: v1.0.0 for `template-application-rails`); pinned ref documented in `strata-template-vars.sh`.

- Rails SDK gem-add (when `--template=rails` and not `--no-sdk`): single-line text-append of `gem "strata", github: "navapbc/strata-sdk-rails"` (gem name is `strata`, not `strata-sdk-rails`, per spike) to the generated `Gemfile`. Idempotent grep-before-append. No Ruby/bundler on host; user's first `make build` runs `bundle install` inside Docker.

- Project layout: `create-dso-app.sh my-prototype` flow creates `my-prototype/` as project root; runs `nava-platform app install --template-uri ... --version v1.0.0 --data app_name=app --data app_local_port=3000 . app` from inside `my-prototype/`. Result: `my-prototype/` is project root with DSO overlay (CLAUDE.md, dso-config.conf, ticket store dir, `.template-application-rails/app.yml`); `my-prototype/app/` is the Rails app. Canonical app subdirectory name: `app`.
- Overlay engine: collision-protection (refuses to overwrite by default; `--overlay-mode=skip|overwrite|merge` flag); binary-safety (text-extension whitelist + `file -b --mime` detection).

- Prereq install contract: OS matrix = macOS + Linux (Windows users directed to WSL2 via clear error). Package manager selection: macOS detects Homebrew (`brew install uv` if present, else `curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh`); Linux uses official `curl` installer. After uv installer runs, unconditionally `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"`; verify with `command -v nava-platform`; fail fast if not found. Failure semantics: prereq install failure aborts (no warn-and-continue). `--auto-install-prereqs` skips interactive confirmation; if NOT passed AND prompt would be required AND no TTY available, abort with `[A1] phase=check-prereqs no TTY for prereq prompt; pass --auto-install-prereqs for unattended`.
- Docker pre-flight check: detect Docker; emit clear pre-flight error if absent (with link to Docker Desktop install page). Docker is NOT auto-installed.
- `--app-name` validation: regex `^[a-z0-9\-_]+$` at parse-args; reject invalid names with clear error before any installation work.
- A1 MUST NOT write `commands.*` keys to `dso-config.conf` outside the shared-defaults file values — those values are A2's exclusive territory beyond the initial seeded set.

- Fork deprecation: `gh repo archive navapbc/digital-service-orchestra-nextjs-template --yes` (NOT `gh repo edit --archived=true`); idempotent per gh source. Sequencing: real-URL E2E test for new flow merged + green BEFORE fork archive commit; fork archive is final PR of the epic. Stderr redirected to log to avoid triggering surrounding error-handling.

- Update fork-URL references in source: `CLAUDE.md:56`, `plugins/dso/README.md:9`, `tests/scripts/test-create-dso-app-real-url.sh:11,33,34`, `docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md:270` (annotated `[deprecated; archived YYYY-MM-DD]`), `docs/onboarding.md:16`, `docs/designs/create-dso-app-template-contract.md` (rewritten), `docs/designs/dso-nextjs-starter-plugin-install.md:3`, `.github/workflows/template-real-url-e2e.yml:4`.

- Behavioral test extending the existing `test-create-dso-app-real-url.sh` opt-in pattern: scaffolds a Rails default, asserts the result has working app + USWDS + SDK gem in Gemfile + DSO overlay files + tickets orphan branch + post-build SDK functional check. Opt-in via `RUN_REAL_URL_E2E=1`; runs daily in CI.
## Out of Scope
- Infrastructure provisioning (`nava-platform infra install`) — future epic.
- Sample-feature scaffolding — Epic B / onboarding territory.
- Layer 4 microservices — Epic C (d08f-03d7-a148-43d0).
- Upstream contributions (`--no-input`, `--answers-file` for `platform-cli`; `gem "strata"` in upstream Rails template Gemfile) — filed as separate non-blocking tickets.
- Migration tooling for fork users — release-notes only.
- Retrofit-DSO-onto-existing-Strata-project tool — future epic that calls `apply-host-overlay.sh`.
- `commands.*` stack-conditional config writes beyond shared-defaults file values — Epic A2.
## Success Criteria

1. One-command Strata Rails+SDK+USWDS scaffold completes non-interactively. Non-technical user (Ruby NOT installed; uv NOT installed; Docker installed) runs `bash <(curl -fsSL .../create-dso-app.sh) my-prototype --auto-install-prereqs` and the script completes with exit zero and zero non-prerequisite interactive prompts. Result `my-prototype/` containing: (a) working Strata Rails app from upstream `template-application-rails@v1.0.0` (`make build` succeeds in Docker); (b) USWDS bundled (`@uswds/uswds@^3.7.1` in package.json); (c) `gem "strata", github: "navapbc/strata-sdk-rails"` present in Gemfile; (d) DSO overlay files with substituted PROJECT_NAME; (e) tickets orphan branch present + pushed if remote configured; (f) SDK functional check: post-build, `make rails-runner CMD='require "strata"; puts Strata::VERSION'` returns a non-empty version string. Additionally, the values written into `dso-config.conf`, `ARCH_ENFORCEMENT.md`, and `project-understanding.md`'s `## Strata Posture` section match what A2's `prompts/strata/*` sub-files would produce when run on the same scaffolded project state — verified by behavioral test asserting zero diffs in those three files. Verified by extending `tests/scripts/test-create-dso-app-real-url.sh`.

2. CLI flag variants produce documented outputs. `--template=nextjs` produces NextJS scaffold without SDK gem. `--template=flask` produces Flask scaffold without SDK gem. `--no-sdk` skips Gemfile append (verified by absence of gem line). `--no-overlay` produces clean upstream Strata scaffold without DSO overlay files. `--port=8080` propagates to upstream `app_local_port`. `--auto-install-prereqs` installs missing uv/nava-platform without prompting. All variants verified by behavioral tests.

3. Defensive guard fails fast at parse-time AND install-time. Parse-time test: synthetic upstream copier.yml with new required var → exit non-zero <10s with `[A1] copier.yml required var '<name>' not in --data list; update plugins/dso/scripts/lib/strata-template-vars.sh` BEFORE platform-cli invocation. Install-time test: simulated prompt-pattern in stderr → kill within 5s with same error class. No hung script in either path.

4. Overlay engine independently testable; collision-protected; binary-safe; idempotent. `apply-host-overlay.sh` invoked directly produces correct output; collision protection refuses overwrite by default; binary files (image/lock-file fixtures) NOT substituted; idempotent re-run (Gemfile dedup, no double-tickets-branch).

5. Fork archived after E2E test green; mechanical grep verification. Fork archive commit is the FINAL PR of the epic. CI for the fork-archive commit shows new E2E test passing. After landing: `gh api repos/navapbc/digital-service-orchestra-nextjs-template --jq .archived` returns `true`; fork README has redirect note; `git grep -l 'digital-service-orchestra-nextjs-template' HEAD -- ':!docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md'` returns zero matches; KNOWN-ISSUES entries annotated `[deprecated; archived YYYY-MM-DD]`.
## Scenario Analysis

11 surviving scenarios (red/blue team filter) all addressed via In Scope mitigations: nava-platform interactive hang protection (input redirect + hang detector); platform-cli version pinning; overlay collision detection (refuse overwrite by default); Gemfile idempotency (grep before append); tickets push exit-code handling; binary file safety in overlay (text-extension whitelist + MIME detection); uv prereq detection + offered install; real-URL E2E test updated BEFORE fork archive (sequencing constraint); --app-name regex validation; defensive guard upgrade (parse copier.yml at pinned hash AND install-time prompt detection).
## Approach

Phased script structure with extracted overlay engine. Defensive guard via hardcoded required-var lists pinned to upstream commit hashes (with copier.yml as source of truth, hardcoded list as coverage map — fail fast on divergence). Container-first Rails SDK installation (no host Ruby). Fork archived via `gh repo archive --yes`. Behavioral test via existing `test-create-dso-app-real-url.sh` opt-in pattern.
## Operational Constraints (Architecture-vs-Evidence Audit Remediation, 2026-05-18)
### Bypass Governance — --no-sdk / --no-overlay / --overlay-mode=overwrite (Probe-4 remediation)
These three flags bypass safety defaults (SDK gem add, DSO overlay, collision protection). The existing single-comment audit in dso-config.conf is upgraded to a structured governance pairing:

- **Audit log:** every invocation of create-dso-app.sh with any of the three flags writes a structured JSON line to `.dso/create-app-bypass.log` with `{timestamp, target_dir, flag, value, justification, operator_uid}`.

- **Required justification companion:** each flag MUST be accompanied by `--bypass-reason="..."` with non-empty content; create-dso-app.sh exits non-zero if a bypass flag is set without `--bypass-reason`. (Hard enforcement, not soft.)

- **Abuse-detection:** retro / debug-everything inspects `.dso/create-app-bypass.log` on every project entry; if the same operator+target_dir combination shows ≥3 bypass invocations within 30 days, surface a MUST-display warning ("bypass pattern detected; investigate") before allowing the next bypass invocation.

- **Verification (in-session, at sprint Phase I):** synthetic test invokes create-dso-app.sh with each of the three flags WITHOUT `--bypass-reason`; asserts non-zero exit + clear error. Then with `--bypass-reason="test"` succeeds; the log captures the entry.
### External-dependency verification (Probe-6 remediation)
Before Phase I:
| Resource | In-session verification | Expected |
| Docker present | `docker --version` | Returns 0 |

| Ruby presence detection works | `command -v ruby \|\| echo "absent"` AND create-dso-app.sh's preflight correctly handles both presence and absence | Test pass against host with Ruby uninstalled (synthetic) |
| uv presence detection works | Same pattern as Ruby | Same |
| `gh` auth + tickets-push remote | `gh auth status && git ls-remote --get-url tickets 2>/dev/null` | Both return 0 |
| `gh repo archive` accessible | `gh api /repos/$OWNER/$REPO --jq '.archived'` (read accessible) | Returns boolean (proves API access; archive operation itself is operator-confirmed) |

| Non-technical-operator host posture | Sprint runs the scaffolder against a fixture with `--mock-host-state=no-ruby,no-uv,docker` flag; asserts scaffolder produces correct guidance output (not a crash) | Test pass before sprint close |

Converts the audit's prose-only external dependencies into structured in-session checks. The "real non-technical operator running the scaffolder on a fresh machine" emergence is operational; the capability (correct preflight + guidance) is verified in-session.
## Dependencies

No upstream blockers. Soft external dependency on `nava-platform` upstream availability via uv-installable git URL pinned to specific tag/commit. Coordination with A2: A1's overlay seeds the FULL Strata Posture section + commands.* + footguns from `strata-config-defaults.conf` at install time; A2's onboarding sources the SAME file → idempotent re-write produces zero diffs (verified by behavioral test). A1 ships `strata-config-defaults.conf` as part of plugin filesystem (not host-project artifact), so A2 has access to it regardless of whether A1's installer was used. A2 declares dependency on A1 for the shared file. Optional follow-on (filed as non-blocking tickets): upstream contribution of `--no-input`/`--answers-file` to `platform-cli` would simplify A1's defensive guard; upstream inclusion of `gem "strata"` in `template-application-rails` would remove the post-install gem-add step.

content.text: ### 1. Technical Environment
* **Plugin/Tool Versions:** dso v1.17.17
* **Context Scope:** worktree-20260522-142331, epic d2f9-ee1a-48ab-4bf6
* **Active Configs:** APPROACH_RESOLUTION=autonomous, SPRINT_MODE=ci-pr
### 2. Incident Overview
* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior
#### Expected Behavior

Per `plugins/dso/skills/implementation-plan/SKILL.md` Step 3, the `dso:task-decomposer` agent emits task drafts whose `Verify:` commands are robust enough to (a) pass plan review on cycle 1 in the typical case and (b) actually succeed at task execution time. Per Step 4, the plan reviewer perspectives (Task Design, Completeness) should catch fragile or incorrect `Verify:` commands before tasks land. The combined system should not require 2-3 review cycles per story to scrub out the same categories of AC defect.
#### Actual Behavior

Across three sequential story impl-plans in a single session (35ee, b386, d94e — all in epic d2f9-ee1a-48ab-4bf6), the task-decomposer produced ACs with the **same categories of defect** repeatedly. Each story required 2 or 3 plan-review cycles to surface and fix these defects. After cycle-pass on d94e, gap analysis still found 5 more AC defects to amend. The recurring categories are:
1. **Substring false positives in grep/awk patterns** — e.g., AC-9 on d94e: `'cycle' in section_text` substring-matches `'review_cycle'`, making the field-presence check trivially pass.
2. **Shell-expansion leakage in Verify command strings** — e.g., b386 task-1 AC-6: `grep -E 'PATH=.*:$PATH'` had `$PATH` expanded by the shell before grep saw it; needed `\$PATH`.

3. **Wrong invocation signature for cited helper scripts** — e.g., 35ee AC-7 cycle 1: passed `validate-review-output.sh "$FIXTURE"` (1 arg) when the script requires `validate-review-output.sh <prompt-id> <output-file>` (2 args, exit 2 on usage error).

4. **Fixture files chosen without validating they work for the AC's purpose** — e.g., 35ee AC-7 cycle 2: used `tests/fixtures/ci-review-corpus/post-loop-findings.json` to assert non-breaking validation, but that fixture fails `code-review-dispatch` validation for unrelated reasons (missing `summary`, `category`, `file`, `cited_excerpt`), so the AC could never pass regardless of the change under test.

5. **Conflicting ACs without a resolution AC** — e.g., b386 task-1 cycle 1: AC-1 ("Unit tests pass — Universal") conflicted with AC-5 ("Test fails RED in isolation") because the required `.test-index` RED-marker AC was missing — neither AC alone signaled the dependency.

6. **Missing prerequisite-state ACs** — e.g., b386 task-1 cycle 1: no AC to add `.test-index` RED marker for the new source, so the pre-commit test gate would block the commit even though all other ACs pointed at a correctly-authored test.

7. **grep patterns too narrow for natural authoring formats** — e.g., d94e AC-5 cycle 1: `'schema_version[[:space:]]*=?[[:space:]]*1'` matches bare prose but NOT `"schema_version": 1` (JSON), `schema_version: 1` (YAML), or `| schema_version | 1 |` (markdown table) — all valid documentation forms.

8. **Wrong assertion target — prose vs structured artifact** — e.g., d94e AC-9 cycle 1: checked field name presence in section TEXT (prose) when DD-2 requires presence in a JSON example block; a section that mentions the field in prose but omits it from the JSON example trivially passed.

9. **No cardinality guards** — e.g., d94e AC-9 cycle 1: "all 5 event types have worked examples" was never asserted as "exactly 5 sections exist"; a doc with fewer sections could pass if the present sections were valid.

10. **Stale or future-only sibling references** — e.g., b386 cycle 1: task description cited `verify-aws-account.sh` as a pattern reference, but that file is created by sibling story ac57 which had not yet been implemented; the existing real sibling is `verify-session-provenance.sh`.

11. **Fragile awk range delimiters** — e.g., d94e AC-12/13 cycle 1: `/^##[[:space:]]+[^P]/` as section-end pattern was a negation that broke for any `## ` section starting with a `P` (e.g., a hypothetical `## Performance` after `## Privacy Disclosure`); the robust form is `/^## /` as the next-section anchor.
### 3. Action History and Workarounds
* **Steps Taken:**
* Story 35ee impl-plan: 3 plan-review cycles required (cycles 1, 2 failed on AC-7 variants; cycle 3 restructured AC-7 to a construction-based check that passed).
* Story b386 impl-plan: 2 plan-review cycles required (cycle 1 surfaced RED-marker absence + regex bugs + sibling reference; cycle 2 passed).
* Story d94e impl-plan: 2 plan-review cycles required (cycle 1 surfaced AC-5 narrowness + AC-9 substring/prose/cardinality/per-type defects + AC-12/13 awk fragility; cycle 2 passed).

* After d94e cycle 2 passed plan review, gap analysis surfaced **5 additional** AC defect categories in the same task — confirming the issue is systemic and not caught even by the cycle-2-passing review.

* **Known Workarounds:** Run the plan-review loop to its 3-cycle limit per story, then file gap-analysis amendments after. This is the current de facto workaround but it (a) doubles or triples planning time per story, (b) consumes opus/sonnet budget on the review loop, and (c) when the 3-cycle limit is hit on a stubborn story (35ee), the orchestrator presents a still-broken plan to the user.
### 4. Chronological Rationalization
* Initial reasoning during 35ee cycle 1: the task-decomposer is opus-level and should produce shippable ACs first try. The 3 review cycles needed felt anomalous.

* During b386 cycle 1: same defect categories surfaced (regex shell expansion, sibling reference accuracy). The repetition across distinct stories signals a systemic generation issue, not a per-story bug.

* During d94e cycle 1: same categories AGAIN (grep narrowness, substring vs structured-artifact assertion, cardinality). At this point the pattern is clear: the task-decomposer is not running an internal "would this Verify command actually work?" sanity check.

* Post-d94e gap analysis returning 5 more amendments confirms that plan review (Step 4) and gap analysis (Step 6) overlap in scope but neither has explicit anti-patterns for Verify-command robustness.
### 5. Skills and Workflows
* **Active Workflow:** `/dso:sprint` Phase B → `/dso:implementation-plan` (Steps 3–6)
* **Skills/Agents Involved:**
- `dso:task-decomposer` (opus) — generates the ACs at Step 3
- `dso:code-reviewer-*` / plan-review perspectives (sonnet) — review the ACs at Step 4
- Gap analysis opus sub-agent — Step 6 surfaces remaining defects
* **Reference files implicated:**
- `plugins/dso/agents/task-decomposer.md`
- `plugins/dso/skills/implementation-plan/docs/reviewers/plan/task-design.md`
- `plugins/dso/skills/implementation-plan/docs/reviewers/plan/completeness.md`
- `plugins/dso/docs/ACCEPTANCE-CRITERIA-LIBRARY.md`
- `plugins/dso/skills/implementation-plan/prompts/gap-analysis.md`
### 7. Additional Details

**Remediation surface** (do NOT remediate the specific tickets 35ee/b386/d94e — those plans are already fixed in-cycle and shipped). Remediate the planning skills/agents so future stories do not produce these defects:
1. **task-decomposer prompt** (`plugins/dso/agents/task-decomposer.md`): add an explicit anti-pattern checklist for Verify commands, including:
- Substring false-positives (word-boundary vs substring matching; quote JSON keys when checking presence in JSON)
- Shell expansion in single-quoted heredocs vs double-quoted (escape `$PATH`, `$?`, etc.)
- Helper script invocation: cite expected argv signature; cross-reference the helper's `--help` or first-line usage comment
- Fixture selection: require that the chosen fixture is independently valid for the AC's purpose, not just convenient
- Cardinality guards: when a DD names a count ("all 5 event types"), the AC MUST assert that count
- Format tolerance: when checking a documented value in a `.md` file, accept JSON, YAML, prose, and pipe-table forms unless one is mandated
- Awk range delimiters: prefer positive `/^## /` next-section anchors over negation patterns
- Prerequisite ACs: when a downstream Universal AC depends on a project mechanism (e.g., RED markers), include the mechanism-setup AC explicitly

2. **Plan-review reviewer perspectives** (`plugins/dso/skills/implementation-plan/docs/reviewers/plan/task-design.md` and `completeness.md`): add a dedicated dimension or rubric item for Verify-command robustness. Specifically scrutinize each AC's command for the 11 defect categories above.

3. **Gap-analysis prompt** (`plugins/dso/skills/implementation-plan/prompts/gap-analysis.md`): add a category for AC-Verify defects so gap analysis catches what plan review missed, rather than rediscovering category-1 issues at gap-analysis time.
4. **AC library** (`plugins/dso/docs/ACCEPTANCE-CRITERIA-LIBRARY.md`): add a "Common Verify-Command Anti-Patterns" appendix referenced by the task-decomposer.

5. **Sanity-check step** (optional, larger change): an inline `mktemp + apply mock content + run Verify` smoke loop in task-decomposer before emitting tasks, catching shell-expansion and substring-false-positive cases at generation time.

**Acceptance for remediation**: after the fix lands, a representative doc-only story (similar in shape to 35ee/d94e) and a representative RED→GREEN script story (similar to b386) should both pass plan review on cycle 1 with no AC defects from the 11 categories above. A test suite simulating these stories against the task-decomposer (or a corpus snapshot of the kind of ACs it produces) would prove the remediation.
**Out-of-scope for this bug**: do not edit tasks 41b8/2607/da20/4830 or their ACs. Those are already cycle-passed and ship-ready.

content.text: Incorporate concrete, measurable UI/UX constraints into DSO's design review process as hard enforcement — not soft suggestions.
## Reference: ui-ux-pro-max-skill
### Interaction timing as enforced constraints (not guidelines)
ui-ux-pro-max-skill treats these as hard constraints checkable in code review:
- Animation durations: 150-300ms with platform-native easing
- Tap/click feedback latency: 80-150ms (ripple/opacity/elevation)
- Touch targets: 44×44pt minimum (Apple HIG) / 48×48dp minimum (Material Design)
- Micro-interactions: 150-300ms
- prefers-reduced-motion: mandatory, not optional
### No emoji as icons — enforced professional quality signal

The skill explicitly bans emoji as UI icons and requires professional SVG icon libraries (Heroicons, Lucide, Phosphor, USWDS icons). This is treated as a concrete, automatable code quality signal — not a style preference.
## What to Add to DSO Design Review
1. Add measurable interaction timing constraints to the design review checklist — reviewer should flag animations outside 150-300ms, missing tap feedback, and touch targets below platform minimums
2. Add an automated check for emoji used as icons in UI code (detectable via regex/AST)
3. Add prefers-reduced-motion support as a required review dimension
4. Make these constraints configurable per project via dso-config.conf (e.g., design.animation_max_ms=300, design.touch_target_min=44)
5. Integrate into the completion verifier for UI stories — verify timing and icon constraints are met before story closure

content.text: Apply Token-Oriented Object Notation (TOON) encoding to structured data outputs that are consumed by LLM agents, reducing token usage by 30-60% on uniform tabular data.
## What is TOON

TOON (Token-Oriented Object Notation) is a compact serialization format that declares field names once as a header, then emits value-only rows. It is lossless — round-trips back to identical JSON. Benchmarked at 76.4% accuracy vs. JSON's 70.7% on retrieval tasks, with ~52% token reduction on uniform arrays.
Example — ticket list (before, JSON):
\`\`\`json

[{"ticket_id": "abc-1234", "ticket_type": "bug", "title": "Auth fails", "status": "open", "priority": 2}, {"ticket_id": "def-5678", "ticket_type": "epic", "title": "Add login", "status": "open", "priority": 1}]
After (TOON):
[2]{ticket_id,ticket_type,title,status,priority}:
abc-1234,bug,Auth fails,open,2
def-5678,epic,Add login,open,1
## Where to Apply
### 1. Ticket System Output
- \`ticket list\` — the primary candidate; returns uniform arrays of ticket objects with identical schemas. At scale (50+ tickets), JSON field name repetition wastes significant tokens.
- \`ticket deps\` — dependency graph output is tabular.
- \`ticket show\` — individual ticket display; less benefit (single object), but comments array could use TOON.
- Add a \`--format=toon\` flag to ticket CLI commands. Default remains JSON for backward compatibility; agents opt into TOON when injecting into prompts.
### 2. Test Results
- \`validate.sh --ci\` output — test pass/fail results are uniform arrays (test name, status, duration).
- \`test-batched.sh\` output — per-test results with runner, status, exit code.
- \`record-test-status.sh\` — test gate status records.
- Test results passed to sub-agents during TEST-FAILURE-DISPATCH are prime candidates — the sub-agent receives a list of failures with identical schema.
### 3. Script Outputs Consumed by Agents
- \`sprint-list-epics.sh\` — epic listing with uniform fields.
- \`review-complexity-classifier.sh\` — scoring output.
- \`issue-quality-check.sh\` — quality scores per ticket.
- \`enrich-file-impact.sh\` — file impact arrays.
- Any script whose output is interpolated into a sub-agent dispatch prompt.
## Implementation Approach
1. Add a TOON encoder utility (Python, minimal — the format is simple enough for a ~50-line function)
2. Add \`--format=toon|json\` flag to ticket CLI and key scripts
3. Update sub-agent dispatch prompts in sprint/debug-everything to request TOON format when passing structured data
4. Measure token savings on real ticket lists and test outputs to validate the 30-60% range for our data shapes
5. Do NOT apply TOON to prose/narrative content (descriptions, comments) — savings are negligible (<10%) on unstructured text
## What NOT to TOON-encode
- Skill instruction text (SKILL.md) — prose, not tabular
- CLAUDE.md content — prose
- Ticket descriptions and comments — unstructured text
- Error messages — human-readable prose
- Any output meant for human consumption (TOON is for agent-to-agent data transfer)
Reference: https://github.com/toon-format/spec (MIT, v3.0)

content.text: Add a /dso:doctor skill that performs a deterministic self-audit of the DSO plugin installation, producing a reproducible health score. Currently DSO validates code but does not validate the health of its own installation.
## Inspiration

everything-claude-code (131k stars) implements /harness-audit — a deterministic quality scoring tool that produces a reproducible baseline reliability score for the plugin installation itself, enabling regression detection when configurations change.
## What /dso:doctor Should Check
1. **Hook integrity** — all required hooks registered and functioning (pre-commit, PostToolUse, PreToolUse dispatchers)
2. **Ticket system health** — tickets branch mounted, worktree accessible, reducer functional, smoke test passes
3. **Config validity** — dso-config.conf parseable, required keys present, referenced paths exist
4. **Script availability** — all scripts in plugins/dso/scripts/ are executable and have required dependencies
5. **Skill registration** — all skills discoverable, SKILL.md files present and parseable
6. **Agent routing** — agent-routing.conf valid, all referenced agents exist in plugins/dso/agents/
7. **Test infrastructure** — .test-index valid, test directories exist, test gate functional
8. **Review gate** — review-gate-allowlist.conf valid, review-gate.sh and pre-commit-review-gate.sh functional
9. **Git hooks** — pre-commit hooks installed and matching expected versions
10. **Dependencies** — required external tools available (python3, ruff, etc.)
## Output
- Deterministic numeric health score (0-100)
- Per-category pass/warn/fail status
- Specific remediation instructions for each failure
- Score should be reproducible — same installation state always produces the same score
- Enable regression detection: run /dso:doctor after config changes to verify nothing broke
Reference: https://github.com/affaan-m/everything-claude-code

content.text: ## Context

The calibration program needs producer-side telemetry. Epic 2 (`d2f9-ee1a`, colder-fin-exile) ships the AWS Lambda endpoint, S3 store, and `telemetry-emit.sh` utility. Epic 1 (`b575-ac1c`, swap-maple-flyby) ships the cycle-end arbiter that writes per-finding rulings to the defense store. This epic delivers the producers: a tool-agnostic adapter framework, four first-party emitters, and a 12-adapter starter pack covering every tech stack DSO currently recognizes. Without these producers the S3 bucket stays empty and downstream consumer epics (LAURA `25b5-78e3`, replay-regression-harness `87b1-7fd0`, reporting `e8ac-6a65`) have nothing to read.

Direct user-visible value lands on day 1: host-project operators get a drop-in 12-adapter pattern they can install and immediately query via `query-stats.sh counts --client-id=<theirs>`; DSO plugin maintainers get 4 first-party emitter streams (review_finding, resolver_outcome, arbiter_ruling, review_cycle) for live dso-self calibration analysis.
## Approach

**Adapter framework.** Discovery by pure filename convention at `plugins/dso/scripts/telemetry-adapters/<tool_id>.sh` (plugin-shipped) with host-project REPLACE override at `.dso/telemetry-adapters/<tool_id>.sh` (host fully replaces plugin; no inheritance — upgrade burden documented in authoring contract). Edge cases: non-executable host file logs a warning and the plugin runs as fallback; syntax error in host file emits a canonical `adapter_error` event and the plugin does NOT run as fallback; symlinks resolved via `realpath` with cycle detection.
**First-party emitters (4).**

- `dso-llm` reads `reviewer-findings.json`; emits one `review_finding` event per finding; `--key dso-llm:<commit_sha>:<run_id>:<cycle>:<finding_index>` (excludes `github.run_attempt` so reruns of the same commit do NOT emit duplicates — Epic 2's `event-id-map.json` dedup suppresses the second emit).

- `dso-resolver` reads defense-store entries; wired into BOTH local REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md (`TrackerDefenseStore`) AND CI `review-fix-dispatch.md` (`GitHubPRDefenseStore`); emits `resolver_outcome` events with enum values `fixed | defended_accepted | defended_disputed | deferred_to_followup | dropped_by_arbiter`; uses `--link dso-llm:<commit_sha>:<run_id>:<cycle>:<finding_index>`; missing target emits `link_status=missing, finding_event_id=null` rather than blocking.

- `dso-arbiter` reads defense-store arbiter-ruling sub-schema (pinned in `plugins/dso/docs/contracts/review-defenses.md` with concrete field names: `arbiter.verdict`, `arbiter.severity_override`, `arbiter.rationale_excerpt`, `arbiter.cycle`, `arbiter.finding_index`); emits `arbiter_ruling` events with the same `--link` pattern. Epic 1's `code-reviewer-arbiter` agent does NOT call `telemetry-emit.sh` inline — this adapter is the sole emitter for arbiter_ruling events (see cross-epic boundary comment on Epic 1).

- `review_cycle` reads `${ARTIFACTS_DIR}/review-cycle-usage.json`; emits one `review_cycle` event per cycle summarizing findings/defenses counts, `review_tier`, `elapsed_ms`, `tokens_used`, `token_cost_usd`.

**12-adapter starter pack.** Python: `ruff`, `mypy`, `bandit`. Ruby/Rails: `rubocop`, `brakeman`. Ruby/Jekyll: `htmlproofer`. Node/TS: `eslint`, `tsc`. Go: `golangci-lint` (regex: `'golangci-lint has version ([0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+)'`). Rust: `cargo clippy`, `rustfmt` (regex: `'(rustfmt|clippy)[[:space:]]+([0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+)'`; clippy invoked as `cargo clippy --version`). Plus `sarif-to-canonical.sh` shared accelerator. Each adapter owns its own `--version` extraction with `"unknown"` fallback (per-adapter, no shared helper).

**sarif-to-canonical accelerator.** Reads minimal SARIF 2.1.0 Result fields: `ruleId`, `message.text`, `level`, `locations[0].physicalLocation.artifactLocation.uri`, `region.startLine`. Documented fallbacks:
- Missing `locations` → emit artifact-level finding with `line=0`.
- Structured `message.arguments` (no `message.text`) → serialize `arguments[0]`.
- Missing `level` → two-step lookup: first `runs[].tool.driver.rules[] | select(.id == $ruleId) | .defaultConfiguration.level`, then fall back to `"warning"`.
- `kind` field present without `level` → treat as `"warning"`.

**CI integration.** Each existing static-analysis CI job (ruff, mypy, ShellCheck, ESLint, etc.) appends a "post telemetry" step. Fail-open semantics: in-adapter `|| true` AND workflow `continue-on-error: true`. Paired heartbeat alarm: a daily `query-stats.sh counts --client-id=dso-self --hours=24` check fires an alarm if event volume is zero over the prior 24 hours.

**Adapter authoring contract** at `plugins/dso/docs/contracts/telemetry-adapter-authoring.md` covers: filename convention; REPLACE semantics + upgrade-burden callout (no inheritance — re-sync workflow documented); edge cases (non-executable, syntax error, symlink); `--key` naming pattern with `run_attempt` exclusion rule; tool_version extraction per-adapter responsibility + `unknown` fallback; fail-open + heartbeat; minimal SARIF subset + documented fallbacks (including the two-step `defaultConfiguration.level` lookup); ordering rule (host REPLACE precedence, deterministic per-tool_id ordering, idempotent re-runs).
## Cross-Epic Coordination

- **Producer-consumer to downstream placeholders** (LAURA `25b5-78e3`, replay-harness `87b1-7fd0`, reporting `e8ac-6a65`): canonical schema (owned by Epic 2) is the contract surface; consumer epics define their read patterns in their own brainstorms.

- **Pending-platform epics** (Java `70d5-37ee`, Terraform `jira-dig-1582`, Jenkins `jira-dig-1583`, .NET `ee22-4785`, Azure DevOps `622a-3955`): each ships its own adapters via the drop-in filename convention. This epic's authoring contract is the reference.
- **SARIF-emitting overlaps** (CodeQL `88d2-6756`, Semgrep `6add-c1fc`): both covered by `sarif-to-canonical` accelerator with documented fallbacks for known edge cases.
- **CI health gate** (`c337-ed61`): fail-open semantics MUST be paired with the zero-volume heartbeat (SC5) to avoid desensitizing CI health signals.
- **Architect tool-validation** (`f06e-9c43`): tool_version extraction logic in this epic's adapters must be updated when `f06e` changes tool invocations; coordination note in authoring contract.
- **Gemini provider** (`f9f8-a15c`): post-telemetry step must execute AFTER LLM review completion in CI workflow ordering.
- **Review severity anchoring** (`jira-dig-2568`): `review_cycle` event captures arbiter-anchored severity (event schema owned by Epic 2).
## Success Criteria

1. **Adapter discovery + REPLACE host override** works end-to-end including documented edge cases. Verifiable by `tests/scripts/test-adapter-discovery.sh` exercising: (a) plugin default invocation, (b) host REPLACE supersedes plugin, (c) non-executable host file logs warning + plugin runs, (d) syntax-error host file emits `adapter_error` and plugin does NOT run, (e) symlinked host file resolved via realpath. Each case asserts the documented outcome.

2. **All 4 first-party emitters** produce canonical events with `--link` cross-event linkage. Dangling `--link` emits `link_status=missing, finding_event_id=null` and does NOT block. Verifiable by running a representative review cycle and confirming via `query-stats.sh counts` that each event type appears with consistent linkage; separately by stubbing a dso-llm failure and asserting dso-resolver emits with `link_status=missing`.

3. **dso-resolver cross-store parity**: wired into BOTH local REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md (TrackerDefenseStore) AND CI `review-fix-dispatch.md` (GitHubPRDefenseStore); produces bit-identical canonical event shapes. Verifiable by `tests/scripts/test-resolver-store-parity.sh` exercising both stores against the same fixture and asserting field-level equality on all emitter-read fields.

4. **12 starter-pack adapters** emit schema-valid `tool_finding` events from representative fixtures with `tool_version` populated or `"unknown"` on extraction failure. `sarif-to-canonical` handles documented SARIF edge cases (missing locations, structured message, missing level via two-step `defaultConfiguration.level` lookup, `kind`-only). Verifiable by `tests/scripts/test-adapters.sh` + `tests/scripts/test-sarif-fallbacks.sh`.

5. **Telemetry adapter failure NEVER fails parent CI tool job**: both in-adapter `|| true` AND workflow `continue-on-error: true` apply. Paired heartbeat alarm fires on zero event volume in prior 24 hours via daily `query-stats.sh counts --client-id=dso-self --hours=24` check. Verifiable by (a) injecting broken adapter and confirming CI exits with tool's own exit code, (b) simulating zero-volume condition and confirming the heartbeat alarm fires.

6. **Adapter authoring contract doc** exists at `plugins/dso/docs/contracts/telemetry-adapter-authoring.md` covering: filename convention; REPLACE upgrade-burden callout + re-sync workflow; edge cases (non-executable, syntax error, symlinks); `--key` naming pattern with run_attempt exclusion rule; tool_version extraction per-adapter responsibility + `unknown` fallback; fail-open + heartbeat; minimal SARIF subset + documented fallbacks; ordering rule (host REPLACE precedence, deterministic per-tool_id ordering, idempotent re-runs). Verifiable by reading the doc and confirming each section is present.

7. **Adapter idempotency**: re-running an adapter against identical input produces exactly one canonical S3 event (Epic 2's event-id-map.json keyed by `--key` enforces dedup). Verifiable by `tests/scripts/test-adapter-idempotency.sh` running a representative adapter twice and asserting exactly one S3 event lands.

8. **dso-arbiter contract pinned** in `plugins/dso/docs/contracts/review-defenses.md` with concrete arbiter-ruling sub-schema fields (`arbiter.verdict`, `arbiter.severity_override`, `arbiter.rationale_excerpt`, `arbiter.cycle`, `arbiter.finding_index`). Verifiable by reading the contract doc + `tests/scripts/test-arbiter-contract.sh` loading a fixture defense-store entry and asserting dso-arbiter produces a schema-valid event.

9. **Adoption signal**: `query-stats.sh counts --group-by=stack,tool_id --days=7` reports event volume per (stack, tool_id) pair over the prior 7 days. Verifiable on demand by running the query against the populated S3 bucket and inspecting (a) dso-self emits non-zero events across all 4 emitter types within 24h of merge, and (b) per-stack adapter coverage breakdown.
## Operational Constraints (Architecture-vs-Evidence Audit Remediation, 2026-05-16)
### External-dependency verification at this epic's layer (Probe-6 remediation)
Before the da4e sprint can be marked complete, the four external dependencies inherited from Epic 2 (d2f9-ee1a) are verified live at this epic's layer (not deferred to the upstream link):
| Resource | In-session verification command | Expected |
| AWS credentials available | `aws sts get-caller-identity` | Returns 0; identity matches the configured maintainer principal |
| Epic 2 Lambda endpoint reachable | `curl -sf -X POST "$(grep '^review_telemetry.endpoint_url=' .claude/dso-config.conf | cut -d= -f2)" -d '{"event":"healthcheck"}'` | 2xx response |
| Epic 2 S3 bucket populated and readable | `aws s3 ls "s3://$(grep '^review_telemetry.bucket_name=' .claude/dso-config.conf | cut -d= -f2)/" \| wc -l` | ≥1 |
| DuckDB CLI present | `command -v duckdb && duckdb --version` | Returns 0; version recorded in sprint transcript |
| Heartbeat alarm scheduled | `gh workflow list --json name,state \| jq '[.[] \| select(.name \| test("heartbeat\|telemetry-heartbeat")) \| select(.state == "active")] \| length'` | ≥1 |

| SC9 dogfooding (24h freshness window): non-zero `dso-self` events across all 4 emitter types | `aws s3 ls "s3://$BUCKET/dso-self/$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)/" --recursive \| grep -cE 'review_outcome\|review_finding\|telemetry_event\|adapter_event'` (event-type names finalized in preplanning) | ≥4 distinct types |

Each row's ownership (operator who runs the check) and access (AWS CLI + gh CLI + DuckDB CLI, all available in the sprint environment) is implicit in the verification command. Converts the audit's prose-only external dependencies into structured in-session checks at this epic's layer rather than deferring to Epic 2's link.
## Dependencies
- `depends_on` Epic 2 (`d2f9-ee1a`, colder-fin-exile) — `telemetry-emit.sh`, canonical event schema, S3 bucket, `event-id-map.json` flock protection, `query-stats.sh`

content.text: ## Story S4: Stale-state auto-recovery + `--force` override with cmdline safety
### Description

**What**: When `test-run start` observes a state dir whose `pid` file is missing, or `kill -0` fails, or the cmdline snapshot mismatches, silently clear the state dir and proceed — no error, no user friction. When invoked with `--force`, unconditionally run the SIGTERM → grace → SIGKILL ladder on the recorded PID, but only after confirming the cmdline snapshot matches. If cmdline does not match, refuse with a clear error (guards against `--force` killing unrelated processes after PID reuse).

**Why**: Without auto-recovery, every orchestrator crash leaves a stuck state dir the user has to clear manually. `--force` is the legitimate "I really do want to restart my own run" path; without cmdline safety it becomes a gun pointed at the user's editor after PID reuse.
**Scope**:
- IN: stale-state auto-clear logic, `--force` flag + cmdline-verified termination, error messages for the `--force` refusal case
- OUT: duplicate-launch guard (S3), legacy harness removal (S6)
### Done Definitions
- When this story is complete, a state dir with a dead recorded PID is silently cleared and `test-run start` proceeds without requiring `--force`

← Satisfies: "when the launcher sees <state_dir> but <state_dir>/pid is missing, or kill -0 <pid> fails, or cmdline does not match the snapshot, the launcher silently clears the state dir and proceeds without requiring the override flag. No error, no agent friction"
- When this story is complete, `.claude/scripts/dso test-run start --force` terminates the recorded PID via SIGTERM → grace → SIGKILL and starts a new run
← Satisfies: "--force unconditionally terminates the recorded PID via the same SIGTERM→grace→SIGKILL ladder the kill subcommand uses"
- When this story is complete, `--force` on a state dir whose cmdline does not match the live process refuses with a clear error instead of sending signals to the unrelated process
← Satisfies: "refuses to kill a process whose cmdline does not match — returns a clear error"
- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic
### Considerations
- [Security] cmdline-verified kill prevents signalling an arbitrary process under PID reuse — covered by the same cmdline snapshot mechanism as S3
## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
