content.text: ## Description

**What**: New shared script plugins/dso/scripts/apply-host-overlay.sh (the overlay engine): walks plugins/dso/templates/host-project/, applies {{PROJECT_NAME}} substitution per existing installer convention, copies into target, leaves a one-line audit comment in dso-config.conf. Reusable beyond create-dso-app.sh. Ship the in-plugin overlay tree with canonical files (CLAUDE.md template, dso-config.conf, .pre-commit-config.yaml, project-understanding.md skeleton, design-notes.md skeleton, ARCH_ENFORCEMENT.md skeleton with {{PROJECT_NAME}} placeholders).
**Why**: Phased installer needs an extracted, independently-testable overlay engine; future retrofit-DSO-onto-existing-Strata-project tools will reuse it.
**Scope**:

- IN: apply-host-overlay.sh with text-extension whitelist + `file -b --mime` binary detection; collision-protection (--overlay-mode=skip|overwrite|merge default skip = refuse to overwrite); idempotent (re-run produces zero diff); audit comment written exactly once per dso-config.conf; in-plugin overlay tree under plugins/dso/templates/host-project/; full Strata Posture written from strata-config-defaults.conf at install time.
- OUT: Sourcing strata-config-defaults.conf from outside this engine (separate story); Rails SDK gem-add (separate story); fork archival (separate story).
## Done Definitions
- When complete, apply-host-overlay.sh invoked directly produces correct output against a target directory ← Satisfies: SC4
- When complete, collision-protection refuses to overwrite by default; --overlay-mode=overwrite/merge work as documented ← Satisfies: SC4
- When complete, binary fixtures (image, lock-file) are NOT substituted ← Satisfies: SC4
- When complete, idempotent re-run produces zero diff ← Satisfies: SC4
- When complete, the FULL Strata Posture section is written from strata-config-defaults.conf using install-time _commit + _src_path so A2's idempotency check produces zero diffs ← Satisfies: SC1
- When complete, unit tests written and passing for substitution, collision modes, binary detection, idempotency
## Considerations
- [Reliability] Audit comment must be detectable for idempotency; do not append duplicates
- [Maintainability] Overlay engine reused outside create-dso-app.sh — keep CLI surface minimal and stable
## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.

content.text: ## Context

Government services teams using DSO ship UI copy ad-hoc through feature-developing agents and developers. The result is inconsistent voice, varying empathy, and copy that often fails federal plain-language standards — citizens completing benefits applications, claims, and tax filings encounter confusing questions, jargon-laden instructions, and error messages that don't tell them what to do next. Hard-coding strings in UI compounds the problem: it blocks future localization, hides cross-page voice drift, and makes copy quality dependent on per-PR review discipline. The worst failure mode is silent — copy that ships and confuses users, violating HCD principles, with no failing test to flag it. The Plain Writing Act of 2010 makes plain language a legal requirement for federal agencies; USWDS, GOV.UK, VA.gov, and 18F publish detailed style canons addressing exactly this problem. None are currently encoded in any DSO sub-agent.
## Success Criteria

- For any DSO epic touching UI copy, /dso:brainstorm tags the epic copy-needed and writes a `## Copy Needs` section conforming to the schema at plugins/dso/docs/contracts/copy-needs-section.md; each item carries stable_id, type, location, page (controlled identifier), validation rule.

- Any epic carrying the copy-needed tag produces a dedicated copy story when /dso:preplanning runs — auto-created by the story-decomposer sub-agent and populated from Copy Needs. When distinct(page) > 1, the story includes a coordination-pass task.

- When dispatched in a copy story, the gov-copy-writer sub-agent (model: sonnet) produces a YAML copy artifact conforming to the schema at plugins/dso/docs/contracts/gov-copy-artifact.md at the project-configured location (copy/<epic-id>.yaml default; overridable via copy.artifact_dir in dso-config.conf; absolute paths and `..` segments rejected).

- The produced copy artifact's items each carry: values: { label, hint, errors{} }; structured rationale: { rule_ids[], conflicts[], deviations[{rule_id, reason}] }; checks: { fk_grade, banned_words_found, active_voice } computed by deterministic post-processing (NOT LLM self-attestation).
- Coordination-pass receives the full first-pass rationale. Items whose rationale.rule_ids cites a hard-constraint canon rule (errors, validation, legal disclosures) cannot be mutated.

- The federal style canon — rules from USWDS forms, GOV.UK error/form patterns, VA.gov error anatomy, 18F content guide, Federal Plain Language Guidelines, and CDC reading-level guidance — ships as entries in the reference library corpus (epic 0b7c-d811), retrievable via ref-query.sh; gov-copy-writer loads relevant entries top-K by relevance (K ≤ 20) on dispatch and applies the documented precedence ladder (canon-rule > Copy Needs constraint > Users archetype > design-notes voice).

- Per-item closing condition: fk_grade ≤ 8, banned_words_found empty, active_voice = true for ≥ 95% of items in the produced artifact. Items below threshold are flagged in rationale.deviations with documented reason.

- Synthetic dogfood closing-session validation: run gov-copy-writer against a representative bad-copy example with intentionally jargon-laden questions, blame-language errors, and vague hints; before/after acceptance bar — average fk_grade decreases by ≥ 1 grade level, active_voice rate increases by ≥ 20 percentage points, banned_words_found count drops to 0.
## Dependencies

Depends on epic 0b7c-d811 (Add searchable UI/UX design knowledge base as a reference library) — provides the corpus schema, ref-query.sh retrieval contract with top-K + relevance scoring, and the canon-entry storage. 0b7c-d811's priority is raised to P0 as part of this epic's bookkeeping, and an SC is added to 0b7c-d811 requiring the federal-style-canon entries to be included.

Relates to: aaa1-7100 (Brainstorm UX understanding loop — same Phase 1.5 surface; future brainstorm coordinates with the copy-needed probe established here), 1048-67d0 (Preplanning UX reference injection — same story-decomposer surface), jira-dig-2569 (Add a Cleanup Story for every epic during preplanning — shared auto-created-story pattern).
## Approach

Add a sonnet-tier gov-copy-writer sub-agent that loads federal-style-canon entries from epic 0b7c-d811's reference library via ref-query.sh (top-K by relevance, K ≤ 20) with a documented canon-source precedence ladder, structured rationale schema, and deterministic post-processing for the checks block (no LLM self-attestation). Brainstorm Phase 1.5 detects UI-copy needs and tags the epic plus writes a formally-schema'd Copy Needs section; preplanning's story-decomposer auto-creates the copy story; multi-page stories include a conditional coordination-pass that respects hard-constraint canon rules.
## State Lifecycle
| Variable | CREATE | UPDATE | CONSUME | RETIRE |
| copy-needed epic tag | /dso:brainstorm Phase 1.5 when copy needs detected | n/a (additive) | /dso:preplanning story-decomposer | n/a — durable; persists with the epic |

| copy.artifact_dir config key | /dso:onboarding per consuming project (optional; default copy/) | Operator edit | /dso:sprint task-dispatch passes path to gov-copy-writer | When consuming project is decommissioned |

| Copy artifact `<copy_dir>/<epic-id>.yaml` | gov-copy-writer first-pass dispatch | gov-copy-writer coordination-pass (multi-page only) | Implementation-story application code | Manual deletion when epic reverted |

content.text: ## Bug Report
**Priority**: 3 (normal)
**Zero Inference Rule**: Directly observed in diff for PR #337 by FP-recovery opus review.
## Observed behavior

check-corpus-schema.py loads a single schema from the corpus_dir argument and reuses it for every recursively-discovered .yaml file. When the hook runs against the top-level ui-reference/ directory, only _schema.yaml is loaded; principles/_schema.yaml and _schema-anti-patterns.yaml are skipped via _SKIP_NAMES and their narrower vocabularies / additional required fields are never enforced.
## Expected behavior
Per-subdirectory schemas (_schema-anti-patterns.yaml etc.) are either enforced for their subdomain or documented as informational-only.
## Fix
Option A: Update the validator to walk per-subdirectory schemas (like check-corpus-schema.sh does for single-file invocations).
Option B: Delete the unused subdirectory schemas and document that the parent schema is authoritative.
Option C: Add a comment to each per-subdirectory schema marking it as informational-only.

content.text: ## Mode Precondition

This epic applies only when enforcement.strategy=ci AND merge.strategy=pr AND a remote is present (verified by git remote get-url origin). At sprint Phase A, the orchestrator detects mode and emits exactly one of two banners: "MODE: ci-pr" (epic mechanisms active) or "MODE: local — per-story PR mechanisms inactive" (existing local workflow unchanged, no breakage). Local-mode parity is filed as a follow-on epic with this scope: TrackerDefenseStore per-story SHA-range support, in-session /dso:review story-close trigger, local Strategy E equivalent, shared pre-merge validation, dual-mode trailer linking.
## Glossary
- session worktree: Claude Code working directory for a sprint
- session branch: git branch checked out there, source of the long-lived draft PR
- story branch: story/<ticket-id> forked from session branch at story dispatch
- Phase A/E/F/I: sprint orchestration phases (Init / Task Dispatch / Post-Batch Processing / Primary Ticket Closure)
- Strategy A: per-story PR + size-gate (this epic)
- Strategy E: region-split FALLBACK for oversized review surfaces
- hash-of-record: diff_hash + SHA range recorded with each attestation, defining the exact range covered
- long-lived draft PR: single draft PR (session→main) opened at Phase A and refreshed across all stories
- claim-fingerprint: SHA-256 of lowercased, whitespace-normalized claim text
- SPRINT_SESSION_ID: sprint-init-generated UUID; written to .sprint-active marker file at Phase A and exposed to CI as a repository variable (vars.SPRINT_SESSION_ID) refreshed by a Phase A step
- sprint-active state: presence of .sprint-active marker file in artifacts dir; created Phase A, removed Phase I
## Context

Today's review pipeline becomes unreliable on large PRs. Empirical PR data on this project since 2026-04-27 (~50 merged) shows every >2-cycle PR was ≥500 LOC and ≥10 files; PR #37 at ~4000 LOC escalated to user with "findings have not converged." Published research (SmartBear/Cisco, Microsoft Research, Google eng-practices) converges on ~200–400 LOC as the reliability cliff. Review-pipeline-side hardening (closed epic 6da2-4cff) addressed reviewer calibration but not surface area. The lever is splitting review into per-story increments on a single long-lived draft PR (Strategy A), with attestation accumulating across stories so the final epic→main merge re-reviews only the unattested delta.

The current /dso:sprint workflow harvests per-task worktrees back to a shared session worktree without per-story isolation, batches mix tasks from multiple stories, and observed reality is that some sub-agents write directly to the session worktree despite worktree.isolation_enabled=true — no leakage detector exists today. This epic adds story-isolated branches with deterministic trailer-based attribution (composing on top of hard dependency 170b-2ac9, which delivers the git-trailer injection library, the DSO-Story/DSO-Task/DSO-Epic trailer schema, and the attribution.enabled config gate), restricts session-worktree commits to merges, fires CI llm-review per-story push against a draft PR pre-created at sprint init, and routes oversized story deltas through a true region-split FALLBACK path (Strategy E) — the current FALLBACK passes the whole diff to one reviewer.
## Success Criteria

1. Mode detection and ci-pr gating: At Phase A, sprint orchestrator detects mode and emits a banner. Local-mode users see "MODE: local — per-story PR mechanisms inactive" and proceed with existing workflow unchanged. ci-pr-mode users see "MODE: ci-pr" and continue with Phase A draft PR creation. Verification: integration test with mocked git remote get-url returning empty asserts banner is "MODE: local" and no gh pr create invocation occurs; with remote present + ci-pr config asserts "MODE: ci-pr" and PR creation proceeds.

2. Story-isolated branches with merge gating (ci-pr mode only): Sprint creates story/<id> per dispatched story; merges into session branch only after that story's CI llm-review attests passed; orphan trailer commits route to story/orphan-<sprint-session-id>. Verification: post-sprint validation script asserts (a) git branch --list story/* shows exactly one branch per dispatched story plus optionally the orphan branch; (b) git log --merges <session-branch> shows one merge commit per story containing a DSO-Story trailer matching the story ID; (c) no non-merge commit appears on the session branch between story merges.

3. Mandatory DSO-Story trailer with explicit --message injection (ci-pr mode only): Sprint-mode commits via /dso:commit carry a DSO-Story (or routed orphan) trailer; session-branch merges constructed by the orchestrator using git merge --no-ff --message=<msg-with-trailer> so trailers survive on every merge SHA. Pre-commit hook validates trailer presence and rejects commits without a DSO trailer. Verification: (a) trailer-less commit rejected with documented error; (b) integration test asserts git interpret-trailers --parse <merge-sha> returns the DSO-Story line on every story-merge SHA; (c) test outside sprint mode with attribution.enabled=false asserts no enforcement.

4. Session-worktree merge-only policy and deterministic leakage handling (ci-pr mode only): Pre-commit hook scoped to sprint-active state via .sprint-active marker file (created Phase A, removed Phase I). Hook accepts merge commits and rejects all non-merge commits with a clear error directing the user to a story worktree. Escape hatch: setting DSO_SPRINT_ACTIVE=0 env var bypasses the hook for emergency commits with an audit log entry. The release pipeline (merge-to-main.sh) operates outside sprint-active state so its non-merge commits are accepted. When a non-merge commit lands on the session branch (bypassing the hook), the post-Phase-F leakage detector cherry-picks it onto the branch named by its DSO-Story trailer; orphan trailers route to story/orphan-<sprint-session-id>; missing-trailer commits cause sprint to hard-fail with a manual-attribution prompt; closed-story-trailer commits hard-fail with named recovery options (rebase-and-retag with git rebase -i and manual trailer edit, or --force-route-to=<story-id> override flag); cherry-pick conflicts trigger git cherry-pick --abort and emit a hard-fail with the conflicting commit SHA and named conflicting paths. Verification: 5 test cases covering each path including the closed-story-recovery flag exercise.

5. Long-lived draft PR with per-story CI review and region-split FALLBACK (ci-pr mode only): At Phase A the orchestrator opens a draft PR via gh pr create --draft, completing before any story-branch dispatch in Phase E (PR creation is a Phase A blocking step, not concurrent with Phase E push triggers). The merge-to-main-pr.sh "refuse if open PR exists" guard is amended to "refuse if non-draft PR exists" — draft PRs are expected for the long-lived pattern. A new workflow file fires CI llm-review on every push to story/* branches, scoped to merge-base(session, story/<branch>)..story/<branch>, with concurrency-group keyed ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-${{ vars.SPRINT_SESSION_ID }} (using vars context per GitHub Actions docs — env is not allowed in concurrency expressions). The PR-scoped GitHubPRDefenseStore is active from day one. When a story-branch delta exceeds 400 LOC or 15 files, the HUGE-diff FALLBACK path activates true region-split review: file-clustered regions reviewed in parallel by tier-appropriate reviewers, findings deduplicated on (file, line-range, dimension, claim-fingerprint) with line-range overlap matching (not exact-match), conflicting severities resolved to MAX, both rationales preserved as a merged-rationale field when severities differ (no silent rationale discard), opus arch synthesis pass for boundary-only issues. Verification: 5 test cases including overlapping-region fixture asserting dedup with MAX-severity and dual-rationale preservation, and second-push assertion that DefenseStore returns prior attestations on the same story branch.

6. Hash-of-record protocol (ci-pr mode only): Each attestation records the diff_hash at the time of attestation plus the SHA range it covers (story-branch tip SHA, story-branch base SHA). DefenseStore.load_for_region validates by SHA-range membership, not by diff_hash equality alone. Merge commits do not invalidate attestations whose covered SHA range is preserved in the merge ancestry. Verification: integration test merges story A into the session branch, then queries DefenseStore for story A's attestations from a final-PR-context session and asserts the attestations are returned (not stale-invalidated).

7. Bug 4724-41a7 fix as Phase 1 prerequisite (applies to all modes): Resolution of bug 4724-41a7 (Claude Code creates sub-agent worktrees from main repo HEAD instead of session HEAD when orchestrator is in a session worktree) ships as Phase 1 of this epic, before any story-branch infrastructure depends on it. Regression test: dispatching a sub-agent from a session worktree with worktree.isolation_enabled=true produces a sub-agent worktree whose base SHA equals the session HEAD SHA, not the main HEAD SHA. Verification: regression test runs at every CI invocation thereafter.

8. Validation acceptance with inline value-signal (ci-pr mode only): A validation sprint of at least 1500 total changed LOC across at least 3 stories runs the entire pipeline end-to-end and lands one final PR to main. Mechanical proxies: (a) the long-lived draft PR exists from Phase A; (b) every story merge into the session branch carries a DSO-Story trailer readable by git interpret-trailers; (c) each story-branch CI run produces a reviewer-findings.json and writes to GitHubPRDefenseStore; (d) on the final PR ready-for-review transition, DefenseStore.load_for_region returns attestations covering each merged story branch; (e) the leakage detector test suite passes 5-case matrix. Inline value-signal assertion: re-reviewed-LOC / total-LOC < 50% (loose falsifiable threshold to confirm the mechanism reduces re-review surface). The headline "<15% LOC re-reviewed" target is filed as a follow-on observability ticket with continuous tracking via the sprint summary log.
## Scenario Analysis
Surviving high-confidence scenarios from Red Team + Blue Team filter, each addressed by an SC or risk mitigation:
- Cherry-pick conflicts on shared-file leaked commits (critical, runtime) — addressed by SC4 hard-fail with abort + named conflict paths.
- Hash-rewriting cascade across task→story→session merges (critical, runtime) — addressed by SC6 hash-of-record protocol with SHA-range membership lookup.
- DSO-Story trailer points to deleted/closed story (high, runtime) — addressed by SC4 named-recovery options (rebase-and-retag or --force-route-to override).
- Region-split cross-boundary findings rationale loss (high, runtime) — addressed by SC5 dual-rationale preservation.
- Pre-commit hook rejects merge-to-main-pr.sh's own non-merge commits (high, runtime) — addressed by SC4 sprint-active-scoped hook + non-sprint-mode release pipeline.
- CI rate-limit exhaustion under parallel story-push storm (high, runtime) — addressed by SC5 concurrency-group keying via vars.SPRINT_SESSION_ID.
- attribution.enabled=false bypass route (high, configuration) — addressed by SC3 sprint-mode override of project config.
- merge-to-main-pr.sh refuse-if-open-PR guard conflicts with single-long-lived-draft-PR pattern (high, deployment) — addressed by SC5 guard amendment to non-draft-only.
- DefenseStore PR-keyed empty for non-PR refs (critical, runtime) — addressed by SC5 pre-create draft PR at Phase A so PR-scoped store is active from day one.
- Bug 4724-41a7 cascade if unresolved (critical, deployment) — addressed by SC7 phasing as Phase 1 prerequisite.
- Phase A PR-creation race vs first push (medium, runtime) — addressed by SC5 explicit ordering: PR creation blocks Phase E dispatch.
- Sprint-active escape hatch ambiguity (medium, configuration) — addressed by SC4 .sprint-active marker file + DSO_SPRINT_ACTIVE=0 env override with audit logging.
- Story-branch cleanup race vs in-flight CI (medium, runtime) — addressed by branch retention until Phase I (no mid-sprint cleanup).
- Orphan-trailer branch unbounded growth (medium, deployment) — bounded by sprint-session scope; ephemeral, cleared at Phase I; documented as known limitation.
## Dependencies

- Hard: 170b-2ac9 (Commit-level source attribution via git-native trailers) must reach closed before this epic enters sprint. Provides DSO-Task/DSO-Story/DSO-Epic trailer infrastructure and attribution.enabled config gate.
- Hard: dbbc-cf67-8cfc-4b4d (Stateful re-review with arbitration) ships DefenseStore.load_for_region() with the no-op default; this epic depends on the interface and activates real region loading.
- Closed prerequisite: 6da2-4cff-ff38-4056 (review-reliability hardening).

- Subsumes: 1083-fb3d (PR-based merge) — this epic absorbs PR-creation scope including the long-lived draft PR pattern. Phase 0 step: ticket list-descendants 1083-fb3d; close as superseded or re-parent each child under this epic before sprint kickoff.
- Disambiguation gate (Phase 0): e407-d35c (possible duplicate of 170b-2ac9) — must be closed-as-duplicate or scoped-as-distinct before sprint kickoff.
- Boundary cross-references:
- vs 70f6-05f1 (worktree isolation parallel review): this epic owns story-branch naming and merge-only restriction; that epic owns clash detection.
- vs 6d90-93d5 (Conventional Commits enforcement): this epic owns post-commit CI region-split dedup; that epic owns pre-commit Conventional Commits format.
- vs 7575-5a90 (static-analysis defense): independent attestation lookups; no shared store mutation.
- vs 4911-c7ba (reviewer rubric expansion): reviewer agent interface must reach stable contract before Phase 4 wires the per-story CI review.
## Approach
One-shot delivery with phased internal ordering enforced via inter-story dependency declarations during preplanning:
- Phase 0 (sprint init): resolve 1083-fb3d descendants and e407-d35c disambiguation gate.
- Phase 1: bug 4724-41a7 fix (foundation; all later phases depend on it).
- Phase 2: trailer enforcement + sprint-active marker + session-worktree merge-only hook + Phase A mode-detection banner.
- Phase 3: story branches + leakage cherry-pick + long-lived draft PR (subsumes 1083-fb3d's PR-creation work).

- Phase 4: CI workflow on story/* push (using vars.SPRINT_SESSION_ID) + DefenseStore region activation + Strategy E region-split FALLBACK with file-clustering, parallel reviewers, line-range-overlap dedup, MAX-severity reconciliation with dual-rationale preservation, and opus arch synthesis pass.
- Phase 5: hash-of-record protocol with SHA-range membership attestation lookup.
## Risk Mitigations
- R1 trailer injection (SC3 explicit --message construction)
- R2 PR-keyed defense (SC5 pre-create draft PR at Phase A)
- R3 hash cascade (SC6 hash-of-record + SHA-range lookup)
- R4 cherry-pick conflicts (SC4 abort + named conflict paths)
- R5 PR guard conflict (SC5 amendment to non-draft-only)
- R6 4724-41a7 cascade (SC7 phasing as Phase 1)
- R7 CI concurrency context (SC5 vars.SPRINT_SESSION_ID, not env)
- R8 mode scoping (SC1 banner + ci-pr precondition)
- R9 deleted-story recovery (SC4 named recovery options)
- R10 cross-boundary rationale loss (SC5 dual-rationale preservation)
### Planning Intelligence Log

- Web research (Step 2.6): triggered. Bright-line conditions fired: External integration (GitHub Actions trigger semantics, gh CLI draft-PR creation, git interpret-trailers behavior on merge commits, GitHub stacked-PR community patterns); Novel architectural pattern (incremental review attestation across long-lived branch). Key findings: SmartBear/Cisco 200-400 LOC reliability cliff; Kubernetes/Gatsby/Mozilla single-PR incremental review patterns; GitLab MR 77758 trailer-on-merge fragility; GitHub Actions concurrency env-context restriction.
- Scenario analysis (Step 2.75): triggered (≥5 SCs + integration signals — full mode). 14 surviving scenarios after Blue Team filter, all addressed by SCs or documented as known limitations.
- Practitioner-requested additional cycles: 1 — local-enforcement / direct-merge / no-remote red team → spec scoped to ci-pr mode only with follow-on epic for local-mode parity.
- Follow-on scrutiny (Step 0): not triggered (epic is the originating brainstorm; prior follow-ons resolved).

- Feasibility resolution (Step 2.5): triggered (4 specialist re-review cycles); critical capability gap on git-interpret-trailers-on-merge resolved via SC3 explicit --message construction; integration_risk on env-context concurrency resolved via SC5 vars.SPRINT_SESSION_ID.

- LLM-instruction signal (Step 5): triggered — keywords: skill file modifications (sprint SKILL.md), hook behavioral logic (pre-commit hooks). Bot-psychologist deferred to implementation-plan stage where actual prompt drafts exist.

- Scale context (Step 0): empirical (~5 PRs/week, 20-25% currently exceed 400 LOC threshold); not inferred. Strategy E region-split activation threshold pinned at 400 LOC / 15 files per SmartBear research.

DIG-4702.summary: Per-Story PR Review Structure with Incremental Attestation

content.text: ## Context

After story 20d7-09d6-b831-4c3a deleted .github/workflows/per-branch-review.yml (epic b575), the project's PR/review workflow has degraded in compounding ways. The DSO maintainer running /dso:sprint and /dso:debug-everything fights a manual battle for every epic merge: ci.yml:llm-review is gated base_ref == 'main' so PRs whose base is a session branch receive no internal LLM review. Session-to-main reviews fail closed on cumulative diffs above ~6000 lines (LLM returns non-JSON, schema correction exhausts). Multiple workflows (ci-python-skills.yml, portability-smoke.yml, mirror-defenses-to-pr, 6+ others to audit) silently skip sub-PRs. .test-index RED markers can reach main. Version-bump commits land directly on main outside the PR (breaks subsequent git pull origin main). Worktree cleanup closes active PRs mid-CI. Three downstream epics (cf7b-86a9, f27a-3c6a, fb32-215c) are blocked.
## Success Criteria

- SC1 — Per-sub-PR LLM review + provenance-narrowed integration review + re-keyed cycle ledger and DefenseStore. Every per-story PR (sprint) and per-batch PR (debug-everything) triggers an internal LLM review via a new .github/workflows/review-sub-pr.yml workflow. The branches: filter targets the PR's BASE branch matching session/**, session-**, session_**, bug-batch/** (story PRs are pushed FROM story/... TO session branch; batch PRs are pushed FROM bug-batch/... to session or main — base-ref filter is the correct primitive). The cycle ledger AND DefenseStore are both keyed by (pr_number, commit_sha); migration contract specifies v1.1.0-to-v1.2.0 sentinel-pr_number rule for existing entries (old commit_sha-only entries match against any pr_number until the next review cycle re-keys them); a contract test reads a v1.1.0 entry and asserts no data loss in v1.2.0 emission. Integration review at session-to-main (ci.yml:llm-review) reuses the existing verify-session-provenance.sh logic: exit 0 → skip LLM dispatch with explicit covered-by-sub-PR-reviews liveness assertion (check-run conclusion skipped + summary message listing covered sub-PR numbers and SHAs); exit 1 (unprovenanced) or exit 2 (budget-exhausted) → keep current full-diff path. A contract test ships with this epic locking the verifier's 0/1/2 exit-code semantics. Verification: the epic's own sprint demonstrates per-story sub-PR review firing AND a synthetic test exercises a 6000+ line all-provenanced session-to-main PR that completes without LLM dispatch.

- SC2 — Runner gracefully degrades on oversized PRs via pre-filter + file-level chunking + LLM aggregation pass + visibility trailer. Pre-filter uses .gitattributes linguist tags (linguist-generated, linguist-vendored, linguist-documentation) PLUS additive configurable ignore.glob / ignore.regex overrides. ignore.glob ships with a non-empty default value (lockfile patterns at minimum: **/package-lock.json, **/yarn.lock, **/poetry.lock, **/go.sum); both max_files and max_calls validate non-zero at config load with a warning on zero. File-level chunking EXTENDS the existing per-directory region-split (Strategy E in region_split.py) with finer-grain per-file dispatch for oversized single-file or single-directory clusters, preserving the file-atomicity invariant (single file is NEVER split across reviewers). An LLM aggregation pass synthesizes cross-file findings before posting. The aggregated PR comment includes a visibility trailer listing every file reviewed and every file skipped with skip reason. A hard upper bound max_files × max_calls routes to admin/FP-recovery via a distinct OVER_BOUND status (NOT FP-suspected) — /dso:fp-recovery rejects PRs with OVER_BOUND status, preserving FP-recovery's signal integrity. Verification: synthetic 7000+ line direct PR with mixed reviewable/ignored files produces aggregated findings with visibility trailer; the LLM never receives the full diff; a 200-file synthetic PR routes to admin/FP-recovery without silent passing.

- SC3 — Every CI gate on path to main fires per (PR, SHA); cross-workflow check naming is consistent. All workflows currently gated base_ref=='main' or pull_request: branches: [main] are audited; their pull_request branch filters are EXTENDED (additive, not narrowed) to cover session/**, session-**, session_**, bug-batch/** base refs OR an always-runs umbrella job is added so the required-check name remains stable across branches that may skip the conditional inner job. Behavioral test test-no-duplicate-checks-per-sha.sh queries the GitHub Actions runs API, groups workflow_run entries by (head_sha, check_suite_id), selects the entry with the highest run_attempt, and asserts uniqueness of check-context names across those latest-attempt entries (re-runs after failure are out-of-scope). Verification: behavioral test passes against a fixture run of the epic's own sprint; RED state on a duplicate-check fixture fails as expected.

- SC4 — Merge pipeline correctness — RED tests blocked + version-bump in PR + worktree cleanup safety with 3 guards. (a) A required CI check scans .test-index for unresolved RED markers and blocks session-to-main merge if any are present; named under an umbrella job for stable branch-protection. (b) merge-to-main-pr.sh commits the version-bump on the source branch's HEAD before merge; the S5 story includes the explicit design decision (bump-before-final-review vs. bump-after-final-review-accepting-re-review-dismissal) documented in the ticket. (c) claude-safe (in agent-batch-lifecycle.sh) and harvest-worktree.sh refuse to remove a worktree when ANY of: (i) the branch has an open PR with CI in flight; (ii) the worktree has uncommitted or unpushed changes; (iii) the branch is in a protected list (main, master, develop, release/*). --force bypass prints which guard fired and the PR URL when applicable. The open-PR check uses a 3-tier fallback chain: (1) gh pr list --head <branch>, (2) gh api repos/.../commits/<sha>/pulls, (3) for fork PRs missed by both, gh pr list --search 'head:<branch>' or equivalent. S1's spike validates the tier-2 reliability for pre-merge session-branch SHAs; if it fails, tier-3 is promoted. Verification: (a) attempted RED-marker push to main is blocked; (b) sub-PR commit history shows version-bump on source branch; (c) cleanup-against-open-PR test refuses without --force and names which guard fired.

- SC5 — Epic execution discipline — verifiable from commit history. (a) The first story (S1) is a hard blocker for S2-S7 AND its Definition of Done requires: (i) a manual dso:code-reviewer-standard (opus) review of S1's own sub-PR with reviewer-findings.json attached and zero unresolved critical/important findings; (ii) two spike outcomes documented in the S1 ticket comment — the branches: filter base-ref semantics confirmed by a minimal test workflow, AND the SHA-based PR lookup reliability for non-default-branch commits confirmed (or the 3rd-tier fallback promoted). (b) All stories use /dso:sprint orchestration only — no /dso:fix-bug invocations. (c) Modifications are additive in the behavior-preservation sense: existing CI/review workflows and scripts may NOT be deleted; pull_request branch filters MAY be extended to additional base refs (broadening, not narrowing); existing inline gating may have provenance-aware skip paths added INSIDE (preserving original main-base coverage). Verification: epic-close audit confirms all three sub-conditions with an explicit files-touched + behavior-preservation-rule-applied checklist attached to the epic-close comment.
## Dependencies
None blocking. Depends on b575's cycle ledger (already merged via PR #232).
Blocked by this epic (unblocked on merge): cf7b-86a9, f27a-3c6a, fb32-215c.
## Approach

content.text: Add a /dso:next skill that reads current project state and automatically routes to the correct next action — no arguments, no confirmation dialogs, zero friction.
## Reference: get-shit-done /gsd:next

get-shit-done (47k stars) implements /gsd:next as a zero-friction auto-router that reads STATE.md and applies 8 conditional routing rules to advance automatically. It is the most-used command in the framework because it eliminates the cognitive overhead of remembering which skill to invoke next.
## Routing Rules for /dso:next
The skill reads ticket state, git state, and validation state, then routes based on conditional rules (evaluated in order, first match wins):
| # | Condition | Action |
| 1 | Open P0 bugs exist | Route to /dso:fix-bug on highest-priority bug |
| 2 | Epic exists with no stories | Route to /dso:preplanning on the epic |
| 3 | Epic exists with scrutiny:pending tag | Route to /dso:brainstorm on the epic |
| 4 | Stories exist with no implementation tasks | Route to /dso:implementation-plan on the story |
| 5 | Open tasks exist ready for implementation | Route to /dso:sprint on the parent epic |
| 6 | All tasks complete, stories open | Route to story closure verification |
| 7 | All stories complete, epic open | Route to epic closure verification |
| 8 | No open work | Report "nothing to do" with suggestion to create new work |
## Design Principles
- **Zero arguments** — reads all state from tickets + git, never asks the user what to do next
- **No confirmation** — routes immediately, explaining what it chose and why in one line
- **Idempotent** — running /dso:next twice in the same state produces the same routing
- **Transparent** — always states which rule matched and what it will do before doing it
- **Composable** — can be chained: after completing a task, the user just runs /dso:next again
## State Sources
- .claude/scripts/dso ticket list — open tickets, priorities, types, parent relationships
- git status — uncommitted changes, current branch
- Validation state — whether validate.sh has passed recently
- Review state — whether a review is pending
## What This Is NOT
- Not a replacement for /dso:sprint (which orchestrates full epic execution with sub-agents)
- Not autonomous — it routes to the next skill, it doesn't execute a loop
- The user stays in control: /dso:next suggests and starts, user can interrupt or redirect

content.text: ## Incident Overview
**This is a META-PROCESS bug, NOT a request to fix the 1000-issue ceiling.**

Epic 4047 (Derivable level-triggered Jira reconciler) shipped a hardcoded 1000-issue ceiling at `plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/fetcher.py:26` (`_ACLI_CEILING = 1000`). The ceiling represents the maximum size of the Jira working set the bridge can process before it must give up. When production runs against the actual DIG project on 2026-05-26, the fetcher immediately raises `SilentTruncationError(reason="ceiling")` and the reconciler cannot make progress at all — the gate is correct, but its threshold was never matched against operational reality.

The bug is that this threshold was specified in a planning document, written into acceptance criteria, implemented mechanically, reviewed by multiple code reviewers, attestation-passed by completion-verifier, AND merged to main — without ANY step in that pipeline asking the load-bearing question: **how many open DIG issues exist today, and is 1000 enough headroom?**
## What was missed
**1. Planning (brainstorm + preplanning + implementation-plan) never verified the value against reality.**
- Epic 4047 story 10e3 description states: "Silent-truncation detector at 1000-issue hard ceiling." The DD enshrines `>= 1000` as the trigger threshold.
- Task 71d4 ("GREEN: refactor fetcher.py to generator + truncation gate + dedup") encodes `cumulative len(snapshot) >= 1000` as an acceptance criterion verbatim.

- Neither brainstorm scrutiny, preplanning red-team review, nor implementation-plan researched the operational size of the DIG working set (issue: `project = DIG AND resolution = Unresolved` returns N issues — N was never queried).

- No reference is recorded for where 1000 came from. Plausible candidates: \"feels round\", \"ACLI default page size limit (which is actually 100)\", or \"JRACLOUD-94632 mention\" — but the citation is not in the epic, the story, or the task.
**2. Implementation gap-analysis lowered the safety bar instead of escalating.**

The task description originally specified using ACLI's `total` / `isLast` / `pageToken` to confirm the working set was bounded. Gap-analysis discovered (comment on task 71d4 at 1779661955030826000): \"plugins/dso/scripts/acli-integration.py:752-796 shows search_issues(jql, start_at, max_results) returns a plain list slice (list[dict]) — NO total field, NO isLast field, NO pageToken returned.\"

The correct response would have been to trigger the implementation-plan→brainstorm escape path (REPLAN_ESCALATE) — \"the canonical detection mechanism we planned for does not exist on this ACLI surface; we need to revisit how truncation is detected before continuing.\" Instead, the gap-analysis amended the AC to a weaker heuristic (\"infer from page size\") and proceeded. The 1000 ceiling was retained without re-justification.
**3. Code review did not flag the magic number.**

PRs #353, #357, #359, #361 (the four-PR series for story 10e3) and the eventual squash to main passed multiple code review cycles. None of them flagged `_ACLI_CEILING = 1000` as a magic number requiring (a) a citation, (b) a config override, or (c) empirical justification against the deployment environment.
**4. Completion-verifier passed the story closure without a live-environment check.**

Story 10e3 closed P1=PASS. The story's DDs were structurally satisfied (the gate exists, the gate raises, the unit tests pass). No DD was written to require \"the ceiling has been validated against the actual DIG project size\" — and so the verifier had nothing to verify against. This is a verifier-rubric gap, not a verifier failure: validation-class success criteria for operational thresholds are not part of the current verifier protocol.
**5. Epic 4047 closure under VALIDATION-CLASS semantics deferred the check to the operator — but the operator was us.**

The epic's LIVE-VERIFIED success criteria were marked deferred-to-operator. When the operator (this sprint session) ran the dry-run reconcile pass on 2026-05-26, the ceiling fired on the very first attempt. The deferral was a fig leaf — there was never going to be a separate, dedicated operator review independent of the sprint, and so deferring the check effectively meant skipping it.
## Failure it's causing
Reconciler workflow run 26430060327 (dry-run, main @ HEAD ${HEAD_SHA}, mode=dry-run):
ERROR: reconcile_once raised: ACLI working set reached the 1000-issue ceiling (JRACLOUD-94632 silent truncation)
Process completed with exit code 1.

The reconciler cannot run, even in dry-run mode, against the live DIG project. Every scheduled and dispatched run since the 1788 fix merged has hit this same wall. The bridge is non-functional end-to-end.
## What this bug IS NOT

- This is NOT a request to raise the ceiling to 2000, implement pagination beyond the ACLI limit, narrow the JQL, or shard by component. Those are remediations for the fetcher; this bug is about the process that allowed the fetcher to ship with an unverified threshold.
## What this bug IS

A process defect spanning brainstorm scrutiny, preplanning red-team, implementation-plan gap-analysis, code review, completion-verifier rubric, and validation-class epic deferral. The remediation is a planning/sprint-process change so that future ceilings, thresholds, and operational constants:
1. Carry a citation OR a measurement at planning time.
2. Are surfaced explicitly in the brainstorm tradeoff-research step (\"is this value verified against the deployment environment?\").

3. Trigger REPLAN_ESCALATE in implementation when discovered to lack a verified upstream basis (this is the documented escape path; story 10e3 did not use it when gap-analysis surfaced the ACLI API mismatch).
4. Are recognized as a verifier rubric category — validation-class \"value is calibrated to environment\" criteria, not just structural satisfaction.
5. Cannot be silently deferred to a phantom \"operator review\" step that the sprint flow does not actually run.
## Related corpus

Companion to meta-bug 5f2a-9a9f-2b4a-4aab (\"production-only defect cluster from epic 4047\"). 5f2a documents the test-coverage / dual-load-key / git-identity / repo-root class of defects. THIS bug documents a different process gap: unverified operational thresholds. Both should inform the same planning-process retrospective.
## Chain context

- Detected: 2026-05-26 dry-run dispatch run 26430060327
- Epic of origin: 4047-3cb1-6cb4-46a1 (closed P1=PASS)
- Story of origin: 10e3-e1fb-5e65-4898 (closed)
- Task of origin: 71d4-be7e-d58b-4dce (archived)
- Code site: plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/fetcher.py:26 (`_ACLI_CEILING = 1000`)

content.text: ## Context

With Confluence integration (e471-dda3) and UI/UX design corpus (0b7c-d811) in place, /dso:implementation-plan still generates tasks without referencing org-specific guidance stored in Confluence or curated design knowledge from the local corpus. This epic closes that gap by adding `ref-library-loader.sh` — a pipeline that queries the local corpus first, supplements with configured URL references, merges the two sets, applies LLM relevance judgment, and annotates each generated task with cited references in one of two formats. Single user outcome: /dso:implementation-plan tasks cite relevant reference sources.
## Success Criteria

- For each task generated by /dso:implementation-plan, ref-library-loader.sh annotates the task with up to 6 relevant reference citations drawn from the merged corpus+URL reference set (headroom from merged-set cap of 20 allows LLM relevance judgment to select top 6); tasks with no relevant matches (merged set empty after LLM judgment excludes all candidates) are generated without citations and no error is raised. The "6" constant is documented in ref-library-loader.sh as `MAX_CITATIONS_PER_TASK=6`.

- Two citation formats supported and visually distinguishable in task output: URL-sourced `> Reference: [Doc Title](url) — [one-sentence excerpt]` and corpus-sourced `> Reference: [Doc Title] (dso:ui-reference:<entry-id>) — [one-sentence excerpt]`.

- ref-library-loader.sh pipeline (per task): (a) query local UI/UX corpus via `dso ref-query --top-n=8` using task title+description with 30s subprocess timeout and explicit PID tracking (no zombie processes); (b) apply topic-tag substring filter to configured URL references, fetch via `confluence-fetch.sh`, cap post-filter set at 12 with consistent budget accounting (failed fetches excluded, retry quota re-filled from next candidate to maintain target budget); (c) merge both sets with local-first precedence — corpus entries preserved; URL slots expand to fill unused corpus budget ONLY when corpus returns fewer than 8 AND merged-set cap of 20 has remaining capacity (explicit slot-reallocation documented); (d) LLM relevance judgment per-entry with UTF-8-safe 200-character excerpt truncation at character boundary, concurrent-invocation cap of 3; (e) select top 6 entries by LLM relevance score for citation annotation.

- Topic-tag filter with no configured tags defaults to match-none semantics (URL references with empty tags field excluded from filter output) — documented default. URL references with explicit tags use substring matching against task title and description.

- Runtime guards: (a) `command -v dso ref-query` at startup; absent → stderr warning, URL-only mode; (b) `command -v confluence-fetch.sh` at startup; absent → stderr warning, corpus-only mode; (c) missing `confluence.base_url` key → configuration error at startup, URL fetch path aborts, corpus-only mode with clear stderr error; (d) BOTH unavailable → stderr warning, tasks generated without citations, no error.

- Integration test suite at tests/integration/test-ref-library-loader-integration.sh validates: (a) corpus-only mode returns corpus-sourced citations; (b) URL-only mode returns URL-sourced citations; (c) merge mode returns both formats with verified local-first precedence; (d) sparse corpus (ref-query returns 3 entries) reallocates up to 5 URL slots without crowd-out; (e) both-unavailable mode generates tasks without citations and no error; (f) UTF-8 multibyte characters in excerpts never split mid-codepoint.
## Sprint Scope Rationale

This epic delivers a single pipeline with one user outcome — /dso:implementation-plan tasks cite relevant reference sources. The three internal steps (corpus query, URL fetch, merge-and-judge) are tightly coupled: the merge logic depends on outputs from both sources; LLM relevance judgment operates on the merged set; the slot-reallocation rule for sparse corpus only has meaning when both paths coexist. Splitting into corpus-only Milestone A and URL-merge Milestone B would ship an incomplete pipeline whose primary value (merged citations with local-first precedence) is unavailable until Milestone B ships. YAGNI: additional decomposition creates sequencing overhead without standalone user value in Milestone A.
## Operational Constraints (Architecture-vs-Evidence Audit Remediation, 2026-05-18)
### Self-use SC (Probe-1 remediation)

The f7d5 sprint exercises the ref-library-loader hook against `/dso:implementation-plan` during sprint execution itself. At least one implementation-plan run during the f7d5 sprint produces output that includes a citation annotation rendered via the ref-library-loader post-rendering hook.
Verification (in-session, at sprint Phase I):
- The sprint planning session for f7d5 produces an implementation plan artifact AND that artifact contains a citation-annotation block with at least one rendered reference.
- `grep -n 'ref-library-loader\|citation_annotation' <implementation-plan-artifact>` returns ≥1 match against the actual planning output (not a fixture).
## Dependencies
- e471-dda3 (BLOCKING): requires confluence-fetch.sh infrastructure for URL fetch path
- 0b7c-d811 (BLOCKING): requires dso ref-query CLI + committed _index.yaml for corpus query path
- Sprint ordering: ships after both parents merge; runtime guards permit partial deployment but full value requires both parents
## Approach

ref-library-loader.sh invoked as a post-rendering step in /dso:implementation-plan task generation — receives fully-rendered task title+description as input (no template variables). Pipeline executes per task. Corpus query via dso ref-query with 30s timeout + explicit PID tracking. URL fetch via confluence-fetch.sh from e471-dda3. Merge step implements explicit slot-reallocation for local-first precedence with sparse-corpus fallback. LLM relevance judgment per-entry (not batched) with concurrent-invocation cap of 3 to balance throughput and rate limits.
## Research Findings

Inherited from parent epics e471-dda3 (Confluence CQL API prior art, Basic Auth patterns, redirect-based credential exfiltration mitigation) and 0b7c-d811 (stdlib BM25 retrieval, corpus schema, _index.yaml format). Additional epic-specific findings: per-entry LLM relevance judgment (vs. batched) preferred at this scale to avoid context-length failures while keeping per-task wall time bounded via concurrent-invocation cap of 3 (empirical sweet spot for rate-limit-bound LLM clients).
## Scenario Analysis

- dso ref-query subprocess hangs past 30s timeout leaving zombie process (high, runtime): 30s timeout alone insufficient — must track child PID and kill on timeout; N tasks → N zombies without PID tracking.

- confluence-fetch.sh fetch failures cause inconsistent budget accounting across tasks in the same plan (high, runtime): failed fetches must not count against 12-entry budget; retry quota refills from next candidate.

- CI/CD pipeline runs ref-library-loader.sh without corpus present, producing different output than developer local runs (high, deployment): `command -v dso ref-query` guard passes if `dso` exists but subcommand missing; check subcommand registration explicitly.

- Missing dso-config.conf key for Confluence base URL causes confluence-fetch.sh to silently fetch from wrong endpoint (high, configuration): ref-library-loader must surface URL-fetch-skipped diagnostic even when corpus path succeeds.

- LLM relevance judgment token budget overflow when 20 entries with 200-char excerpts are passed in a single prompt (high, runtime): per-entry judgment (not batched) with concurrent-invocation cap of 3 avoids both context-length and rate-limit failures.
- 200-character excerpt truncation splits multibyte UTF-8 characters, corrupting citation output (medium, runtime): truncate at character boundary (not byte offset); integration test (f) verifies.

- Topic-tag filter with no configured tags matches all URL references, exhausting the 12-entry budget on irrelevant results (medium, configuration): default to match-none when tags empty; documented default.

- Max-20 merge cap is not split proportionally, allowing URL references to crowd out corpus results (medium, configuration): explicit slot-reallocation rule — URL slots expand only when corpus returns fewer than 8 AND merge-cap headroom exists.
### Planning Intelligence Log
- **Web research (Step 2.6)**: inherited from parent epics
- Bright-line conditions that fired in parents: external integration (Confluence CQL, dso ref-query), novel pattern (local-first merge with slot reallocation)
- **Scenario analysis (Step 2.75)**: triggered
- Scenarios surviving blue team filter: 8
- **Practitioner-requested additional cycles**: Agent Clarity re-review 1 time (fix SC1 K definition + SC7 pass threshold); Scope re-review 1 time (YAGNI rationale against further split)
- **Follow-on scrutiny (Step 0)**: not triggered — this epic is itself a follow-on from e471-dda3; depth 0
- **Feasibility resolution (Step 2.5)**: not triggered
- **LLM-instruction signal (Step 5)**: triggered — keyword: skill file modifications (implementation-plan SKILL.md post-rendering hook for ref-library-loader.sh invocation)
- **Scale context (Step 0)**: small scale (default) — per-implementation-plan-task (moderate number of plans per day, 5-20 tasks per plan); not volume-sensitive at current scale
## Closure Checks

- Validation signal (executable within sprint): Before/after comparison on exactly 3 representative implementation-plan tasks drawn from recent org work. Baseline (ref-library-loader inactive) vs. treatment (ref-library-loader active). Pass threshold: ALL 3 treatment tasks must cite at least one Confluence or corpus source (URL-sourced or corpus-sourced format) that is ABSENT from the corresponding baseline task's generated output, verified by string comparison of the full annotated vs. unannotated task body (citation lines grep'd on prefix `> Reference:`). Any of the 3 comparisons failing this check fails the validation signal and blocks sprint closure.

content.text: ## Testing Mode GREEN ## Overview Insert the entry and exit validator invocation blocks into implementation-plan SKILL.md. Makes T3's RED tests pass. content.text: ## Context

When orchestration skills (sprint, debug-everything, fix-bug) hit usage quota thresholds and pause sub-agent dispatch (per epic dso-t7af), the session currently stops and the user must manually resume after the billing window resets. This creates unnecessary friction — the system knows when the quota will reset (the OAuth endpoint returns resets_at timestamps) and could automatically schedule a session resumption.
## Success Criteria
1. When check-usage.sh returns a paused verdict, it also outputs the earliest reset timestamp from the OAuth response
2. The orchestration skill, upon receiving a pause verdict, offers to schedule an automatic session resume at the reset time
3. Scheduled resume launches a new Claude Code session that picks up where the paused session left off, using ticket checkpoint notes for state recovery
4. A configurable session.auto_resume config key enables/disables auto-scheduling (default: prompt user)
## Dependencies
- Depends on dso-t7af (Remove 5-sub-agent cap): requires the check-usage.sh infrastructure and pause verdict mechanism
## Notes
Inspired by mironmax/claudecode-plugins scheduler-plugin pattern which auto-schedules session resumption at the usage reset time.

content.text: Placeholder for the deeper-signal extension of test creation calibration metrics. Sibling of 7f42-e41f (which delivers (a) manifest-claim breadth + (a+) static header-vs-source-import check in its first version) and 411b-a047 (mutation infrastructure / Tier 3).
Scope: extends 7f42's first-version metric set with two stronger signals:
## (b) Intent-anchored line coverage

For each changed source line in a PR, compute the percentage exercised by tests whose intent-claim header (per d566's Rule 6) references an intent_id from the PR's parent ticket subtree (per 94ed's manifest). Requires polyglot per-test line-coverage infrastructure (coverage.py + pytest-cov for Python; bashcov or trace-harness for bash; istanbul/nyc for JS/TS if present), per-test attribution storage, and a join step that maps per-test coverage to intent_ids via the header.

Catches the failure mode where a test is added with a valid intent-claim header but its assertions never actually exercise the changed source lines. Stronger than 7f42's (a)+(a+) which only verify manifest registration and symbol reference. Does NOT catch tautological assertions, behavior-irrelevant assertions, or header-lying tests — those require 411b's mutation-kill verification.
## (c) Manifest-claim depth

Per intent_id, count the number of distinct test scenarios registered (counting Rule 7 sibling parameterized cases as separate scenarios). Surfaces intent items that are 'covered' by one test only when the SC implies multiple scenarios should exist (e.g., 'users can export as CSV' likely needs at least empty/single-row/multi-row scenarios).
## Cost-value justification for deferral

The honest assessment from 7f42 brainstorm: (b) closes roughly half the gap from (a) to 411b's catch power at roughly the same engineering cost as 411b itself. 411b's mutation-kill verification strictly dominates (b) for the failure modes (b) doesn't catch (tautological assertions, behavior-irrelevant assertions, header-lying). Best ROI sequence: ship 7f42 (a)+(a+) and 411b first; revisit (b)+(c) once we see real-world catch-rate gaps in the simpler signals.
## Dependencies
Depends on 7f42-e41f (defines the (a)+(a+) base) and 411b-a047 (mutation infrastructure, which may obviate (b) entirely; do not start this epic until 411b's catch-rate is empirically known).
## Out of scope
Anything outside per-test line coverage and manifest-claim depth metrics. Suite-wide aggregation, longitudinal dashboards, telemetry pipelines — separate epics if/when needed.
Refine via /dso:brainstorm when prioritized.

content.text: ## Context

Developers running DSO on nava-platform projects experience friction from accumulated codebase bloat that prevention gates cannot address retroactively. Specifically: false test failures from change-detector tests slow CI and erode trust in the test suite; stale documentation sections generate noise in code review; and dead code (unreachable branches, unused variables) slows codebase comprehension for new contributors. This epic adds a /dso:remediate skill that safely prunes high-confidence bloat patterns and surfaces lower-confidence candidates through an opus blue-team filter before presenting them for human resolution. The observable improvement: after running /dso:remediate --all, the developer sees a structured summary of what was cleaned, flagged, or skipped — and the next CI run, code review, and onboarding session encounters less noise.

Pattern namespace: bright-line patterns use category prefixes (T, D, C) and are eligible for auto-remediation. Probabilistic patterns use the P- prefix (P-T1, P-D3, P-C1) and are always routed to the blue-team agent when in confidence range — never auto-remediated regardless of threshold.
## Success Criteria

SC1. A new skill /dso:remediate is added, invoked with one of four scoped flags: --tests, --docs, --code, or --all. Invocation without a flag prints usage and exits non-zero. A sub-agent guard runs at skill entry: if the Agent tool is unavailable, the skill returns an error message and exits without mutations. Before any mutation, the skill checks for staged changes (git diff --cached --quiet); if staged changes exist, it aborts with an error.

SC2. A static confidence mapping file (YAML) ships with the plugin at plugins/dso/config/remediate-confidence-map.yaml, declaring {pattern_id, engine} -> confidence_score for every pattern/engine combination. Each per-stack linter (ruff, eslint, rubocop) has its own engine entry. Two new dso-config.conf keys control routing: remediate.auto_threshold (default: 90) and remediate.blue_team_threshold (default: 60). At runtime, the skill detects installed engines via command -v, looks up the highest-confidence installed engine for each pattern, and routes: >= auto_threshold -> auto-remediate, >= blue_team_threshold -> route to blue-team agent, < blue_team_threshold -> skip with a note in the summary.
SC3. The skill detects and auto-remediates the following bright-line patterns when confidence meets the auto threshold:
- --tests: T1 (assertion-less test body — auto-delete the test function), T2 (exact-duplicate test — auto-delete the duplicate), T3 (import-only test file — auto-delete the file)

- --docs: D2 (broken internal links — annotate with TODO: fix or remove inline comment), D4 (duplicate headings — included in summary as flagged_for_review with file path), D5 (large unstructured file — included in summary as flagged_for_review with file path)

- --code: C1 (unreachable branch after unconditional return/raise/throw — auto-delete the dead block), C2 (unused local variable without suppression annotation — auto-delete), C3 (exact-duplicate function body — included in summary as flagged_for_review with both file paths)

For C2, auto-prune is suppressed if the line contains # noqa, # type: ignore, or # side-effect; such matches are flagged for human review instead. For C1 and C2, the skill delegates to per-stack linters when available, falling back to semgrep rules.

SC4. For probabilistic patterns where the best available engine's confidence falls between the two thresholds, the skill dispatches a dso:bloat-blue-team opus sub-agent. Engine selection follows the same rule as SC2: the highest-confidence installed engine determines the routing decision. The blue-team agent emits one of three verdicts per candidate: CONFIRM, DISMISS (with rationale), or NEEDS_HUMAN (with ambiguity note). DISMISS candidates are excluded from the user-facing report. CONFIRM and NEEDS_HUMAN candidates both proceed to SC5 resolution paths. NEEDS_HUMAN is counted as a distinct field in the SC6 summary. Probabilistic patterns: P-T1 (change-detector test), P-D3 (stale example referencing absent symbol), P-C1 (feature flag never toggled to true). If no installed engine covers a probabilistic pattern, it is skipped and recorded in skipped_pattern_ids.
SC5. After blue-team filtering, the skill presents the user with a choice of two resolution paths:

- Path A (manual): Displays a numbered list of CONFIRM and NEEDS_HUMAN candidates with file location, pattern ID, and blue-team note. User enters item numbers to remove (comma-separated), or presses Enter to skip all. Fixture tests simulate Path A by injecting a pre-set selection list via DSO_REMEDIATE_SELECT env var.

- Path B (auto-resolve): Dispatches a dso:bloat-resolver opus sub-agent that applies all CONFIRM candidates and emits NO_CHANGE: <reason> for any it declines. Changes from the resolver follow the normal commit workflow (COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md -> /dso:review), ensuring at least two independent agents review every change.

SC6. The skill emits a structured session-end summary written to $ARTIFACTS_DIR/remediate-summary-<timestamp>.json with schema: {"auto_remediated": 0, "blue_team_dismissed": 0, "blue_team_needs_human": 0, "skipped_below_threshold": 0, "skipped_pattern_ids": [], "flagged_for_review": 0, "user_resolved": 0, "resolver_applied": 0, "resolver_no_change": 0, "flags": ["--tests"]}

SC7. Validation is run against each nava-platform template (flask, nextjs, rails, jekyll-uswds) using synthetic test fixtures at tests/fixtures/remediate/<template>/. Each fixture includes a fixture-manifest.json declaring expected counts and file-level outcomes. Validation asserts: auto-remediated items -> target file/function absent and auto_remediated count matches; flagged items -> no mutation and flagged_for_review count matches; skipped items -> skipped_pattern_ids contains expected IDs. Each fixture also includes at least one valid-but-pattern-matching item (e.g., intentional golden-file test, changelog with duplicate headings) that must NOT be removed — the manifest declares these as expected_false_positive_safe and the test asserts they remain unmodified.
Out of scope: P-D4 (concept drift), P-D1 (orphaned sections), P-T2 (mock-heavy tests), P-C2 (redundant parameters). These are deferred to follow-on epic bc7f-1a0d.
## Scenario Analysis
- P-T1 golden-file false positives (critical): Intentional regression tests are structurally identical to change-detectors; the static confidence mapping cannot distinguish them by project context.
- P-C1 env-flag false positives (critical): Feature flags gated on environment variables are statically never true during analysis, matching every env-conditional flag.
- auto_threshold=0 bypass (critical): Setting threshold to 0 routes all matches to auto-prune, bypassing blue-team entirely.
- Unbounded resolver batch (important): 50+ auto-prune candidates in a single dispatch may exhaust agent context.
- Test coverage gap after deletion (important): Deleting the sole test covering a source file leaves an invisible coverage gap.
- Interrupted mid-batch state (important): No checkpoint/state file to resume from after SIGURG.
- Inverted thresholds dead zone (important): blue_team_threshold > auto_threshold creates undefined routing behavior.
- Missing config key (important): Absent threshold keys cause bash comparison failure and silent abort.
- Stack-detection mismatch (important): Monorepo stack detection may select wrong linter for confidence lookup.
## Prompt Alignment Findings
- Blue-team agent must form its verdict before consulting the engine confidence score to avoid anchoring
- Blue-team should default to DISMISS when uncertain — false CONFIRMs are amplified by the resolver; false DISMISSes are recoverable
- Resolver prompt must NOT mention the downstream review gate — prevents moral hazard
- Resolver must check for callers before deleting any function/class/export and emit NO_CHANGE with CASCADE_RISK when callers exist outside the candidate list
- Embed these as hard constraints in agent definition files during implementation
## Research Findings
### Code Bloat Remediation

- Polyglot Piranha (Uber, https://github.com/uber/piranha): Java/Kotlin/Swift/ObjC/JS/Go. Tree-sitter AST with cascading cleanup rules. Auto-remediates (210K lines deleted, 1611 PRs). Binary match/no-match — no confidence tiering. Excels at feature flag cascading cleanup.
- DCE-LLM (NAACL 2025, https://aclanthology.org/2025.naacl-long.501/): Hybrid CodeBERT triage + LLM judgment. 94%+ F1. Architecturally closest to our approach but requires fine-tuned models.
- Knip (https://github.com/webpro-nl/knip): JS/TS only. TypeScript type checker as ground truth. Highest-precision JS/TS dead code detector — candidate linter delegate for JS/TS stack.
- Semgrep autofix (https://semgrep.dev/docs/writing-rules/autofix): 20+ languages. Rule-based or LLM-assisted (https://choly.ca/post/semgrep-autofix-llm/). No native confidence tiering.
- Datadog: LLM false-positive filtering for static analysis (https://www.datadoghq.com/blog/using-llms-to-filter-out-false-positives/)
### Documentation Bloat Remediation
- lychee (https://github.com/lycheeverse/lychee): Async Rust link checker. Fast, caching, .lycheeignore. Report only.
- markdownlint (https://github.com/DavidAnson/markdownlint): MD024 duplicate headings with siblings_only option (changelog-aware). Has auto-fix. More precise than bash-grep for D4.
- Doc Detective (https://github.com/doc-detective): Execution-based stale example detection (runs docs against live system). Complementary to LLM approach.
- Vale (https://github.com/errata-ai/vale): Prose style linter with YAML rules. Can approximate P-D3 with deprecated-term lists but brittle vs LLM approach.
### Test Bloat Remediation
- TSDetect (https://github.com/TestSmells/TSDetect): Java only. 20 test smells including assertion-less (Unknown Test). Report only.
- TestIQ (https://github.com/pydevtools/TestIQ): Python/pytest. Coverage-based duplicate detection. Higher FP rate than AST hashing.

- UTRefactor (FSE 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.16739): Java. LLM-based auto-refactoring of test smells (89% reduction). Closest to our blue-team filter but collapses detection and remediation into one pass.
- Mutation testing (PIT, mutmut): Ground truth for test redundancy but too slow for commit gates.
### Key Tradeoff Summary

No existing tool implements all three of our architectural pillars: per-pattern confidence mapping, tiered routing (auto/LLM/skip), and per-stack linter delegation. Implementation should consider: Knip as JS/TS linter delegate, markdownlint for D4 (siblings_only precision), Piranha's cascading pattern for resolver design.
## Dependencies

No blocking epic dependencies. The confidence mapping YAML (plugins/dso/config/remediate-confidence-map.yaml) is a deliverable artifact — its schema is a stable interface that follow-on epic bc7f-1a0d will consume. Two new dso-config.conf entries: remediate.auto_threshold, remediate.blue_team_threshold. Runtime tool availability handled by confidence mapping graceful degradation.
## Approach

Option A: Tiered Engine Selection. Ship a static confidence mapping YAML declaring {pattern_id, engine} -> confidence_score. At runtime, detect available engines via command -v, look up the highest-confidence available engine for each pattern, and route through three tiers using two global config thresholds. Detection engines: semgrep (declarative AST rules, polyglot), ast-grep (structural queries), bash-grep (textual fallback), plus delegation to per-stack linters (ruff, eslint, rubocop) where they already detect the pattern.
## Resolved Implementation Gaps
### Gap 1: Agent Contracts (resolved 2026-04-14)
**dso:bloat-blue-team input**: {candidates: [{candidate_id, pattern_id, file, line_range, excerpt, engine, confidence}]}
**dso:bloat-blue-team output**: {verdicts: [{candidate_id, verdict, rationale, rationale_basis}]}
- rationale required for DISMISS and NEEDS_HUMAN, optional for CONFIRM
- rationale_basis enum: excerpt_only | file_context | cross_file (required)
- Contract file: plugins/dso/docs/contracts/bloat-blue-team-payload.md
**dso:bloat-resolver input**: {confirmed_candidates: [{candidate_id, pattern_id, file, line_range, action}]}
- action enum: delete_function | delete_file | delete_block | annotate | flag
**dso:bloat-resolver output**: {applied: [{candidate_id, action_taken}], no_change: [{candidate_id, category, reason}]}
- no_change.category enum: CASCADE_RISK | INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT | PATTERN_UNCLEAR | STACK_UNCERTAINTY (required)
### Gap 2: Config Validation Behavior (resolved 2026-04-14)

Add to SC2: If either config key (remediate.auto_threshold, remediate.blue_team_threshold) is absent, non-numeric, or outside 1-100, log warning to stderr naming the invalid key and value, then use defaults (auto=90, blue_team=60) for the entire run. If blue_team_threshold >= auto_threshold after resolution, log warning (inverted thresholds) but proceed.
### Gap 3: Monorepo Multi-Stack Support (resolved 2026-04-14)

Add to SC2: At scan start, classify files in scope into language groups by extension. For each language group, select the highest-confidence installed engine. Extension-to-language mapping is a static lookup table shipped alongside the confidence mapping YAML. Unrecognized extensions scanned with bash-grep only.
### Gap 4: Prompt Engineering Constraints (resolved 2026-04-14)
Blue-team: form verdict before consulting confidence; default to DISMISS when uncertain; 80%+ definitive rate; declare rationale_basis.
Resolver: no mention of downstream review gate; check callers before deleting; categorize every NO_CHANGE.
### Gap 5: Feasibility Spike Results (resolved 2026-04-14)

SC3 ACHIEVABLE on all 4 stacks. Confidence ranges: Python python-ast 95, semgrep 85; JS/TS ast-grep 88; Ruby ast-grep 85; Markdown bash-grep 90. Ruby C1 lower confidence — consider routing to blue-team.

content.text: ## Incident Overview
**Component:** plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/applier.py (_apply_batch drift detector)
**Condition:** Filtered reconciler pass with mixed inbound and outbound mutations on a fresh tickets-branch worktree
**Observed Result:** HeadDriftError raised mid-apply-loop even with d822 defer-bug-filing fix and try/finally remediation in place; bindings save() skipped, orphan Jira issues
## Reproduction
1. Run e2e_field_validation_probe.sh (DSO_FIELD_VALIDATION_PROBE=1)
2. Probe creates 10 local tickets, sets assignee on ticket 5, adds comment on ticket 8
3. Runs reconciler: `python -m dso_reconciler --mode bootstrap-throttle --filter-local-ids <ids>`
4. Reconciler fails with: `ERROR: reconcile_once raised: drift: 78392cd6→19da05f6`
5. All 10 bindings show 'unbound' afterwards; Jira issues DID get created (DIG-4711-4720) but bindings.json wasn't saved
## Expected Behavior

Filtered reconciler pass completes without drift error. The d822 fix (defer conflict bug-filing out of apply loop) was supposed to eliminate in-apply-loop commits to the tickets branch. PR #425 landed that fix, and the try/finally remediation ensures deferred filing runs even on exception paths.
## Actual Behavior
Drift still fires. Even though:
- d822 defer-fix is in main (PR #425 merged as commit 9cd7755888)
- Phase 1 of probe has zero inbound conflicts (all 10 mutations are outbound creates)
- _file_conflict_bug_ticket is NOT in the apply path for outbound creates
- The probe Phase 1 reconciler still hits drift
This means a DIFFERENT commit source exists during `_apply_batch` execution that we haven't identified yet.
## Suspected Root Causes

H1: `create_one` (applier.py:1462) writes identity markers via `client.add_label(jira_key, dso-id:local_id)` and `client.set_entity_property(jira_key, dso_local_id, local_id)`. These are Jira API calls, but if any retry or fallback path commits to the tickets branch, that would explain drift.

H2: The reconciler's legacy snapshot differ emits inbound_create mutations alongside the outbound_creates (because the Jira snapshot has issues that the differ thinks need local creation). `_apply_typed` dispatches inbound_create which calls `_write_event_file` to create local jira-* tickets. _write_event_file writes to .tickets-tracker/ filesystem but does NOT commit. So this shouldn't cause drift unless something else triggers a commit.
H3: The reconciler may be calling `acquire_pass_lock` or similar mid-pass. acquire_pass_lock commits to the tickets branch. If it's called inside apply()... unlikely but possible.
H4: There's a deferred-write or background-sync mechanism (binding_store.save? mapping.json write?) that commits during the pass.
H5: A git hook (post-write, post-event-file) commits automatically.
## Investigation steps

1. After a failed probe run, run `git -C $REPO_ROOT/.tickets-tracker log --oneline -20` to see which commits accumulated during the failed reconciler invocation. Compare to the drift SHAs in the error message to identify the offending commit's author/message.
2. Add temporary print statements around `concurrency.snapshot_head` calls inside `_apply_batch` to log when HEAD changes (and what was just being processed when it changed).
3. Audit ALL the calls inside `_apply_batch` that touch git or filesystem state. Specifically inspect: create_one, _audit_dso_id_label_writes, _persist_field_provenance, _write_pass_record.
## Key code paths
- plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/applier.py:2271-2278 (drift detector)
- plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/applier.py:1462+ (create_one — the dispatcher for outbound create batch entries)
- plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/_concurrency.py:41-69 (snapshot_head implementation — reads git rev-parse tickets)
## Affected Validation
The e2e_field_validation_probe cannot complete Phase 1 binding verification. All downstream phases cascade-fail.

content.text: ## Incident Overview
**Component:** plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/applier.py (post-C2-fix outbound update dispatch path)
**Condition:** Local edits to bound tickets, reconciler runs without error, Jira unchanged
**Observed Result:** Outbound UPDATE matrix shows FAIL for title, description, priority, assignee, labels, comments — but reconciler reports OK and no exceptions
## Reproduction
`cd /Users/joeoakhart/digital-service-orchestra && DSO_FIELD_VALIDATION_PROBE=1 plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/e2e_field_validation_probe.sh`
Latest run: /tmp/field-probe-full-1779988610.log. Phase 1 PASSES (all 10 bindings confirmed, drift tolerance working). Phase 2 makes local edits then runs reconciler which logs:
`filter: 690 mutations computed, 10 match filter (10 local IDs, 10 target keys)` — no errors.
But Phase 2 verify reads Jira via get_issue_by_rest and sees:
- title: original (not 'UPDATED title')
- description: empty
- priority: Highest (not Low, expected 3→Low)
- assignee: Joe Oakhart (not unassigned)
- labels: only dso-id:*, no user labels
- comments: missing
## Expected Behavior
Local field edits propagate to Jira via the outbound UPDATE path. The C2 fix landed two coordinated changes that should make this work:
1. _mutation_to_batch_dict properly maps changed_fields → fields for UPDATE mutations
2. update_one propagates labels (add_label/remove_label) and comments (add_comment) alongside the scalar update
Both are present in the current applier.py (verified via grep: 16 occurrences of changed_fields/CREATE-branching, 3 occurrences of add_label/remove_label paths in update_one).
## Hypotheses

- H1: Outbound update mutations route through _apply_outbound_update (the typed leaf) which only pushes scalar fields via update_issue — bypasses the labels/comments propagation in update_one. The legacy batch path with update_one (where labels/comments DO propagate) isn't being reached.
- H2: The differ doesn't produce UPDATE mutations after the local edits. Possibly the local ticket state isn't reflecting the EDIT events (event-sourcing bug), or the differ compares stale snapshots.
- H3: ticket-CLI edit doesn't emit EDIT events for some field types.
- H4: ACLI calls succeed but silently no-op. get_issue_by_rest is reading stale state.
- H5: The mutations are produced and routed, but get filtered out by --filter-local-ids (filter target set mis-classified).
## Investigation goals
1. After a probe failure, examine the manifest at bridge_state/snapshots/<pass_id>.manifest.json — does it show update mutations with results indicating success? Or no update mutations at all?
2. Run `ticket show <id>` after Phase 2 edits to confirm local reducer captured the change. If priority shows 3, the local state is correct. If still 0, the EDIT didn't take effect locally.

3. Trace: for an outbound update typed Mutation, which dispatch arm runs — _apply_outbound_update (typed leaf, allowlist-filtered, no labels/comments) or update_one (legacy batch, labels/comments propagation)? Read apply() partitioning at lines 1995-2090.
4. If the typed leaf is the actual path: the C2 fix to update_one isn't reachable, and the typed leaf needs the same labels/comments-aware logic.
## Affected Files
- plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/applier.py — _apply_outbound_update (typed leaf), update_one (legacy batch), apply() partitioning
- plugins/dso/scripts/dso_reconciler/outbound_differ.py — verify UPDATE mutations are emitted
This bug blocks bidirectional sync verification beyond CREATE operations.
